## Done

### Show the selected album's running time before the total in the album-list footer, like the song-list footer (planned 2026-10-29 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-29 by the feature role

**Goal.** While a song row is selected, the song-list footer shows that song's length before the
total (`2 songs - 3:30/4:15`, `song_list_summary` in `src/ui/views/browse/rows/text.rs`), like
Winamp's playlist status line. Album rows can be selected too (`BrowseList::select_row`, painted
by `scrollable_list`), but the album-list footer (`album_list_summary`) ignores the selection and
always reads `3 albums - 45:30`. Make it read `3 albums - 10:30/45:30` while an album is selected,
in the Albums, All Albums, and Recently Added views (all three build through `rows::album_list`).

**Approach.**
1. `src/ui/views/browse/rows/text.rs`: change `album_list_summary(albums: &[Album])` to
   `album_list_summary(albums: &[Album], selected: Option<usize>) -> String`, following
   `song_list_summary`'s shape. The total and its `+` rule stay as they are. When
   `selected.and_then(|i| albums.get(i))` names an album, the output is
   `"<count> <noun> - <selected>/<total>"`. `<selected>` is that album's `duration_ms` from
   `format_minutes_seconds`, with a trailing `+` when the album's `duration_ms == 0`. An index past
   the list falls back to the plain form. Update the doc comment: drop "Selecting a row does not
   change it" and describe the selected form.
2. `src/ui/views/browse/rows.rs` `album_list`: pass its existing `selected` argument, so the
   footer becomes `album_list_summary(albums, selected)`. Update its doc comment to say the footer
   includes the selected album's running time.
3. Tests in `src/ui/views/tests/browse.rs`. Change the calls in
   `album_list_summary_counts_albums_and_sums_their_running_time` to pass `None`, keeping their
   expected strings. Then add:
   - `album_list_summary_puts_the_selected_running_time_before_the_total`:
     `[summary_album(630_000), summary_album(210_000)]` with `Some(1)` gives
     `"2 albums - 3:30/14:00"`.
   - `album_list_summary_marks_an_unknown_selected_running_time`:
     `[summary_album(0), summary_album(210_000)]` with `Some(0)` gives `"2 albums - 0:00+/3:30+"`.
   - `album_list_summary_ignores_a_selection_past_the_list`: `Some(5)` on one album gives the
     plain form.
4. Rendered test in `src/ui/tests/view_tests.rs` (next to
   `root_view_artists_footer_totals_the_album_counts`):
   `root_view_album_footer_shows_the_selected_running_time`. Set `player.all_albums.items` to two
   albums with known `duration_ms` and `loading = false`, and set
   `current_view = CurrentView::AllAlbums`. Select row 1 with
   `player.all_albums.select_row(player.all_albums.epoch, 1)`, then assert through
   `captured_root_view_text_bounds` that the expected `"2 albums - <a>/<total>"` text is drawn.
5. `docs/usage.md`: in the album-lists clause of the browse paragraph (the one with
   `3 albums - 45:30`), add that while an album row is selected, the footer shows that album's
   running time before the total (`3 albums - 10:30/45:30`), with the same trailing `+` rule.
6. `docs/invariants.md`: add a `## Album-list footer` section right after `## Song-list footer`,
   in the same Guarantee / Enforced by / Pinned by / History form. It names `album_list_summary`,
   `album_list`, and the tests above.

**Files touched.** `src/ui/views/browse/rows/text.rs`, `src/ui/views/browse/rows.rs`,
`src/ui/views/tests/browse.rs`, `src/ui/tests/view_tests.rs`, `docs/usage.md`,
`docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With no selection, a loaded album list's footer is unchanged (`3 albums - 45:30[+]`), and the
  existing `album_list_summary` expectations pass with `None`.
- While an album row is selected, the footer reads `<count> album(s) - <selected>/<total>`, and
  an unknown-length selection is marked `+`. The three new unit tests and the rendered test pin it.
- An empty album list still draws no footer: `an_empty_browse_level_draws_no_count_footer` passes
  unchanged.
- No new dependency, message, state field, cache, or setting.
- `docs/usage.md` and `docs/invariants.md` describe the selected form, and `make check` passes.

### Show the Genres, Years, and Composers lists' total playing time beside their count in the footer, like the album-list footer (planned 2026-10-29 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-29 by the feature role

**Goal.** Each grouped row already reads like the song-list footer (`group_row_label`:
`2 songs - 5:05`). The album lists' footer reads `3 albums - 45:30` (`album_list_summary`). But
the Genres, Years, and Composers footers still use the bare item count from `list_with_count`
(`2 genres`). Make each grouped footer read `<count> <noun> - <total>`: `2 genres - 7:10`,
`1 year - 3:30`, `2 composers - 7:10`. `<total>` is the `u64::saturating_add` sum of
`duration_ms` over every song in every listed group, formatted by `format_minutes_seconds`. It
gets a trailing `+` when any of those songs has `duration_ms == 0`, the same unknown-length rule
as `group_row_label` and `album_list_summary`. Every song is in exactly one group (`group_songs`
in `src/ui/song_groups.rs` puts keyless songs in the last `Unknown` group), so the total is the
playing time of the whole grouped library. An empty grouped list still draws only its
placeholder. The footer has no selected-row form. The row labels and the Artists, playlist,
album, and song footers stay as they are.

This plan is independent of the waiting Artists-footer plan above. Both make `with_footer` in
`src/ui/views/browse/rows.rs` `pub(in crate::ui::views)`. Whichever plan merges second finds
that change already made and keeps it, adding its own view to `with_footer`'s doc list.

**Approach.**
- `src/ui/song_groups.rs`: move `group_row_label`'s total-and-mark code into a private
  `fn songs_total<'a>(songs: impl IntoIterator<Item = &'a Song>) -> String`. It returns
  `format_minutes_seconds(sum)` followed by `+` when any song has `duration_ms == 0`; for no songs
  it returns `0:00`. `group_row_label` keeps its output and calls `songs_total(&group.songs)`.
  Add `pub(in crate::ui) fn group_list_summary(groups: &[SongGroup], singular: &str, plural: &str) -> String`
  directly after `group_row_label`, returning `format!("{count} {noun} - {total}")`. `count` is
  `groups.len()`, `noun` is `singular` exactly when `count == 1`, and `total` is
  `songs_total(groups.iter().flat_map(|group| &group.songs))`. Doc comment in the style of
  `group_row_label`'s. Update the module doc's first line so it names the footer too.
- `src/ui/views/browse/rows.rs`: make `with_footer` `pub(in crate::ui::views)` if it is not
  already. Name the Genres, Years, and Composers lists in its doc's list of footer layouts. In
  `list_with_count`'s doc, say it now serves only the artist and playlist lists (or only the
  playlist list if the Artists-footer plan has merged).
- `src/ui/views/browse.rs`, `grouped_list`: change the first parameter from
  `names: impl ExactSizeIterator<Item = &'a str>` to `groups: &'a [SongGroup]`, building each row
  from `group.name.as_str()`. Return the `scrollable_list` alone when `groups.is_empty()`;
  otherwise return `with_footer(list, group_list_summary(groups, singular, plural))`. `view_genres`,
  `view_years`, and `view_composers` pass their slices (`Genre`, `Year`, and `Composer` are aliases
  of `SongGroup`). Import `SongGroup` and `group_list_summary` from `crate::ui::song_groups` and
  `with_footer` from `rows`. Rewrite `grouped_list`'s doc and the "item-count footer" sentence in
  `view_genres`'s doc to name the count-and-time footer. Summing per frame is a plain `u64` walk
  with one format call, so no cache is needed.
- `src/ui/song_groups.rs` tests: add
  `list_summary_counts_groups_and_totals_every_song`, using `by_genre` and `song`:
  - three songs in two groups gives `2 genres - 10:30`;
  - one group gives the singular `1 genre - 3:30`;
  - a group holding a `duration_ms: 0` song gives a trailing `+`;
  - `u64::MAX` plus another duration does not panic and starts with `2 genres - `.
  The existing `row_label_*` tests must pass unchanged.
- Rendered tests, using `captured_root_view_text_bounds` (`src/ui/tests/mod.rs`) and asserting
  the captured texts contain the footer:
  - `src/ui/tests/flat_lists_tests.rs`: `genres_view_footer_counts_genres_and_totals_their_songs`
    with `player_with_genres()`, expecting `2 genres - 7:10`;
  - `src/ui/tests/years_tests.rs`: the `player_with_years()` twin, expecting `2 years - 7:10`;
  - `src/ui/tests/composers_tests.rs`: the `player_with_composers()` twin, expecting
    `2 composers - 7:10`.
  Each fixture's row labels are `2 songs - 5:05` and `1 song - 2:05`, which add up to 7:10.
  Confirm each helper leaves `current_view` on its list, and set it if not.
- `docs/usage.md`: in the sentence listing the footers ("album lists showing their album count
  and total playing time beneath theirs …"), add that the Genres, Years, and Composers lists show
  their count and total playing time beneath theirs (`2 genres - 7:10`, with the same trailing
  `+`), and keep artist and playlist lists on their item count.

**Files touched.** `src/ui/song_groups.rs`, `src/ui/views/browse.rs`,
`src/ui/views/browse/rows.rs`, `src/ui/tests/flat_lists_tests.rs`, `src/ui/tests/years_tests.rs`,
`src/ui/tests/composers_tests.rs`, `docs/usage.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A loaded Genres, Years, or Composers list draws `<count> <noun> - <total>[+]` beneath its rows.

- `group_list_summary` pluralizes, sums with `saturating_add`, and marks unknown lengths with `+`.

- An empty grouped list draws no footer, only its placeholder.
- The `row_label_*` tests, `genres_loaded_stores_rows_with_song_count_labels` and its Years and

- No new dependency, message, state field, cache, or setting.
- `docs/usage.md` describes the new grouped footer, and `make check` passes.

### Show the Artists list's total album count beside its artist count in the footer, like Winamp's "All (N albums)" row (planned 2026-10-29 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-29 by the feature role

**Goal.** In Winamp's Media Library, the artist pane's top row counts the artists and the album
pane's top row counts their albums. Our Artists list puts each artist's album count on its row
(`album_count_label`: `2 albums`, `1 album`, nothing for `0`), but its footer only reads
`3 artists`. Make the Artists footer read `<count> artist(s) - <albums>`, where `<albums>` is
`album_count_label` of the `usize::saturating_add` sum of the listed artists' `Artist::album_count`.
Examples are `3 artists - 5 albums` and `1 artist - 1 album`. When that sum is `0`, the footer stays
`<count> artist(s)` with no album part, matching the row rule that shows no count for `0`. A
signed-in artist whose name matched no album (`get_favorite_artists` in
`src/apple_music/browse.rs`) has a count of `0`, so this rule avoids a misleading `0 albums`. An
empty Artists list still draws only its placeholder. The footer has no selected-row form. The
album, playlist, song, and Genres/Years/Composers footers and every row label stay as they are.
This plan is independent of the waiting album-footer plan above: it adds a different function and
edits `view_artists`, not `album_list`.

**Approach.**
- `src/ui/views/browse/rows/text.rs`: add
  `pub(in crate::ui::views) fn artist_list_summary(artists: &[Artist]) -> String` directly after
  `album_count_label`. Build the artist part with `list_count_summary(artists.len(), "artist",
  "artists")`. Sum `album_count` with `saturating_add`. When `album_count_label(total)` is empty,
  return the artist part alone; otherwise return `format!("{artists} - {albums}")`. Give it a doc
  comment in the style of `song_list_summary`'s, naming the zero rule and why it exists. Fix
  `list_count_summary`'s doc comment so it no longer claims the artist list. That list then names
  the playlist and grouped lists, plus album lists if the album-footer plan has not merged yet.
- `src/ui/views/browse/rows.rs`: make `with_footer` `pub(in crate::ui::views)`. Add
  `[`super::view_artists`]` to its doc's list of footer layouts.
- `src/ui/views/browse.rs`, `view_artists`: keep the `scrollable_list` call. Return it alone when
  `artists.is_empty()`, otherwise `with_footer(list, artist_list_summary(artists))`. Import
  `with_footer` from `rows` and `artist_list_summary` from `rows::text`. Update the doc comment's
  last sentence so it names the new footer instead of `list_with_count`. Summing per frame is a
  plain `usize` walk with no formatting per row, so no cache is needed.
- `src/ui/views/tests/mod.rs`: add `artist_list_summary` to the `rows::text` import list.
- `src/ui/views/tests/browse.rs`: add
  `artist_list_summary_counts_artists_and_totals_their_albums`, using `sample_artist()` copies
  (`src/test_support/fixtures.rs`) with `album_count` set:
  - one artist at 1 → `"1 artist - 1 album"`
  - counts 2, 0, 3 → `"3 artists - 5 albums"`
  - one at 0 → `"1 artist"`
  - two at 0 → `"2 artists"`
  - one at `usize::MAX` beside one at 1 → no panic, and the result starts with `"2 artists - "`
- `src/ui/tests/view_tests.rs`: the fixture artist has `album_count: 0`, so
  `root_view_draws_the_current_browse_levels_own_rows` (`"1 artist"`) and
  `an_empty_browse_level_draws_no_count_footer` (`"0 artists"`) should pass unchanged. Run them
  and confirm. Add one view-level case: set the root view's artist to `album_count = 2` and
  assert the captured text includes `"1 artist - 2 albums"`. Either extend the existing Artists
  case or add a small sibling test built the same way.
- `docs/usage.md`: in the browse-list paragraph, change the closing clause "and artist, album,
  and playlist lists showing their item count beneath theirs" to "the artists list showing its
  artist count and the total of its rows' album counts beneath it (`3 artists - 5 albums`, or
  just `3 artists` when no artist has a counted album), and album and playlist lists showing their
  item count beneath theirs". If the album-footer plan has merged first, keep its wording for
  album lists and change only the artist part.

`src/ui/views/browse.rs`, `src/ui/views/tests/mod.rs`, `src/ui/views/tests/browse.rs`,

### Show the album lists' total playing time beside their album count in the footer, like the song-list footer (planned 2026-10-29 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-29 by the feature role

**Goal.** Song lists' footers read `2 songs - 3:30`, and the Genres, Years, and Composers rows
read `3 songs - 10:30`. The three album lists (an artist's Albums, All Albums, Recently Added)
only show a count, `3 albums`, even though every row already shows that album's running time
(`Album::duration_ms`, filled for the sample library and for the signed-in loads by
`with_album_durations` in `src/apple_music/browse.rs`). Make an album list's footer read
`<count> album(s) - <total>`, such as `3 albums - 45:30`. The total is the sum of the rows'
`duration_ms`, formatted by `format_minutes_seconds`, with a trailing `+` when any album has
`duration_ms == 0` (no reported songs), the same rule `song_list_summary` uses for unknown
song lengths: `1 album - 0:00+`. The album footer has no selected-row form: selecting an album
row does not change it. The artist and playlist footers, the empty-list case (no footer),
and the row labels do not change. This plan touches none of the files the waiting
release-year search plan above does.

**Approach.**
- `src/ui/views/browse/rows/text.rs`: add
  `pub(in crate::ui::views) fn album_list_summary(albums: &[Album]) -> String` next to
  `song_list_summary`. Sum `duration_ms` with `u64::saturating_add`, pick `album`/`albums` by
  `albums.len() == 1`, format the total with `format_minutes_seconds`, append `+` unless every
  album's `duration_ms != 0`, and return `format!("{count} {noun} - {total}")`. Write a doc comment
  in the same style as `song_list_summary`'s. Edit `list_count_summary`'s doc comment so it covers
  only the artist and playlist footers.
- `src/ui/views/browse/rows.rs`, `album_list`: stop wrapping in `list_with_count(..., "album",
  "albums")`. Build the `scrollable_list` and return it alone when `albums.is_empty()`;
  otherwise return `with_footer(list, album_list_summary(albums))`, the same shape `song_list`
  has. Import `album_list_summary` from `text`. Update the doc comments of `album_list`,
  `with_footer`, and `list_with_count` so they say album lists use the count-and-time footer.
- `src/ui/views/tests/mod.rs`: add `album_list_summary` to the `text` import list.
- `src/ui/views/tests/browse.rs`: add
  `album_list_summary_counts_albums_and_sums_their_running_time`. Use `sample_album()` copies
  (`src/test_support/fixtures.rs`) with `duration_ms` set. One album at 630_000 →
  `"1 album - 10:30"`. Two at 630_000 and 210_000 → `"2 albums - 14:00"`. 630_000 and 0 →
  `"2 albums - 10:30+"`. One at 0 → `"1 album - 0:00+"`. Add a second album with
  `u64::MAX` beside one at 1_000 so the sum saturates without panicking; assert only that the
  result starts with `"2 albums - "`.
- `src/ui/tests/view_tests.rs`: `root_view_draws_the_current_browse_levels_own_rows` expects
  `"1 album"` for `CurrentView::Albums` and `CurrentView::AllAlbums`; the fixture album has
  `duration_ms: 0`, so change both expectations to `"1 album - 0:00+"`. In
  `an_empty_browse_level_draws_no_count_footer`, change the absent-footer strings for `Albums` and
  `AllAlbums` from `"0 albums"` to `"0 albums - 0:00"`, so the test still pins the footer that
  must not be drawn.
- `docs/usage.md`: in the browse-list paragraph, the clause "and artist, album, and playlist
  lists showing their item count beneath theirs" becomes "album lists showing their album
  count and total playing time beneath theirs (`3 albums - 45:30`, with the same trailing `+`
  when an album has no known running time), and artist and playlist lists showing their item
  count beneath theirs".

**Files touched.** `src/ui/views/browse/rows/text.rs`, `src/ui/views/browse/rows.rs`,
`src/ui/views/tests/mod.rs`, `src/ui/views/tests/browse.rs`, `src/ui/tests/view_tests.rs`,
`docs/usage.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A non-empty Albums, All Albums, or Recently Added list draws the footer
  `<count> album(s) - <total>`, and the `+` mark follows the rule above; the new unit test

- An empty album list still draws only its placeholder (the updated

- Artist and playlist footers still read `N artists` / `N playlists`

### Match release years in the offline library search, like Winamp's quick search (planned 2026-10-29 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-29 by the feature role

**Goal.** With no Apple Music session, the `Search library` box matches a song's title, artist,
album title, genre, and composer (`sample_songs_matching` in `src/apple_music/sample.rs`), but
not its release year, though the Years list and the File info panel both show it. Winamp's
Media Library quick search matches every column, the year included. Make the offline search also
match a song whose `Song::year`, written as a plain decimal number (`2001`), contains the trimmed
query, so typing `2003` returns the songs from 2003. A song with `year: None` never matches by
year. The signed-in REST search, the blank-query rejection, and result order do not change.
This plan is independent of the grouped-row playing-time plan above: it touches none of its files.

**Approach.**
- `src/apple_music/sample.rs`, `sample_songs_matching`: add one more `||` arm to the filter,
  `song.year.is_some_and(|year| year.to_string().contains(&needle))`. Plain substring, the same
  as the other fields, so `200` matches every song from 2000–2009. Update the doc comment's field
  list to "title, artist, album title, genre, composer, or release year".
- `src/apple_music/browse.rs`, `AppleMusicService::search_songs` doc comment: add release year to
  the signed-out field list.
- `src/apple_music/tests/browse_sample.rs`: add
  `search_songs_matches_the_sample_library_by_release_year`, using the sample library's years
  (song-1..song-3 are 2001, song-4 is 2003, song-5 is 2005):
  - `"  2001  "` returns `song-1`, `song-2`, `song-3` in that order (whitespace trimmed);
  - `"2003"` returns only `song-4`; `"2005"` returns only `song-5`;
  - `"200"` returns all five songs in library order (substring match);
  - `"1999"` returns an empty list.
  Before adding the test, confirm no sample title, artist, album title, genre, or composer
  contains these digit strings (none does today), so the year arm is what makes them match.
- `docs/invariants.md`, `## Library search matching`: add release year to the Guarantee's and
  Enforced-by's field lists, and add the new test to Pinned by.
- `docs/usage.md`: in the `Search library` sentence, extend "title, artist, album title, genre,
  and composer" to "title, artist, album title, genre, composer, and release year".

**Files touched.** `src/apple_music/sample.rs`, `src/apple_music/browse.rs` (doc comment only),
`src/apple_music/tests/browse_sample.rs`, `docs/invariants.md`, `docs/usage.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Signed out, searching `2003` lists only `B-side` (song-4); searching `2001` lists the three
  First Record songs in library order; `200` lists all five sample songs in library order;
  `1999` lists none.
- Existing search tests (`..._by_title_or_artist`, `..._by_album_title`,
  `..._by_genre_or_composer`, `search_songs_rejects_a_blank_query`,
  `search_songs_uses_the_rest_library_when_signed_in`) pass unchanged.
- No new dependency, message, state, or setting; the REST path is untouched.
- `docs/usage.md` and `docs/invariants.md` name release year as a searched field, and
  `make check` passes.

### Show each Genres, Years, and Composers row's total playing time beside its song count, like the song-list footer (planned 2026-10-29 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-29 by the feature role

**Goal.** A Genres, Years, or Composers row's secondary label reads only `1 song` / `N songs`
(`song_count_label` in `src/ui/song_groups.rs`). Album rows already show their running time, and
opening a group shows a song-list footer of `N songs - M:SS`. Winamp's Media Library shows the
same per-row totals. Make each grouped row's label read the way that footer does:
`<count> song(s) - <total>`, for example `2 songs - 5:05`. As in the footer, a total that
includes a song of unknown length (`duration_ms == 0`) gets a trailing `+`, for example
`2 songs - 3:30+` or `1 song - 0:00+`. Grouping, row order, and row names stay the same.

**Approach.**
- `src/ui/song_groups.rs`: rename `song_count_label` to `group_row_label` and rewrite its doc
  comment. Sum `group.songs`' `duration_ms` with `u64::saturating_add`, format the sum with
  `crate::ui::views::format_minutes_seconds` (already `pub(in crate::ui)` in
  `src/ui/views/mod.rs`), and append `+` when any song's `duration_ms` is `0`. The result is
  `format!("{count} {noun} - {total}")`, where `noun` is `song` for one song and `songs` for
  any other count. The arithmetic and wording follow `song_list_summary` in
  `src/ui/views/browse/rows/text.rs`, using its unselected form. Do not change that function's
  visibility or call it: it is `pub(in crate::ui::views)`, and the grouped label takes only a few
  lines.
- `src/ui/handlers/browse/fetch.rs`: update the `use` and the three `store_with_labels(…,

### Show each album row's release year beside its running time, like Winamp's Media Library (planned 2026-10-29 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-29 by the feature role

**Goal.** Winamp's Media Library album view has a Year column. Nostalgia's album rows (per-artist
Albums, All Albums, Recently Added) show `artist - title` and, at the right, only the running
time (`10:30`). Show the album's release year before the running time, `2001  10:30` (two
spaces between them). An album with no known year still shows only `10:30` (or `--:--`).

**Approach.**
- `src/library.rs`: add `pub year: Option<u16>` to `Album`, marked `#[serde(default)]` and with a
  doc comment matching `Song::year`'s (`None` means the source supplied no usable release date).
  Add `year: None,` to every `Album { .. }` struct literal (`grep -rn 'Album {' src` lists them,
  in about 13 files, most of them tests). The exceptions are the sample albums below and
  `into_album`.
- `src/apple_music/rest/wire/mapping.rs` `Resource::into_album`: read `attributes.release_date`
  next to `name`/`artist_name` and set `year: release_date.as_deref().and_then(release_year)`,
  which reuses the existing `release_year` helper that `into_song` uses. `Attributes::release_date`
  already exists in `src/apple_music/rest/wire.rs`, so the wire struct does not change.
- `src/sample_library.rs`: give the sample albums the years their songs carry: `First Record`
  `Some(2001)`, `Second Record` `Some(2003)`, `Debut` `Some(2005)`.
- `src/ui/views/mod.rs`: next to `pub fn format_track_time`, add
  `pub fn album_row_label(album: &Album) -> String`. It returns
  `format!("{year}  {}", format_track_time(album.duration_ms))` when `album.year` is `Some`, else
  `format_track_time(album.duration_ms)`. Make it the fallback label in `album_row`
  (`src/ui/views/browse/rows/text.rs`). Then `store_albums` in `src/ui/handlers/browse/fetch.rs` passes
  `views::album_row_label` instead of `views::format_track_time(album.duration_ms)`, so the cached
  label and the fallback match.
- Sorting, Jump to File and selection read `display_title`, so they do not change.

**Files touched.** `src/library.rs`, `src/apple_music/rest/wire/mapping.rs`,
`src/sample_library.rs`, `src/ui/views/mod.rs`, `src/ui/views/browse/rows/text.rs`,

`docs/invariants.md`.

### Share one song-grouping module between the Genres and Years lists (planned 2026-10-29 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-29 by the feature role

**Goal.** `src/ui/genres.rs` (`Genre`, `group_by_genre`) and `src/ui/years.rs` (`Year`,
`group_by_year`) are near-line-for-line copies: the same `{ name, songs }` row struct, the same
find-or-push grouping loop, the same trailing `Unknown` group and the same `song_count_label`.
Extract the shared part into one module, so a further grouped list (Composers, say) becomes a
key function instead of a third copy. This is a refactor: nothing the player shows changes.

**Approach.**
- New `src/ui/song_groups.rs` (declare `mod song_groups;` in `src/ui/mod.rs`), holding:
  - `pub(in crate::ui) struct SongGroup { pub(in crate::ui) name: String, pub(in crate::ui) songs: Vec<Song> }`
    with the derives `Genre` has today (`Debug, Clone, PartialEq`).
  - `pub(in crate::ui) fn group_songs<K: Ord>(songs: Vec<Song>, key: impl Fn(&Song) -> Option<(K, String)>) -> Vec<SongGroup>`:
    `key` returns `None` for a song with no value (it goes in the `Unknown` group) or
    `Some((sort_key, display_name))`. Songs with equal sort keys share a group named after the
    first display name seen; groups are ordered by sort key, songs keep input order inside a
    group, and an `Unknown` group (the `"Unknown"` constant moves here) is appended last only
    when non-empty. Same algorithm as today's two loops.
  - `songs_label` (moved from `genres.rs`) and `song_count_label(group: &SongGroup)`.
- `src/ui/genres.rs`: `pub(in crate::ui) type Genre = SongGroup;`, and `group_by_genre` becomes
  `group_songs(songs, |song| …)` returning `Some((trimmed.to_lowercase(), trimmed.to_string()))`
  for a non-blank trimmed genre, else `None`. Re-export `song_count_label` (`pub(in crate::ui) use`)
  or update its one caller in `src/ui/handlers/browse/fetch.rs` `genres_loaded` to import it from
  `song_groups`. Its existing tests stay and must pass unchanged.
- `src/ui/years.rs`: `pub(in crate::ui) type Year = SongGroup;`, and `group_by_year` becomes
  `group_songs(songs, |song| song.year.map(|year| (year, year.to_string())))`. Drop its
  `song_count_label` and its `use super::genres::songs_label`; point `years_loaded` in
  `fetch.rs` at `song_groups::song_count_label`. Its existing tests stay and must pass unchanged.
- Callers that name `Genre`/`Year` (`src/ui/player.rs`, `src/ui/message.rs`,
  `src/ui/views/browse.rs`, `src/ui/tests/mod.rs`, `src/ui/tests/sort_tests.rs` struct literals)
  keep compiling through the aliases; no edit is needed there beyond what the compiler demands.
- No `docs/usage.md` change (nothing visible changes). No `docs/invariants.md` change: its
  browse sections name behaviors and test names, none of which move.

**Tests.** In `src/ui/song_groups.rs`'s own `#[cfg(test)]` module, with a key over `Song::id`
or `Song::genre` built from `crate::test_support::sample_song`:
- groups are ordered by sort key, not by display name or first appearance;
- two songs with equal keys but different display names share one group named after the first;
- `None`-keyed songs form a last `Unknown` group, and no `Unknown` group appears when every song
  has a key;
- `song_count_label` reads `1 song` / `2 songs`.
Move `genres.rs`'s `count_label_pluralizes` test here, or keep it there if
`song_count_label` stays re-exported from `genres`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `genres.rs` and `years.rs` each contain only their alias, their key function wrapper and their
  existing behavior tests; neither has its own grouping loop or `Unknown` constant.
- The pre-existing tests in `genres.rs`, `years.rs`, `src/ui/tests/flat_lists_tests.rs`,
  `src/ui/tests/years_tests.rs` and `src/ui/tests/sort_tests.rs` pass without edits to their
  assertions; the new `song_groups` tests pass; `make check` passes.
- Independent of "Reopen the library at the Years list across launches (part 2/2)": that plan
  touches settings, `library_view` and `restore_view`, not the grouping modules.

### Browse the library by genre from a Genres list, like Winamp's Media Library (part 1/2) (planned 2026-10-29 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-29 by the feature role

**Goal.** Winamp's Media Library lets you filter the audio library by Genre. Nostalgia shows each
song's primary genre in File info and uses it for AUTO (`Song::genre`, filled by
`primary_genre` in `src/apple_music/rest/wire/mapping.rs`), but you can't browse by it. Add a
`Genres` button to the Artists view. It opens a Genres list with one row per genre and the
genre's song count. Opening a row shows that genre's songs in the Songs view, and Back returns to
Genres. Part 2/2 ("Reopen the library at the Genres list across launches") makes the list
persist across launches.

**Approach.**

  { name: String, songs: Vec<Song> }` (derive `Debug, Clone, PartialEq`) and a pure
  `pub(in crate::ui) fn group_by_genre(songs: Vec<Song>) -> Vec<Genre>`. Group by
  `song.genre.trim()`, comparing names case-insensitively, and name the group after the first
  spelling seen. Order groups by lowercase name. Songs with a blank genre go in a group named
  `Unknown`, always last; the sample library does set genres, so signed out it shows Alternative, Electronic, and Rock. Songs
  inside a group keep their input (library) order.

- `src/ui/message.rs`: add `ShowGenres`, `GenresLoaded(Vec<Genre>)`, `GenresLoadFailed(String)`,
  and `GenreSelected { epoch: u64, index: usize }`, documented like their Playlists twins. Route
  them in `src/ui/mod.rs`'s `update`.
- `src/ui/handlers/browse.rs`:
  - `show_genres`: a copy of `show_playlists` that calls
    `fetch_level(&mut player.genres, …, "loading library genres", |service| async move {
    service.get_all_songs().await.map(group_by_genre) }, Message::GenresLoaded,
    Message::GenresLoadFailed)`.
  - `genre_selected`: resolve the row with `player.genres.select(epoch, index)` and clone its
    songs. Call `player.songs.begin_fetch()` so an in-flight album or playlist `SongsLoaded`

- Views: in `src/ui/views/browse.rs`, add `view_genres` (a copy of `view_playlists` that uses

### Shift+click Stop fades the song out and then stops, like Winamp (planned 2026-10-28 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-29 by the feature role

**Goal.** In Winamp a Shift-held click on the Stop button fades the playing song out before
stopping, the same as Shift+V. Our Shift+V already does this (`Message::FadeOutAndStop`, handled by
`handlers::playback::fade::fade_out_and_stop`), but the ■ button always sends `Message::Stop`, so a
Shift-click stops at once. Make a Shift-held click on Stop fade out and stop in the main transport
row, the shade strip, and the library footer. This plan does not touch the waiting "Reopen the
library at the last top-level browse list" plan's files beyond `src/ui/mod.rs` and
`src/ui/message.rs` (separate arms and variants).

**Approach.** Decided, so the implementer has no open questions. It follows the Ctrl-click
Previous/Next pattern (`control_held`, `listeners::modifiers_message`, `stepping::previous_button`).
- Carry Shift with Control. In `src/ui/message.rs`, replace `ControlHeld(bool)` with
  `ModifiersHeld { control: bool, shift: bool }` (comment: whether Control and Shift are held; both
  false when the window loses focus), and add `StopButton` next to `NextButton`/`PreviousButton`
  (comment: a click on Stop: fade out and stop while Shift is held, otherwise stop at once).
- `src/ui/player.rs` `WinampPlayer`: add `pub(in crate::ui) shift_held: bool` beside
  `control_held` (doc: tracked from modifier events so a Shift-click on Stop fades out; not saved in
  settings), `false` at construction.
- `src/ui/subscriptions/listeners.rs` `modifiers_message`: `ModifiersChanged(m)` gives
  `ModifiersHeld { control: m.control(), shift: m.shift() }`; window `Unfocused` gives both false.
  Update its doc comment to name Shift and the Stop button.
- `src/ui/mod.rs` update: the `ModifiersHeld { control, shift }` arm sets `player.control_held` and
  `player.shift_held` and returns `Task::none()`. `StopButton` calls a new
  `handlers::playback::fade::stop_button(player)`, which returns `fade_out_and_stop(player)` while
  `shift_held` and `stop(player)` otherwise. A Shift-click therefore keeps every Shift+V guarantee
  (acts as Stop while paused or stopped; a second Shift-click mid-fade leaves the countdown alone),
  and a plain click mid-fade keeps Stop's stop-then-restore-volume behavior.
- `src/ui/views/transport.rs` `transport_glyphs`: the Stop entry sends `Message::StopButton`; the
  shade strip and library footer pick it up through `views::mini_transport`. Extend the doc
  comment's last sentence to say Stop sends its button message, which fades out while Shift is
  held. Keys keep their messages: V and the media Stop key still send `Message::Stop`.
- Only Shift matters for Stop, and only Control for Previous/Next: a Shift-click on Previous/Next
  and a Ctrl-click on Stop behave like plain clicks. No other button changes.

**Files touched.** src/ui/message.rs, src/ui/player.rs, src/ui/mod.rs,
src/ui/subscriptions/listeners.rs, src/ui/handlers/playback/fade.rs, src/ui/views/transport.rs,
src/ui/views/tests/transport.rs (`glyphs[3].3` asserts `Message::StopButton`),
src/ui/views/tests/shade.rs (`messages[3]` asserts `Message::StopButton`),
src/ui/tests/ctrl_click_tests.rs (switch its `ControlHeld(..)` sends and asserts to
`ModifiersHeld { .. }`), src/ui/tests/fade_tests.rs, docs/usage.md, docs/invariants.md.

**Tests.**
- In src/ui/tests/fade_tests.rs, using its `playing_with_recording`, `tick`, and `volumes` helpers:
  `shift_click_stop_starts_the_fade` (send `ModifiersHeld { control: false, shift: true }` then
  `StopButton` while playing: no backend call on the click, `fade_out_ticks == FADE_OUT_TICKS`,
  and ticking runs the same volume steps and final Stop as Shift+V);
  `plain_stop_click_stops_at_once` (with `shift_held` false, `StopButton` records `AudioCall::Stop`
  and starts no fade); `shift_release_restores_a_plain_stop_click` (Shift held then released, then
  `StopButton` stops at once).
- In src/ui/tests/ctrl_click_tests.rs, `modifiers_message_tracks_control_and_focus_loss` asserts
  `ModifiersChanged(Modifiers::CTRL)` gives `{ control: true, shift: false }`,
  `ModifiersChanged(Modifiers::SHIFT)` gives `{ control: false, shift: true }`, `Unfocused` gives
  both false, and a `KeyPressed` gives `None`; the Ctrl-click tests keep passing with
  `ModifiersHeld { control: true, shift: false }`, and a new `shift_click_previous_steps_one_song`
  checks Shift alone leaves `PreviousButton` a one-song step.

**Docs.** docs/usage.md: after the Shift+V clause in the keyboard paragraph ("…while paused or
stopped it acts as Stop)"), add that a Shift-held click on the Stop button, in the transport row,
the shade strip, or the library footer, does the same, while a plain click stops at once.
docs/invariants.md `## Fade-out stop`: extend the guarantee to a Shift-clicked Stop
(`Message::StopButton`), name `fade::stop_button` and `listeners::modifiers_message` under
Enforced by, and add the new tests to Pinned by. In `## List edge jumps`, rename the
`control_held` sentence's message to the new `ModifiersHeld`. In the two sections that list the
strips' button messages (`Message::PreviousButton`, `Message::Play`, `Message::Pause`,
`Message::Stop`, `Message::NextButton`), change `Message::Stop` to `Message::StopButton`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With Shift held, clicking ■ in any of the three transport rows while a preview plays fades the
  output volume down over about two seconds and then stops, exactly like Shift+V, leaving the saved
  volume unchanged; while paused or stopped it stops at once.
- Without Shift, the Stop button stops exactly as today; Ctrl-click on Previous/Next still jumps to
  the list's edge, and Shift alone does not.
- Losing window focus clears both held flags.
- Every keyboard binding maps to the same message as before (V and media Stop send `Message::Stop`).
- The new tests pass, the docs describe the Shift-click, and `make check` passes.

### Reopen the library at the last top-level browse list across launches, like Winamp's Media Library (planned 2026-10-28 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-28 by the feature role

**Goal.** Winamp's Media Library reopens on the node it last showed. Nostalgia always opens on
Artists, so a user who lives in All Songs or Playlists clicks through on every launch. Save which
top-level browse list was showing and reopen it at the next launch. Persist only the top-level
list, never a drilled-in album, playlist, or search: those ids can go stale between launches.

**Approach.**
1. New file `src/settings/library_view.rs` (declare it `pub mod library_view;` in
   `src/settings.rs`). It holds `pub enum LibraryView { Artists, AllSongs, AllAlbums, RecentlyAdded,
   RecentlyPlayed, Playlists }` (derive `Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default`, with
   `#[default] Artists`), plus `fn key(self) -> &'static str` returning `artists`, `all_songs`,
   `all_albums`, `recently_added`, `recently_played`, `playlists`, and
   `fn from_key(&str) -> Option<Self>`, its exact inverse.
2. `src/settings.rs` `Settings`: add a `library_view: LibraryView` field, defaulting to `Artists`
   in `Default` and in `from_state`, with a `library_view()` getter and a `set_library_view` setter
   beside `window_position`. Update the struct doc comment's list of player-owned fields.
   `src/settings/text.rs`: `to_text` writes `library_view=<key>` on every save. `from_text` gets a
   `"library_view"` arm that sets the field when `LibraryView::from_key(value.trim())` is `Some` and
   otherwise keeps the default.
3. `src/ui/player.rs`: add `pub(in crate::ui) fn library_view(&self) -> LibraryView`, which maps the
   browse state to its top-level list. An active search (`search_active`) gives `Artists`, because
   Back from a search goes to Artists. `CurrentView::Artists` and `Albums` give `Artists`. Each flat
   view gives itself. `Songs` gives the list it came from by `songs_origin`: `Album` gives
   `Artists`, `AllAlbums` gives `AllAlbums`, `RecentlyAdded` gives `RecentlyAdded`, and `Playlist`
   gives `Playlists`. `persist_settings_if_changed` calls
   `snapshot.set_library_view(self.library_view())`. `adopt_saved_settings` leaves the view alone
   (the restore is a task, step 4). Update its doc comment.
4. `src/ui/handlers/browse.rs`: add `pub(in crate::ui) fn restore_view(player, view: LibraryView)
   -> Task<Message>`. It returns `Task::none()` for `Artists`. For the other views it returns the
   matching existing handler (`show_all_songs`, `show_all_albums`, `show_recently_added`,
   `show_recently_played`, `show_playlists`). In `src/ui/mod.rs` `init_ui`'s boot closure, after
   `adopt_saved_settings`, batch the boot task with `restore_view(&mut player,
   saved.library_view())`. `boot` keeps its `LoadArtists`, because Back from a restored list
   returns to Artists and needs those rows.
5. Signed-in launches. `boot` starts the first fetches before the background sign-in stores a
   session, so they answer from the sample library. Today only the artists list is refetched when
   the session arrives: `wait_for_session` maps to `Message::LoadArtists`. A restored All Songs
   list would keep its sample rows. Add `Message::SessionReady` in `src/ui/message.rs` and map
   `boot`'s `wait_for_session` future to it in place of `LoadArtists`. Route it in `update` to a new
   `handlers::browse::session_ready(player)`. That handler batches `fetch::load_artists(player)`
   with, when `!player.search_active` and `current_view` is one of the five flat views,
   `restore_view` for that view, which refetches it and snaps it to the top. Albums, Songs, and
   search results are left as they are today. Update the `wait_for_session` doc comment in
   `src/apple_music.rs`, which names `Message::LoadArtists`.

**Files touched.** `src/settings/library_view.rs` (new), `src/settings.rs`,
`src/settings/text.rs`, `src/ui/player.rs`, `src/ui/handlers/browse.rs`, `src/ui/mod.rs`,
`src/ui/message.rs`, `src/apple_music.rs` (doc comment only), `src/ui/tests/settings_tests.rs`,
`src/ui/tests/loading_tests.rs` with the `await_boot_artist_loads` helper in
`src/ui/tests/mod.rs`, `docs/usage.md`, and `docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `LibraryView::from_key(v.key()) == Some(v)` for each of the six variants, and
  `from_key("albums")` and `from_key("")` are `None`.
- A `Settings` with `set_library_view(LibraryView::Playlists)` round-trips through
  `to_text`/`from_text`. `from_text("library_view=bogus\n")` and text with no `library_view` line
  both give `LibraryView::Artists`.
- Settings tests on `test_player()` with a `MemorySettingsStore`, in the same way as
  `toggle_panels_reach_the_saved_snapshot`: after `update(.., Message::ShowAllSongs)` the latest
  snapshot's `library_view()` is `AllSongs`. A
  Songs view opened from Playlists saves `Playlists`, a Songs view opened from an artist's album
  saves `Artists`, and an active search saves `Artists`.
- `restore_view(&mut player, LibraryView::RecentlyAdded)` leaves `current_view ==
  CurrentView::RecentlyAdded`, and `restore_view(.., Artists)` leaves `CurrentView::Artists`.
- `session_ready` on a player showing All Albums schedules both the artists fetch and an All
  Albums refetch. On the Albums view or with a search active, it leaves `current_view` and
  `search_active` unchanged.
- `boot_schedules_loading_the_artist_list` still passes unchanged.
  `boot_reloads_artists_after_the_startup_sign_in_stores_a_session` (and the
  `await_boot_artist_loads` helper it uses) is updated to wait for a `Message::SessionReady` output
  after the first `LoadArtists`, in place of a second `LoadArtists`, and passes.
- `docs/usage.md`'s settings paragraph adds "the library's top-level browse list (Artists, All
  Songs, All Albums, Recently Added, Recently Played, or Playlists; a list opened from one of them
  saves that one)" to the list of saved values, and says a list showing when sign-in completes is
  refetched from the signed-in library. `docs/invariants.md` `## Settings persistence` names
  `library_view` beside the other player-owned values and the new tests.
- `make check` passes.

### Shift+V fades the playing song out and then stops, like Winamp's "Fade out and stop" (planned 2026-10-28 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-28 by the feature role

**Goal.** Winamp's Shift+V fades the playing song out and then stops. Nostalgia binds V to Stop.
The plain-key match in `src/ui/shortcuts.rs` `shortcut` matches the letter ignoring case and allows
Shift, so Shift+V is a plain Stop today. Add the fade: Shift+V while a preview plays lowers the
output volume to silence over two seconds, then stops exactly like Stop. The saved volume never
changes, so the slider, the settings file, and the next play keep the user's level.

**Approach.**
- Fixed fade length: `FADE_OUT_TICKS: u8 = 8` steps of the existing LCD timer (`MARQUEE_TICK`,
  250 ms), so about 2 s. This plan makes that call (it fits 30-second previews), so no question
  is left open. Put the constant beside `MIXER_FLASH_TICKS` in `src/ui/player.rs`. Add a
  `fade_out_ticks: u8` field to `WinampPlayer` (start 0, never saved). Make
  `WinampPlayer::needs_lcd_tick` also return true while `fade_out_ticks > 0`, so the marquee
  subscription runs during a fade (`src/ui/mod.rs` already passes `needs_lcd_tick()` to
  `subscriptions`).
- New `Message::FadeOutAndStop` in `src/ui/message.rs`, dispatched in `src/ui/mod.rs` `update`
  next to `Message::Stop`. In `shortcut`'s plain-key match, add an arm before the `"v"` → `Stop`
  arm: `"v"` with `modifiers.shift()` gives `FadeOutAndStop`. Plain V stays Stop. Ctrl+V and
  Ctrl+Shift+V stay `ToggleStopAfterCurrent`, because the Control block runs first.
- New module `src/ui/handlers/playback/fade.rs`, declared beside `preview`/`stepping`/
  `title_drag` in `src/ui/handlers/playback.rs`, holding:
  - `fade_out_and_stop(player)`: when shared state `is_playing` is false (stopped or paused;
    Pause clears it), behave exactly like `playback::stop`. When a fade is already running, do
    nothing. Otherwise set `fade_out_ticks = FADE_OUT_TICKS` and return `Task::none()`; no
    backend call happens on the press itself.
  - `fade_out_tick(player) -> Task<Message>`: called at the top of `playback::marquee_tick`,
    with the existing flash/offset logic left as it is. With `fade_out_ticks > 0`, decrement it.
    If ticks remain, forward `state.volume() * remaining / FADE_OUT_TICKS` through
    `AppleMusicService::set_output_volume`. Log a failure the way `seek_preview` does, and never
    write shared state. When it reaches 0, return `stop_restoring_volume(player)`.
    `marquee_tick` returns that task.
  - `stop_restoring_volume(player)`: does what `playback::stop` does
    (`reset_position_readout`, `begin_position_transition`, then `transport_into`). Its
    action is `service.stop().await?; service.set_output_volume(volume)`, where `volume` is
    `state.volume()` read before spawning. The restore therefore reaches the backend only after
    the audio has stopped, so a muted backend cannot carry over into a later Play-after-Stop
    resume (`resume_locked` does not re-send the volume).
  - `cancel_fade_out(player)`: when `fade_out_ticks > 0`, zero it and forward `state.volume()`
    to the backend. Otherwise do nothing.
- Interruptions: `playback::play`, `pause`, and `play_pause` call `cancel_fade_out` first.
  `track_selected` calls it once the song resolves (after its `let Some(song)` early return), so
  Next, Previous, row plays, and preview-end advances keep playing at full volume. `playback::stop`
  with a fade running zeroes the ticks and returns `stop_restoring_volume(player)`. With no fade it
  stays unchanged, so the existing `AudioCall::Stop`-only assertions still hold. A volume nudge
  during a fade stores and forwards the new level as today, and the next tick rescales from it.
- The options menu gets no row (it is a full, non-scrolling column).

**Files touched.** `src/ui/shortcuts.rs` (binding and its tests), `src/ui/message.rs`,
`src/ui/mod.rs`, `src/ui/player.rs`, `src/ui/handlers/playback.rs`, new
`src/ui/handlers/playback/fade.rs`, new `src/ui/tests/fade_tests.rs` (registered in
`src/ui/tests/mod.rs`; drive it like `transport_tests.rs`/`mixer_tests.rs` with the recording
audio fake and `AudioCall`), `docs/usage.md`, `docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `message_for` maps Shift+V (`"V"` and `"v"` with `Modifiers::SHIFT`) to
  `Message::FadeOutAndStop`, and plain `v` to `Message::Stop`. Ctrl+V and Ctrl+Shift+V still map
  to `ToggleStopAfterCurrent`. `assert_letter_bindings` is shared with the Shift-held uppercase
  mapper, so its `v` → `Stop` check moves to the unshifted test only.
- While playing, `FadeOutAndStop` records no audio call and makes `needs_lcd_tick()` true. Each of
  the next seven `MarqueeTick`s records exactly one `AudioCall::SetVolume` lower than the last
  (7/8, 6/8, … 1/8 of the saved volume). The eighth runs the returned task and records
  `AudioCall::Stop` followed by `SetVolume(saved volume)`. Afterwards shared state is stopped,
  `state.volume()` equals its value before the fade, and `needs_lcd_tick()` reflects only the
  title/flash again.
- While paused or stopped, `FadeOutAndStop` records the same calls as `Message::Stop` and starts
  no fade (`fade_out_ticks` stays 0).
- A second `FadeOutAndStop` mid-fade does not restart the countdown.
- `Play` (and a `TrackSelected` play) mid-fade records `SetVolume(saved volume)`, zeroes the fade,
  and later ticks record no `SetVolume` and no `Stop`. `Stop` mid-fade records `Stop` and then
  `SetVolume(saved volume)`.
- The settings file written after a full fade holds the pre-fade volume.
- `docs/usage.md`'s keyboard paragraph (beside "V stops, Ctrl+V arms …") says Shift+V fades the
  playing song out over about two seconds and then stops, leaving the volume setting unchanged,
  and acts as Stop while paused or stopped. `docs/invariants.md` gets a short `## Fade-out stop`
  section stating those guarantees and naming the new tests under Pinned by.
- `make check` passes.

### Remember the window's screen position across launches, like Winamp (planned 2026-10-28 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-28 by the feature role

**Goal.** Winamp reopens where it was last left on screen. Nostalgia saves every other layout
choice (the readout mode, visualizer, EQ and library panels, always-on-top, shade mode), but the
window opens wherever the window manager puts it on every launch. Persist the window's last
reported screen position in the settings file and open the next launch there. The window is not
resizable (`init_ui` calls `.resizable(false)`), so position is the only placement worth saving;
size stays unpersisted. On Wayland iced reports no moves and ignores a requested position, so
there the line is never written and behavior is unchanged.

**Approach.**

- `src/settings.rs`: add a private `window_position: Option<(f32, f32)>` field, kept as plain
  floats so the settings module stays free of iced types. `Settings::default` and
  `Settings::from_state` leave it `None`. Add `window_position()` / `set_window_position(Option<(f32,
  f32)>)` accessors in the same style as `shaded()` / `set_shaded`. `apply_to` leaves it alone (it is
  player-owned like the other six). Update the module, struct, and `shaded()` docs: the "window's
  size and position are deliberately not persisted" sentences now say the position is persisted
  and the size is not; the UI-owned count goes from six to seven.
- `src/settings/text.rs`: `to_text` writes `window_position=<x>,<y>\n` (f32 `Display`, so `120,80`
  or `120.5,-40`) only when the field is `Some`, so files written without a known position stay
  as they are. `from_text` handles a `"window_position"` key with a new `parse_window_position`
  helper: `split_once(',')`, trim each half, parse both as `f32`, and accept the pair only when
  both are finite (`f32::is_finite`, which rejects NaN and the infinities). A malformed value
  leaves the field unchanged, matching `parse_into`'s rule. Negative coordinates are valid,
  because a monitor left of or above the primary has them.
- `src/ui/player.rs`: add a `window_position: Option<(f32, f32)>` field on `WinampPlayer` (initialized
  `None` in `WinampPlayer::new`). `persist_settings_if_changed` calls
  `snapshot.set_window_position(self.window_position)`, and `adopt_saved_settings` restores
  `self.window_position = saved.window_position()`. Update both doc comments.
- `src/ui/message.rs`: add `WindowMoved(iced::Point)`. `src/ui/mod.rs`'s `update` routes it to a new
  `handlers::window::window_moved(player, point)` in `src/ui/handlers/window.rs`, which stores
  `Some((point.x, point.y))` and returns `Task::none()`. `update`'s existing trailing
  `persist_settings_if_changed` call then saves it. A drag-move sends many events, and
  `BackgroundWriter` already collapses a burst to its newest snapshot.
- `src/ui/subscriptions/listeners.rs`: add `window_moved_message(event, status, window)`, mapping
  `iced::Event::Window(iced::window::Event::Moved(point))` to `Some(Message::WindowMoved(point))`
  and every other event to `None`. Re-export it from `src/ui/subscriptions/mod.rs` beside
  `modifiers_message`, and push `iced::event::listen_with(window_moved_message)` into the
  always-on `subscriptions` vector there. Extend the `subscriptions` doc comment.
- Restore at launch: add `pub(in crate::ui) fn launch_position(saved: Option<(f32, f32)>) ->
  iced::window::Position` in `src/ui/handlers/window.rs`, returning `Position::Specific(Point::new(x,
  y))` for `Some` and `Position::Default` for `None`. `init_ui` in `src/ui/mod.rs` chains
  `.position(handlers::window::launch_position(saved.window_position()))` on the
  `iced::application` builder (iced 0.14's `Application::position`) before `.run()`. The
  `saved` snapshot is already in scope there; read it before the boot closure moves it, or clone it.
  Decided, not left open: no clamping to monitor bounds, because iced cannot query monitors
  before the window opens. A position saved on a since-removed monitor is restored as saved,
  and the usage doc names deleting the `window_position` line as the fix.

**Files touched.** `src/settings.rs`, `src/settings/text.rs`, `src/ui/player.rs`, `src/ui/message.rs`,
`src/ui/mod.rs`, `src/ui/handlers/window.rs`, `src/ui/subscriptions/listeners.rs`,
`src/ui/subscriptions/mod.rs`, `src/ui/tests/settings_tests.rs` (or the listener tests' module),
`docs/usage.md`, `docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- `src/settings.rs` tests: a new `window_position_round_trips_and_ignores_malformed_values` shows
  that `Some((120.0, -40.5))` survives `to_text` → `from_text`, that a default snapshot's text
  has no `window_position` line, and that `window_position=abc`, `window_position=10`,
  `window_position=NaN,5`, and `window_position=inf,5` each leave it `None`.
  `to_text_round_trips_every_field` (with `state_with_every_field_set` or its caller) sets a
  position so the full round trip covers it.
- `src/ui/tests/settings_tests.rs`: `window_moved_reaches_the_saved_snapshot` attaches a
  `MemorySettingsStore`, sends `Message::WindowMoved(Point::new(300.0, 200.0))`, and sees one
  snapshot with `window_position() == Some((300.0, 200.0))`. A repeat of the same point saves
  nothing new. `saved_window_position_is_restored_on_boot` shows that `adopt_saved_settings` sets
  `player.window_position` from the snapshot and back to `None` from `Settings::default()`.
- A listener test shows that `window_moved_message` maps a `Moved(point)` window event to
  `Message::WindowMoved(point)` and returns `None` for `window::Event::Focused` and a key press.
- A test of `launch_position` shows `Some((10.0, 20.0))` gives `Position::Specific` at that point
  (checked with `matches!`, since `Position` has no `PartialEq`) and `None` gives
  `Position::Default`.
- `docs/usage.md`'s settings sentence names the window's screen position among the saved values,
  says it is not restored on Wayland, and says deleting the `window_position` line resets an
  off-screen window. The "There are no CLI flags yet" sentence stays. `docs/invariants.md`'s
  `## Settings persistence` section names the position in its Guarantee and its malformed-line
  fallback. It changes the "size and position are not persisted" sentences there to say only
  the size is not, and its Pinned-by list names the new tests.
- `make check` passes.

### Show the current track's content rating (Explicit or Clean) in the File info panel (planned 2026-10-28 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-28 by the feature role

**Goal.** Apple Music marks each song `explicit` or `clean` in `attributes.contentRating`.
`library-songs` resources carry this attribute, and the Apple Music apps show it as the "E" badge.
Nostalgia drops it. The File info panel (Alt+3) already lists the tag-like
fields Winamp's ID3 panel shows (title through composer). Add one more line, `Rating: Explicit` or
`Rating: Clean`, so the panel names what the library knows about the track. Leave the line out
when the source supplied no rating.

**Approach.** Follow the path the `Composer:` line took (see `docs/invariants.md`, the File info
section), one field end to end:
1. **Model (`src/library.rs`).** Add `pub enum ContentRating { Explicit, Clean }` deriving
   `Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize` with
   `#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]`. Give it `pub fn label(self) -> &'static str`, which returns
   `"Explicit"` or `"Clean"`. Add `Song::content_rating: Option<ContentRating>` with
   `#[serde(default)]`, after `composer`, with a doc comment in the style of the `composer` field's.
2. **Wire (`src/apple_music/rest/wire.rs`).** Add `#[serde(rename = "contentRating")]
   content_rating: Option<String>` to `Attributes`, beside `composer_name`.
3. **Mapping (`src/apple_music/rest/wire/mapping.rs`).** In `Resource::into_song`, destructure the
   new attribute (extend the tuple and its `None` arm). Map it through a new private
   `fn content_rating(raw: Option<String>) -> Option<ContentRating>`. That function trims the value,
   then matches `explicit` → `Explicit` and `clean` → `Clean` ignoring ASCII case
   (`eq_ignore_ascii_case`). Anything else, including absent, blank, or an unknown value, maps to
   `None`. Add "content rating" to `into_song`'s doc list of fields that fall back to their "source
   supplied none" sentinel.
4. **Known track.** Add `pub content_rating: Option<ContentRating>` to `KnownTrack`
   (`src/ui/views/now_playing/text.rs`), documented like `disc_number`. In
   `src/ui/handlers/playback.rs`, the `known_tracks.insert` in the track-selection handler copies it
   from `song.content_rating`.
5. **Panel (`src/ui/views/file_info.rs`).** Add `const CONTENT_RATING_LABEL: &str = "Rating: ";`.
   In `view_file_info_overlay`, push `Rating: <label>` after the composer line and before
   `Length:`, only while `track.content_rating` is `Some`. Update the module doc and the function
   doc's list of lines.
6. **Literals.** Every `Song { … }` and `KnownTrack { … }` struct literal gains
   `content_rating: None`. The `composer: ` literals show where they are: `src/sample_library.rs`,
   `src/test_support/fixtures.rs`, `src/apple_music/tests/mod.rs`,
   `src/apple_music/rest/tests/library.rs`, `src/ui/tests/mod.rs`, `src/ui/views/tests/mod.rs`, and
   `src/ui/views/tests/chrome.rs` (`sample_known_track`). Literals that end in `..` need nothing.
   The sample library keeps `None` on every song, because its songs are invented and have no rating.

**Files touched.** `src/library.rs`, `src/apple_music/rest/wire.rs`,
`src/apple_music/rest/wire/mapping.rs`, `src/ui/views/now_playing/text.rs`,
`src/ui/handlers/playback.rs`, `src/ui/views/file_info.rs`, the test files and fixtures listed in
step 6, `src/ui/tests/readouts_tests.rs`, `docs/usage.md`, `docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `src/apple_music/rest/tests/library.rs`: `songs_from_album_maps_the_content_rating` checks that
  `"explicit"`, `"clean"` and `" Explicit "` map to `Some(Explicit)`, `Some(Clean)` and
  `Some(Explicit)`. `songs_from_album_maps_a_missing_blank_or_unknown_content_rating_to_none`
  covers an absent key, `null`, `""`, `"   "` and `"notExplicit"`. Both go through the existing
  `song_from_attributes` helper.
- `src/library.rs` tests: `song_round_trips_its_content_rating` checks that `Some(Explicit)`
  serializes as `"explicit"` and round-trips. `song_content_rating_defaults_to_none_when_the_payload_omits_it`
  covers the omitted field. The existing every-field-required and unknown-field tests pass.
- `src/ui/tests/readouts_tests.rs`: `known_tracks_record_the_played_songs_content_rating`, in the
  style of `known_tracks_record_the_played_songs_composer`.
- `src/ui/views/tests/chrome.rs`: `file_info_overlay_draws_the_tracks_content_rating` checks that
  `Rating: Explicit` sits after `Composer: …` and before `Length: …`.
  `file_info_overlay_omits_the_content_rating_line_when_the_source_supplied_none` uses
  `assert_no_file_info_line(&texts, "Rating:")`.
- `docs/usage.md`'s Alt+3 sentence names the content rating among the panel's lines and among the
  lines left out when the source supplies none. The File info section of `docs/invariants.md`
  describes the `Rating: …` line and its `contentRating` mapping, and its Pinned-by list names the

### Open the Jump to time box holding the current position, selected, like Winamp (planned 2026-10-28 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-28 by the feature role

**Goal.** Winamp's Jump to time dialog opens with its box already holding the playing track's
current position, so you can see where you are and type over it. Nostalgia's Ctrl+J panel opens
with an empty box (`handlers::jump::toggle_jump_time` calls `player.jump_time_query.clear()`).
Opening should instead fill the box with the current position in the `M:SS` form that
`parse_jump_time` already accepts, and select all of it, so typing replaces it and Enter on the
untouched text seeks to where playback already is.

**Approach.**
- `src/ui/views/mod.rs`: make `format_minutes_seconds` `pub(in crate::ui)`, so the handler can
  reuse it. Keep its doc comment and add the Jump to time prefill to the list of its users. Do not
  use `format_track_time`, because it turns `0` into `--:--`, which `parse_jump_time` rejects.
- `src/ui/handlers/jump.rs` `toggle_jump_time`: replace `player.jump_time_query.clear()` with:
  set `jump_time_query` to `views::format_minutes_seconds(ms)` when `player.playback_position` is
  `Some(position)`, where `ms` is `u64::try_from(position.as_millis()).unwrap_or(u64::MAX)` (the
  same conversion `view_jump_time_overlay` uses for the length). When it is `None`, clear the query.
  Leave the position unclamped: `jump_time_submitted` already clamps to `playback_duration`.
  Replace the `focus` task with
  `Task::batch([iced::widget::operation::focus(views::JUMP_TIME_INPUT_ID), iced::widget::operation::select_all(views::JUMP_TIME_INPUT_ID)])`
  (`select_all` is in iced_runtime 0.14's `widget::operation`, next to `focus`). Keep the
  existing shaded branch, which batches `toggle_window_shade` before the focus task. Update the
  doc comment: opening now fills the query with the position, or clears it when there is none,
  where it used to just clear the query. The Options menu's `Jump to time` row calls this same
  function, so it gets the prefill with no change of its own.
- `src/ui/tests/jump_time_tests.rs`:
  - Keep `toggle_opens_with_an_empty_query_and_closes_again` for the `None` position.
    `player_with_duration` sets no position, so it must still see an empty query after a stale one.
  - Add `toggle_opens_holding_the_current_position`. With `playback_position = Some(95 s)`, opening
    leaves `jump_time_query == "1:35"` and schedules work.
  - Add `toggle_opens_holding_zero_at_the_start`. `Some(Duration::ZERO)` gives `"0:00"`, not `--:--`.
  - Add `submitting_the_prefilled_query_seeks_to_the_current_position`. Open at `Some(12 s)` with
    the existing 30 s duration, send `JumpTimeSubmitted` without typing, and assert three things,
    the way `submit_seeks_records_the_position_and_closes` does: `playback_position` is still
    `Some(12 s)`, `position_epoch` went up by one (so a seek really ran), and the panel is closed.
- `docs/usage.md`: in the Ctrl+J sentence, say the box opens holding the current position (`1:35`),
  selected so typing replaces it, or empty when no position is known.
- `docs/invariants.md` `## Jump to time panel`: change "Opening clears the query" to "Opening
  sets the query to `format_minutes_seconds` of `playback_position`, or clears it when that is
  `None`, and focuses and selects the box". Add the new tests to **Pinned by**.

**Files touched.** `src/ui/handlers/jump.rs`, `src/ui/views/mod.rs`,
`src/ui/tests/jump_time_tests.rs`, `docs/usage.md`, `docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With a known preview length and a playback position of 95 s, Ctrl+J (or the Options menu's
  `Jump to time` row) opens the panel with `1:35` in the box. A position of 0 shows `0:00`.
- With no known position, the box opens empty, as it does today.
- Opening focuses the box and selects its text, so a typed time replaces the prefill.
- Enter on the untouched prefill seeks to the current position and closes the panel.
- Closing, the other panels' mutual closing, and the shaded restore behave as before. The existing
  tests in `jump_time_tests.rs` pass unchanged.
- `docs/usage.md` and `docs/invariants.md` describe the prefill.
- `make check` passes.

### Show the current track's disc number in the File info panel, like Winamp's ID3 panel (planned 2026-10-28 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-28 by the feature role

**Goal.** Winamp's File info dialog lists a track's position in a multi-disc set beside its track
number. Nostalgia's File info panel shows the title, artist, album, year, genre, track number,
composer, length, and loaded preview format. `Song` carries no disc number even though Apple
Music reports one as `attributes.discNumber`. This change carries that attribute through `Song`
and the `KnownTrack` cache. The panel then draws a `Disc #: <n>` line between `Track #:` and
`Composer:` while the source supplies a positive number. It adds no new state, handlers,
settings, or playback behavior, and it leaves search and sorting alone. It mirrors the finished
"Show the current track's composer in the File info panel" and "Show the current track's track
number in the File info panel" plans in PLANS-DONE.md. It does not depend on the Recently Played
series. Both edit `src/apple_music/rest/wire/mapping.rs`, but this plan touches only
`Resource::into_song` (plus a new private helper) there, and Recently Played 1/2 adds
`Resource::is_song` beside `Resource::is_library_album`.

**Approach.**

- `src/library.rs`: add `#[serde(default)] pub disc_number: Option<u32>` to `Song`, after
  `track_number`. Its doc comment follows `Self::track_number`'s: the track's 1-based disc in its
  album's set; `None` when the source supplied none or reported a non-positive number; the File
  info panel draws a `Disc #:` line only while it is `Some`. In the test module:
  - add the `"disc_number": null` key to `song_payload`;

  Option<serde_json::Number>` to the private `Attributes`, after `track_number`. Its doc comment
  matches `track_number`'s (parsed as a JSON number so an out-of-`u32` value maps to `None`
  instead of failing the whole response).
- `src/apple_music/rest/wire/mapping.rs`: move the `track_number` chain in `Resource::into_song`
  (`as_u64`, `> 0`, `u32::try_from`) into a private
  `fn positive_position(number: Option<serde_json::Number>) -> Option<u32>` beside
  `primary_genre`, carrying the existing comment as its doc comment. Map both
  `track_number` and `disc_number` through it. Carry `disc_number` through the attributes
  destructure (add one more `None` to the fallback tuple). Name the disc number in
  `into_song`'s doc comment among the fields it falls back for.
- `src/sample_library.rs`: give Opening, Middle, and Ending (First Record) `disc_number:
  Some(1)`, and give B-side and Headliner `None`. Signed out, the panel then shows both the line

  order.
- `src/ui/views/now_playing/text.rs`: add `pub disc_number: Option<u32>` to `KnownTrack`, after
  `track_number`. Its doc comment says it is copied from `Song::disc_number`, and that `None`

- `src/ui/views/file_info.rs`: add `const DISC_NUMBER_LABEL: &str = "Disc #: ";` between
  `TRACK_NUMBER_LABEL` and `COMPOSER_LABEL`. In `view_file_info_overlay`, push a
  `Disc #: <n>` line after the conditional track-number line and before the conditional composer
  line, only while `track.disc_number` is `Some`. Name the disc number in the module and
  `view_file_info_overlay` doc comments.
- Tests:
  - In `src/apple_music/rest/tests/library.rs`, use the existing `song_from_attributes` helper.
    `songs_from_album_maps_the_disc_number` checks that `"discNumber":2` maps to `Some(2)`.

  - In `src/ui/tests/readouts_tests.rs`, add `known_tracks_record_the_played_songs_disc_number`,

    `file_info_overlay_omits_the_disc_number_line_when_the_source_supplied_none`, modelled on the

### Show the current track's composer in the File info panel, like Winamp's ID3 panel (planned 2026-10-28 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-28 by the feature role

**Goal.** Winamp's File info dialog lists a track's composer beside its year, genre, and track
number. Nostalgia's File info panel shows the title, artist, album, year, genre, track number,
length, and loaded preview format. `Song` carries no composer even though Apple Music reports one
as `attributes.composerName`. This change carries that attribute through `Song` and the
`KnownTrack` cache. The panel then draws a `Composer: <name>` line between `Track #:` and
`Length:` while the source supplies one. It adds no new state, handlers, settings, or playback
behavior, and it leaves search matching alone. It mirrors the finished "Show the current track's
track number in the File info panel" plan in PLANS-DONE.md. It does not depend on the Recently
Played series. The two share a few files (`src/apple_music/rest/wire/mapping.rs`,
`src/ui/handlers/playback.rs`, and test files), but this plan edits only `Resource::into_song`
and the recorded `KnownTrack` literal in them.

**Approach.**

- `src/library.rs`: add `#[serde(default)] pub composer: String` to `Song`, after
  `track_number`. Its doc comment says `""` means the source supplied none (the sentinel
  `Self::album` uses) and that the File info panel draws a `Composer:` line only when it is
  non-empty. In the test module:
  - add the `"composer": ""` key to `song_payload`;
  - add `song_round_trips_its_composer` and
    `song_composer_defaults_to_empty_when_the_payload_omits_it` (built from

  Option<String>` to the private `Attributes`. Its doc comment says absence means the API omitted
  it.
- `src/apple_music/rest/wire/mapping.rs`: in `Resource::into_song`, carry `composer_name`
  through the attributes destructure (add one more `None` to the fallback tuple). Map it the way
  `album` is mapped: `composer_name.filter(|name| !name.trim().is_empty()).unwrap_or_default()`.
  An absent or whitespace-only name becomes `""`, and any other name is kept exactly as carried.
  Name the composer in `into_song`'s doc comment among the fields it moves into the model.
- `src/sample_library.rs`: give Opening, Middle, and Ending (First Record) the composer
  `"Sam Ample"`, and give B-side and Headliner `""`. Signed out, the panel then shows both the
  line and its omission. Add `songs_carry_the_documented_composers` beside
  `songs_carry_the_documented_track_numbers`, pinning every song's id and composer in library
  order.

  says it is copied from `Song::composer`, and that `""` means the source supplied none and the

  records `track_number: song.track_number` also records `composer: song.composer.clone()`.
- `src/ui/views/file_info.rs`: add `const COMPOSER_LABEL: &str = "Composer: ";` beside

    `"composerName":"Jane Doe"` maps to `"Jane Doe"`.

### Read the user's recently played songs through the service seam (Recently Played, part 1/2: planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** Winamp's playlist is the songs you have been listening to, and Apple Music keeps that
history server-side, but Nostalgia cannot read it. This part adds the data path,
`AppleMusicService::get_recently_played_songs`, over Apple's
`GET /v1/me/recent/played/tracks` with a sample-library fallback. A later part 2/2 (not yet
planned; it would show the list as a flat song view beside `All Songs`) depends on it. This part
changes nothing the player shows, so `docs/usage.md` is untouched. It touches none of the UI
files that "Show a Recently Added list on the Artists view" edits, so the two can run side by side.

**Approach.**
- `src/apple_music/rest/wire/mapping.rs`: beside `Resource::is_library_album`, add
  `Resource::is_song(&self) -> bool`, true when `kind` is `Some("songs")` or
  `Some("library-songs")`. Its doc comment says these are the two types
  `RestLibrary::get_recently_played_songs` maps. A catalog `songs` resource carries the same
  attributes `Resource::into_song` reads (`name`, `artistName`, `albumName`, `durationInMillis`,
  `previews`, …), so no mapping change is needed.
- `src/apple_music/rest.rs`: after `get_recently_added_albums`, add
  `RestLibrary::get_recently_played_songs(&self, session) -> Result<Vec<Song>, AppleMusicError>`.
  It requests `{API_BASE}/me/recent/played/tracks` with no query string, the same way
  `get_recently_added_albums` sends no `limit`, and follows `next` through `self.fetch`. It maps
  each resource where `is_song()` holds with `into_song("")`, the empty album id that
  `get_all_songs` also gives, and drops every other resource, such as `music-videos` or an
  untyped one. As in `get_recently_added_albums`, use `Ok(None)` and then `flatten`. Keep
  Apple's order, which is most recent first. The doc comment follows `get_recently_added_albums`.
- `src/apple_music/sample.rs`: add `pub(super) fn sample_recently_played_songs() -> Vec<Song>`
  returning `sample_all_songs()` reversed. Its doc comment says the sample library keeps no play
  history, so this stands in, just as `sample_recently_added_albums` does.
- `src/apple_music/browse.rs`: after `get_recently_added_albums`, add
  `pub async fn get_recently_played_songs(&self) -> Result<Vec<Song>, AppleMusicError>` through
  `self.browse(|rest, session| rest.get_recently_played_songs(session),
  sample_recently_played_songs)`. Import the new sample function where the other `sample_*`
  imports sit. Its doc comment follows `get_all_songs`'s, including the `# Errors` section.

**Tests.**
- New file `src/apple_music/rest/tests/recently_played.rs`, registered in
  `src/apple_music/rest/tests/mod.rs` next to `mod recently_added;` and modelled on
  `recently_added.rs` (`library_over`, `StubTransport`, `assert_single_call`, `assert_ids`).
  Its `URL` constant is `https://api.music.apple.com/v1/me/recent/played/tracks`.
  - `get_recently_played_songs_keeps_catalog_and_library_songs`: a body with one `songs`, one
    `library-songs`, and one `music-videos` resource maps the two songs in order, with full
    `Song` equality on the catalog one (title, artist, album, and its `previews[0].url` as
    `preview_url`, using `PREVIEW_URL` from `test_support`, and an empty `album_id`). It also
    asserts a single call to `URL`.
  - `get_recently_played_songs_drops_a_resource_without_a_type`: an untyped resource gives an
    empty list.
  - `get_recently_played_songs_keeps_apples_order_and_follows_a_next_page`: two pages, the first
    ending in `"next":"/v1/me/recent/played/tracks?offset=10"`. Assert the ids in order and that
    the second call's URL is the absolute next URL, the same way the recently-added paging test
    asserts it.
- `src/apple_music/tests/browse_rest.rs`:
  `get_recently_played_songs_uses_the_rest_library_when_signed_in` uses `signed_in_service` and
  `assert_call_urls` to show one call to the tracks URL and the mapped song.
- `src/apple_music/tests/browse_sample.rs`:
  `get_recently_played_songs_returns_the_sample_songs_reversed` compares against
  `get_all_songs()` reversed, the same way the Recently Added sample test does.

**Files touched.** `src/apple_music/rest.rs`, `src/apple_music/rest/wire/mapping.rs`,
`src/apple_music/sample.rs`, `src/apple_music/browse.rs`, new
`src/apple_music/rest/tests/recently_played.rs`, `src/apple_music/rest/tests/mod.rs`,
`src/apple_music/tests/browse_rest.rs`, `src/apple_music/tests/browse_sample.rs`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- When signed in, `AppleMusicService::get_recently_played_songs` issues
  `GET https://api.music.apple.com/v1/me/recent/played/tracks` (plus any `next` pages). It returns
  the `songs` and `library-songs` resources as `Song`s in Apple's order and drops every other
  resource type and untyped resources.
- When signed out, it returns the sample library's songs in reverse library order, and it never
  fails.
- No UI, `docs/usage.md`, or `docs/invariants.md` change. The tests above pass under
  `make check`.

### Read the library's recently added albums through the service seam (Recently Added, part 1/2: planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** Apple Music's own app opens on a Recently Added shelf, but Nostalgia has no way to
read it: `AppleMusicService` offers artists, all albums, all songs, playlists, and search only.
This part adds the data path, `AppleMusicService::get_recently_added_albums`, over Apple's
`GET /v1/me/library/recently-added` with a sample-library fallback, so part 2/2 ("Show a Recently
Added list on the Artists view") can show it. No UI changes here.

**Approach.**
- `src/apple_music/rest/wire.rs`: give `Resource` an optional resource type,
  `#[serde(rename = "type")] kind: Option<String>`, documented as Apple's resource type
  (`library-albums`, `library-playlists`, …). Update every `let Resource { id, attributes } = self;`
