### Flash the balance or equalizer level on the LCD after a wheel roll over its slider (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** A drag on the balance, preamp, or an equalizer band slider shows its level
(`Balance: 31% Left`, `Preamp: -12 DB`, `EQ: 60HZ +3 DB`) in the LCD title's place, and since the
volume-flash plan a volume key or wheel nudge shows `Volume: N%` for about a second. A wheel roll
over the balance, preamp, or a band slider changes that level silently, and also cancels a volume
flash that is showing. That leaves the player inconsistent: the only way to read the new level is
to drag. After such a roll, show that slider's own drag readout for the same four
`MARQUEE_TICK`s, through the volume flash's existing timer. The slider-wheel handlers left
`mixer_drag` unset only because nothing would clear it without a release (see PLANS-DONE.md, "Point
the mouse wheel at the balance and equalizer sliders"). The timed flash removes that problem. This
plan touches none of the files the waiting Shuffle-round-stop plan touches, so either can merge
first.

**Approach.**

- `src/ui/player.rs`: rename `VOLUME_FLASH_TICKS` to `MIXER_FLASH_TICKS` and the field
  `volume_flash_ticks` to `mixer_flash_ticks`, updating their doc comments to say "a key or wheel
  nudge of a mixer level". Add `pub(in crate::ui) mixer_flash: views::MixerDrag`, initialized to
  `views::MixerDrag::Volume` beside it. Its doc comment should say it names the slider whose
  readout the flash shows, means nothing while `mixer_flash_ticks` is 0, and is never saved.
  `needs_lcd_tick` reads the renamed field; update its doc comment ("a mixer flash").
- `src/ui/handlers/mixer.rs`: add a private helper
  `fn flash(player: &mut WinampPlayer, slider: views::MixerDrag)`. It sets `mixer_flash = slider`
  and `mixer_flash_ticks = MIXER_FLASH_TICKS`. `volume_up` and `volume_down` call
  `flash(player, MixerDrag::Volume)` where they set the ticks today. `balance_wheel`,
  `eq_preamp_wheel`, and `eq_band_wheel` replace their `volume_flash_ticks = 0` lines with
  `flash(player, MixerDrag::Balance)`, `flash(player, MixerDrag::EqPreamp)`, and
  `flash(player, MixerDrag::EqBand(band))`. Each call stays after the zero/NaN/out-of-range early
  return, so a no-op roll still flashes nothing. Update those three handlers' doc comments: they
  still leave `mixer_drag` alone, and they flash the readout instead. As today, `mixer_released`
  must not touch the flash.
- `src/ui/handlers/playback.rs` `marquee_tick`: use the renamed field. Its behavior is unchanged.
- `src/ui/view/player_panels.rs`: the last `or_else` of the readout chain passes
  `player.mixer_flash` to `views::mixer_readout_text` instead of `views::MixerDrag::Volume`, still
  only while `mixer_flash_ticks > 0`. A drag readout and a seek readout still take precedence.

### Stop at the end of a Shuffle round when Repeat is off, like Winamp (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** In Winamp, Shuffle with Repeat off plays the list once in shuffled order and then stops,
just as an unshuffled list stops after its last song. Today a natural preview end with Shuffle on
always moves on to another song. The Shuffle-rounds plan (see PLANS-DONE.md, "Let Shuffle play
every song once before repeating any") deliberately left this behavior unchanged:
`ShuffleRound::record` (src/ui/transport/round.rs) clears the round once every song has played,
and `ShuffleRound::pick` falls back to `transport::shuffled_track_id`. As a result,
`handlers::playback::preview::playback_finished` never sees a round end. After this change, a
natural end on the song that completed the round, with Shuffle on and Repeat off, takes the
existing `stop` path and keeps that song current for Play, the same way Repeat off stops on an
unshuffled list's last song. Next, the Next button, and Repeat on keep starting a new round as
they do now; only the preview-end advance stops.

**Approach.**
- `src/ui/transport/round.rs`: add a field `completed_by: Option<String>` to `ShuffleRound`; the
  derived `Default` gives `None`. In `record`, set it to `Some(track_id.to_owned())` in the branch
  that clears `played` (this play completed the round). Otherwise set it to `None`, so any later
  committed play clears it. That includes Play restarting the same song, which then counts as the
  first play of the new round. Add
  `#[must_use] pub fn ends_round(&self, current: Option<&str>) -> bool`, which returns true when
  `current` is `Some` and equals `completed_by`. Its doc comment says that the round is the list
  that was showing when that song's play was recorded. Leave `pick` unchanged, along with the
  existing eager clear and restart.
- `src/ui/handlers/playback/preview.rs` `playback_finished`: under the same lock, after the
  `stop_after_current` check and before `forward_track_id`, add a check: if `state.shuffle &&
  !state.repeat && player.shuffle_round.ends_round(state.current_track.as_deref())`, drop the
  state lock and `return stop(player)`, in the same way as the `stop_after_current` branch. Extend
  the function's doc comment to cover this. Leave `stepping::forward_track_id` and `step_track`
  untouched, so Next still starts a new round.

**Files touched.** `src/ui/transport/round.rs` (with its in-file tests),
`src/ui/handlers/playback/preview.rs`, `src/ui/tests/stepping_tests.rs`, `docs/usage.md`,
`docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Unit tests in `round.rs` over `stepping_songs()`:
  - `the_play_completing_a_round_ends_it`: after recording song-1, song-2, and song-3,
    `ends_round(Some("song-3"))` is true, and `ends_round(Some("song-1"))` and
    `ends_round(None)` are false.
  - `a_later_play_clears_the_round_end`: recording song-3 again after that makes
    `ends_round(Some("song-3"))` false. Before the round completes (only song-1 and song-2
    recorded), `ends_round(Some("song-2"))` is false.
- UI tests in `src/ui/tests/stepping_tests.rs`, next to the Shuffle preview-end tests, using
  `player_playing_stepping_song`, `record_a_play`, and `drive_playback_finished` as
  `preview_end_with_shuffle_on_a_single_song_stops` does:
  - `preview_end_with_shuffle_on_and_repeat_off_stops_after_the_round`: song-3 is playing with
    Shuffle on and Repeat off, and song-1, song-2, and song-3 have been recorded. The finished
    reply takes the Stop path (`Message::TransportSettled`, and `recording.calls()` is
    `[AudioCall::Stop]`), `is_playing` is false, and `current_track` stays `song-3`.
  - `preview_end_with_shuffle_and_repeat_on_starts_a_new_round`: the same setup with Repeat on
    advances instead of stopping. The landing is random, so check that `drive_playback_finished`
    returns `Message::TrackSelected` with `index` 0 or 1 (song-1 or song-2), not the Stop path.
  - `next_with_shuffle_after_a_completed_round_keeps_playing`: with the same recorded plays and
    Repeat off, `Message::NextTrack` selects a song other than song-3, with no Stop.
- The existing Shuffle tests in `round.rs` and `stepping_tests.rs` pass unchanged, including
  `preview_end_with_shuffle_on_picks_the_other_song`,
  `preview_end_with_shuffle_on_plays_the_unplayed_song`, and
  `preview_end_with_shuffle_on_a_single_song_stops`.
- `docs/usage.md`, in the preview-end advance paragraph: "or, with Shuffle on, to a shuffled song
  when another exists" now says that with Shuffle on and Repeat off it stops once every song of
  the round has played, like Winamp, keeping that song queued for Play, and that Repeat on starts
  a new round. In `docs/invariants.md` `## Shuffle rounds`, add the stop to the guarantee, name
  `ShuffleRound::ends_round` and `playback_finished` under Enforced by, and list the new tests
  under Pinned by. `make check` passes.

### Flash the volume on the LCD after a key or wheel nudge, like Winamp (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** Winamp's title display briefly reads `VOLUME: 72%` when the volume changes from the
keyboard or the mouse wheel. Today only a volume *drag* swaps the LCD title for the level, through
`player.mixer_drag` and `views::mixer_readout_text`. A nudge (`handlers::mixer::volume_up` /
`volume_down`, reached from the Up/Down arrows, keypad 8/2, and `volume_wheel`) changes the level
and leaves the title alone. After a nudge, show the drag's own `Volume: N%` text in the title's
place for about one second (four `MARQUEE_TICK`s of 250 ms), then bring the title back. The
waiting Shuffle-rounds plan touches none of these files, so either can merge first.

**Approach.**

- `src/ui/player.rs`: add `pub(in crate::ui) volume_flash_ticks: u8` (initialized to 0 beside
  `mixer_drag`) with a doc comment. It holds the number of LCD ticks the nudge readout has left and
  is never saved. Add `pub(in crate::ui) const VOLUME_FLASH_TICKS: u8 = 4;` with a doc comment
  saying it is one second at `MARQUEE_TICK`. Add `needs_lcd_tick(&self) -> bool`, which returns
  `self.volume_flash_ticks > 0 || self.needs_marquee()`. Leave `needs_marquee` unchanged.
- `src/ui/mod.rs`: pass `player.needs_lcd_tick()` as `subscriptions`' first argument instead of
  `player.needs_marquee()`. Then the existing marquee timer also runs while a flash is counting
  down, and no new thread or subscription module is needed. Update the `subscriptions` doc
  comment in `src/ui/subscriptions/mod.rs` to say the timer also runs while a volume flash shows.
- `src/ui/handlers/mixer.rs`: `volume_up` and `volume_down` set
  `player.volume_flash_ticks = VOLUME_FLASH_TICKS` before `mutate_volume`, so `volume_wheel`
  inherits it, and its zero/NaN no-op path still sets nothing. `balance_wheel`, `eq_preamp_wheel`
  and `eq_band_wheel` set it to 0 on their non-no-op paths, so a balance or gain roll never shows a
  stale volume. `mixer_released` must **not** touch it: `mixer_key_message`
  (`src/ui/subscriptions/listeners.rs`) turns the same Up/Down key press into
  `Message::MixerReleased`, and clearing the flash there would cancel it immediately.
- `src/ui/handlers/playback.rs` `marquee_tick`: while `volume_flash_ticks > 0`, decrement it and
  leave `marquee_offset` alone, so the title resumes where it paused (as it does after a drag
  readout). Otherwise advance the offset as today.
- `src/ui/view/player_panels.rs`: in the readout chain passed to `views::view_now_playing`, after
  the `mixer_drag` readout and the `seek_preview` readout, add one more `or_else`. It shows
  `views::mixer_readout_text(views::MixerDrag::Volume, volume, balance, eq_preamp, &eq_bands)`
  while `player.volume_flash_ticks > 0`. A drag or a seek drag therefore takes precedence.

**Files touched.** `src/ui/player.rs`, `src/ui/mod.rs`, `src/ui/subscriptions/mod.rs` (doc
only), `src/ui/handlers/mixer.rs`, `src/ui/handlers/playback.rs`, `src/ui/view/player_panels.rs`.
New test file `src/ui/tests/volume_flash_tests.rs`, registered with `mod volume_flash_tests;` in
`src/ui/tests/mod.rs` (`mixer_tests.rs` is already over 1000 lines). Plus `docs/usage.md` and
`docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.** The tests live in `volume_flash_tests.rs` and are synchronous

- `Message::VolumeUp` (and separately `Message::VolumeDown`) with a seeded title `Tune` makes

  `a_key_or_wheel_event_ends_a_mixer_readout`, and the volume-wheel tests pass unchanged.

### Let Shuffle play every song once before repeating any, like Winamp (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** Winamp's Shuffle plays the playlist in a shuffled order, so every song plays once
before any song plays again. Today a shuffled forward step (`stepping::forward_track_id`, used by
Next in `step_track` and by the preview-end advance in `handlers/playback/preview.rs`) calls
`transport::shuffled_track_id`, which picks any song except the current one. In a three-song list
it can go song-1, song-2, song-1 and never reach song-3. Fix this by tracking a shuffle *round*:
a shuffled forward step picks only from the showing list's songs not yet played this round.
Once every song in the list has played, a new round starts.

**Approach.**
- Add `src/ui/transport/round.rs` with `pub struct ShuffleRound { played: HashSet<String> }`
  (`#[derive(Debug, Default)]`), declared beside `mod history;` in `src/ui/transport.rs` and
  re-exported like `PlayHistory`. It has two methods:
  - `record(&mut self, track_id: &str, songs: &[Song])` inserts `track_id`, then drops `played`
    ids that `songs` no longer contains (so the set stays bounded by the showing list). If every
    song in a non-empty `songs` is now in `played`, the round is complete: clear `played` and
    re-insert just `track_id`, so the new round starts with the song now playing.
  - `pick(&self, songs: &[Song], current: Option<&str>, roll: u64) -> Option<String>` (`#[must_use]`)
    takes candidates in list order: songs that are neither `current` nor in `played`. If any exist,
    return `candidates[roll % len]`. Otherwise fall back to
    `transport::shuffled_track_id(songs, current, roll)`, so behavior with no unplayed song left
    (for example a one-song list, or a list whose plays were never recorded) is unchanged.
- Add `pub(in crate::ui) shuffle_round: transport::ShuffleRound` to `WinampPlayer` in
  `src/ui/player.rs`, defaulted where `play_history` is.
- `handlers::playback::track_played` (src/ui/handlers/playback.rs): in the same committed branch
  that calls `player.play_history.record(current)`, also call `player.shuffle_round.record(current,
  items)`. Here `items` is the list the current view shows (`all_songs.items` for
  `CurrentView::AllSongs`, otherwise `songs.items`). Pick it through the disjoint fields as
  `step_track` does, not through `showing_songs(player)`, so that the mutable borrow of
  `shuffle_round` does not conflict. Record every committed play, whether or not Shuffle is on: a
  song played in order before Shuffle was switched on has still been heard this round. Failed and
  superseded completions record nothing, as for the history.
- `stepping::forward_track_id` gains a `round: &transport::ShuffleRound` parameter. Its shuffle
  branch calls `round.pick(items, current, transport::shuffle_roll())`. Update its doc comment and
  both callers (`step_track` passes `&player.shuffle_round`, and the preview-end advance in
  `preview.rs` does the same next to `showing_songs(player)`; both borrows are shared). The
  preview-end advance's existing same-song filter stays as it is.
- Out of scope: Shuffle's Previous (`PlayHistory`) is unchanged, and so is Shuffle with Repeat
  off, which still keeps going into a new round rather than stopping (the documented "a shuffled
  song when another exists").

**Files touched.** `src/ui/transport/round.rs` (new, with its in-file `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`
like `history.rs`), `src/ui/transport.rs`, `src/ui/player.rs`, `src/ui/handlers/playback.rs`,
`src/ui/handlers/playback/stepping.rs`, `src/ui/handlers/playback/preview.rs`,
`src/ui/tests/stepping_tests.rs`, `docs/usage.md`, `docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Unit tests in `round.rs` over `test_support::stepping_songs()` (song-1..song-3):
  - `pick_skips_songs_played_this_round`: after `record("song-1")` and `record("song-2")`,
    `pick(.., Some("song-2"), roll)` is `Some("song-3")` for every roll in `0..10`.
  - `a_completed_round_starts_over_from_the_current_song`: after recording all three songs ending
    with song-3, `pick(.., Some("song-3"), roll)` over `0..10` returns both song-1 and song-2 and
    never song-3.
  - `pick_falls_back_when_no_unplayed_song_remains`: a one-song list with that song recorded and
    current returns that song's id, matching `shuffled_track_id`.
  - `record_forgets_songs_the_list_no_longer_shows`: a song recorded from a different list does
    not keep a song of the current list from being picked, and does not count toward completing
    its round.
- UI test `next_with_shuffle_plays_the_unplayed_song` in `src/ui/tests/stepping_tests.rs`: build
  the player with `player_stepping_from(None)`, turn Shuffle on, and `record_a_play` song-1 then
  song-2. `Message::NextTrack` must then select index 2, checked with `assert_track_selected`.
- A preview-end test alongside the existing Shuffle preview-end tests in `stepping_tests.rs`. It
  records song-1 and song-2 as plays, then a finished reply while song-2 plays with Shuffle on.
  The advance must land on song-3 (index 2).
- `next_with_shuffle_never_reselects_the_current_track` and the existing Shuffle/Previous
  tests pass unchanged.
- docs/usage.md's Shuffle sentences (the preview-end advance paragraph and Next's description)
  say Shuffle plays each song of the showing list once before any repeats, like Winamp. A new
  `## Shuffle rounds` section in docs/invariants.md states the guarantee, names `ShuffleRound`
  and `track_played` as the enforcement, and lists the new tests. `make check` passes.

### Mark a song-list footer total that skips unknown lengths with `+`, like Winamp (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** Winamp's playlist editor adds a `+` after a time total when one or more of the
entries it covers has no known length (`3:30+`), so the total does not look exact when it
isn't. Today `song_list_summary` sums `duration_ms` and treats `0` ("the source supplied no
duration", per `Song::duration_ms`) as zero time without saying so. `[210_000, 0]` therefore
reads `2 songs - 3:30`, and a selected unknown-length row reads `0:00` as if it really were zero.

**Approach.** Make the change in `song_list_summary` (`src/ui/views/browse/rows/text.rs`) only.
It is a pure helper, and `views::browse::rows::song_list` already passes its result to the footer.
- Total: append `+` to `format_minutes_seconds(total_ms)` exactly when some song in `songs`
  has `duration_ms == 0` (`songs.iter().any(|song| song.duration_ms == 0)`). The song count
  is unchanged, so every entry still counts.
- Selected part: when the selected song's `duration_ms == 0`, it reads `0:00+` (Winamp's
  selection total is marked the same way for the same reason). A known selected length is
  unchanged.
- An empty list has no unknown entries and still reads `0 songs - 0:00`, so

### Separate the scrolling LCD title's repeats with `  ***  `, like Winamp (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** Winamp 2.x scrolls an overlong song title through a `  ***  ` separator (two spaces,
three asterisks, two spaces) before the title repeats. Nostalgia's Now Playing marquee repeats
through three blank spaces instead, so the wrap point is hard to see. Make the scrolling line read
`… - Opening  ***  1. The Sample …`. A line that fits the LCD is unchanged: it shows whole, with no
separator.

**Approach.**
- `src/ui/views/now_playing/text.rs`: replace `const MARQUEE_GAP: usize = 3` with
  `const MARQUEE_SEPARATOR: &str = "  ***  ";` and update its doc comment.
- `marquee_cycle_len` returns `display_len(..) + MARQUEE_SEPARATOR.chars().count()`. The
  title-drag wrap in `src/ui/handlers/playback/title_drag.rs` reads this function, so it follows
  the new cycle without its own change.

  (`let cycle: Vec<char> = text.chars().chain(MARQUEE_SEPARATOR.chars()).collect()`). Window
  `width` chars from `offset % cycle.len()`, wrapping by index. The `chars.len() <= width` early
  return stays, so a line that fits never shows the separator. Update the doc comments of
  `marquee_cycle_len` and `marquee_text` to name the separator instead of gap spaces.

### Press Play while a song plays to restart it from the start, like Winamp (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** In Winamp 2.x, pressing Play (or X) while a song is playing restarts that song from the
beginning. In Nostalgia, `Message::Play` while playing does nothing audible.
`AppleMusicService::resume` (`src/apple_music/playback.rs`) goes straight to `resume_locked`,
which calls `audio.resume()` on a player that is already running. Make Play while playing seek the
loaded preview back to zero. Play while paused still resumes from the paused position. Play while
stopped still restarts from the remembered URL. The media Play/Pause toggle is unchanged. Decision:
Winamp's Play-while-paused restart is out of scope; resuming a paused song is documented
behavior today, and the waiting Pause/Unpause plan builds on it.

**Approach.**
- `src/apple_music/playback.rs`, `AppleMusicService::resume`: after taking the transport lock,
  read `self.state.lock().await.is_playing` and drop that guard. When `transport.loaded` and
  playing are both true, call `self.seek_output_to(Duration::ZERO)?`. Then
  `println!("Restarted playback")` and return `Ok(())`, leaving the shared state alone (it stays
  playing). Otherwise call `self.resume_locked(&mut transport).await` as today. Leave
  `resume_locked` alone, since `toggle_play_pause` reaches it only when not playing. Update
  `resume`'s doc comment to describe the restart. Import `std::time::Duration`.
- Do the check in the service, not in the UI handler. `handlers::playback::play`
  (`src/ui/handlers/playback.rs`) cannot read `is_playing` with `blocking_lock`: the
  `#[tokio::test]` transport tests drive `update(…, Message::Play)` inside a runtime, where
  `blocking_lock` panics. Leave `play` unchanged except for its doc comment ("Play resumes (or
  restarts) the preview") — mention that it restarts a playing preview. Its
  `begin_position_transition` already holds the position poll until `TransportSettled`. The next
  once-per-second poll then shows the restarted position, so the readout catches up within about
  a second. Do not try to reset `playback_position` from the UI.
- This entry and the waiting "Press Pause again to resume a paused song" entry both edit
  `play_and_pause_set_the_playback_flag_explicitly` and the same usage.md transport sentence. Each
  edits a different half, so whichever merges second adapts its edit to the other's text.

**Files touched.** `src/apple_music/playback.rs`, `src/ui/handlers/playback.rs` (doc comment
only), `src/apple_music/tests/transport.rs`, `src/ui/tests/transport_tests.rs`, `docs/usage.md`,
`docs/invariants.md`.

**Tests.**
- `src/apple_music/tests/transport.rs`: add `resume_while_playing_restarts_the_preview_from_zero`,
  modeled on `resume_resumes_the_audio_backend`. Build `recording_service_with_preview` and call
  `service.resume()` once without pausing. Assert the recorded calls are exactly
  `[AudioCall::SeekTo(Duration::ZERO)]`, `assert_playback_state(&state, Some("song-1"), true)`, and
  `assert_transport_mode(&state, TransportMode::Playing)`.
- Same file: add `resume_while_playing_reports_a_seek_failure`. Use
  `service_with_preview_playing(Arc::clone(&audio) as …)` over `FailingAudio::failing_seek()`
  (see `assert_seek_failure_propagates` in `src/apple_music/tests/audio_forwarding.rs`). Assert
  that `resume()` returns the error "the audio device is gone",
  `audio.attempts(FailingCommand::Seek) == 1`, and the state is still playing `song-1`.
- `src/ui/tests/transport_tests.rs`, `play_and_pause_set_the_playback_flag_explicitly`: the
  "play again" step keeps `is_playing` true. Change its comment ("X plays even when already
  playing…") to say X restarts a playing song. In `transport_messages_drive_the_audio_backend`,
  add a Play-while-playing case over a fresh `RecordingAudio`. Drive `Message::Play` through
  `assert_transport_settled` without pausing first, and assert the recorded calls are
  `[AudioCall::SeekTo(Duration::ZERO)]`.
- The existing `resume_resumes_the_audio_backend`, `resume_after_stop_restarts_the_preview`, and
  `toggle_play_pause_*` tests pass unchanged. They pin that paused, stopped, and toggle paths
  did not move.

**Docs.**
- `docs/usage.md`: in the transport paragraph ("Play starts or resumes the loaded preview"), add
  that Play restarts it from its start while it is already playing, like Winamp. Do the same in
  the playback paragraph's "Play resumes a paused preview or restarts a stopped one from the
  beginning".
- `docs/invariants.md`: add a `## Play restart` section after `## Previous restart`. Guarantee:
  Play on a loaded, playing preview sends exactly one absolute seek to zero and leaves the
  current track and `Playing` mode unchanged. Paused and stopped Play keep their resume and replay
  paths, and a rejected seek is reported without changing state. Enforced by
  `AppleMusicService::resume`. Pinned by the two new service tests and the new
  `transport_messages_drive_the_audio_backend` case.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With a preview playing, `Message::Play` (Play button, X, keypad 5, media Play key) records one
  `SeekTo(Duration::ZERO)` and no `Resume` or `Play`, and the transport stays `Playing` on the
  same track.
- Play while paused still records `Resume`. Play after Stop still replays the remembered URL. The
  media Play/Pause toggle still pauses while playing.
- A backend that rejects the seek makes `resume` return its error after one attempt, with the

### Press Pause again to resume a paused song, like Winamp's Pause/Unpause (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** In Winamp 2.x the Pause button and the C key toggle the pause: pressing either while
paused unpauses and playback continues from where it stopped. Nostalgia's Pause does nothing on
a second press. `AppleMusicService::pause` (`src/apple_music/playback.rs`) always calls
`audio.pause()` and `AppState::pause` (`src/state.rs`), whose doc comment says it is "an
explicit, idempotent set, so a second press keeps the player paused rather than resuming".
`play_and_pause_set_the_playback_flag_explicitly` (`src/ui/tests/transport_tests.rs`) pins that
with its "pause again" step. Make Pause while paused resume the loaded preview. Pause while
playing still pauses, and Pause while stopped still leaves the transport stopped.

**Approach.**
- `src/apple_music/playback.rs`: in `AppleMusicService::pause`, take the transport lock as
  `let mut transport` and read `self.state.lock().await.paused` under it, dropping that state
  guard before going on. When `paused && transport.loaded`, return
  `self.resume_locked(&mut transport).await`. That calls `audio.resume()` and `AppState::play`,
  the same path `toggle_play_pause` takes while paused. Otherwise keep today's body unchanged:
  `audio.pause()`, then `state.pause()` when loaded or `state.stop()` when not. Doing the read and
  the call under the one transport lock means two Pause presses close together run one after
  the other, the way `concurrent_toggles_serialize_on_the_transport_lock` pins for the toggle.
  Update the method's doc comment to describe the unpause.
- `src/state.rs`: `AppState::pause` itself stays idempotent, because the service now chooses
  between pause and resume. Reword its doc comment so it no longer says a second press of the
  button or C key keeps the player paused. Say instead that the service resumes a paused preview
  before calling this.
- `src/ui/handlers/playback.rs`: reword the `pause` and `play_pause` doc comments. Pause now
  unpauses a paused preview, so it differs from the media Play/Pause toggle only in what it does
  while stopped (it does not start playback). No code change is needed here.
- `Message::Pause` is already sent by every Pause control: the transport row and shade strip `II`
  glyphs, the C key, and the media Pause key (`shortcuts::shortcut`). All of them get the
  unpause, which matches Winamp, whose Pause command toggles too. No new message or mapping is
  needed.

**Files touched.** `src/apple_music/playback.rs`, `src/state.rs`,
`src/ui/handlers/playback.rs`, `src/apple_music/tests/transport.rs`,
`src/ui/tests/transport_tests.rs`, `docs/usage.md`, `docs/invariants.md`.

**Tests.**
- `src/apple_music/tests/transport.rs`: add `pause_while_paused_resumes_the_preview`, modeled on
  `toggle_play_pause_resumes_while_paused`. Build `recording_service_with_preview` and call
  `service.pause()` twice. Assert that the recorded calls are exactly
  `[AudioCall::Pause, AudioCall::Resume]`, that `assert_playback_state(&state, Some("song-1"), true)`
  holds, and that `assert_transport_mode` gives `TransportMode::Playing`. Keep
  `pause_after_stop_leaves_the_transport_stopped` and
  `pause_without_a_loaded_preview_leaves_the_transport_stopped` passing unchanged; they pin that
  Pause never starts a stopped transport.
- `src/ui/tests/transport_tests.rs`: in `play_and_pause_set_the_playback_flag_explicitly`, change
  the "pause again" step's assertion so the second `Message::Pause` leaves `is_playing` true.
  Update the step's comment (today "C pauses even when already paused") to say C unpauses a
  paused song. Then add a third `Message::Pause` that pauses again, so the test pins the full
  pause → unpause → pause cycle.

**Docs.**
- `docs/usage.md`: in the transport paragraph ("Play starts or resumes the loaded preview and
  Pause pauses it"), say that Pause while paused resumes, like Winamp. In the keys paragraph,
  change "C pauses" to "C pauses, or resumes while paused".
- `docs/invariants.md`, `## Media keys`: the guarantee says the Pause mapping is the same
  explicit message the on-screen control sends. Add that `Message::Pause` resumes a paused
  preview, and pin it with `pause_while_paused_resumes_the_preview`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With a preview playing, `Message::Pause` pauses it (mode `Paused`). A second `Message::Pause`
  resumes it (mode `Playing`, backend records `Resume`). A third pauses it again.
- `Message::Pause` while stopped, or with no loaded preview, still leaves the transport `Stopped`.
  The existing tests for both cases pass unchanged.
- X (`Message::Play`) and the media Play/Pause toggle behave as before.
- The new and updated tests pass, docs/usage.md and docs/invariants.md describe the unpause, and
  `make check` passes.

### Let the LCD spectrum bars fall off gradually, like Winamp's analyzer falloff (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** In Winamp the analyzer bars jump up to a louder level right away but sink back down
over several frames ("analyzer falloff"). Their peak markers fall more slowly still. Ours behave
differently. `handlers::playback::preview::spectrum` (`src/ui/handlers/playback/preview.rs`)
stores each reply as-is (`player.spectrum = spectrum`), so a band that goes quiet drops to the
rail in one poll, about 250 ms. Only the peak markers (`next_spectrum_peaks`) hold and fall. Make
the bars fall too, faster than the markers.

**Approach.**
- `src/ui/views/now_playing/visualizer.rs`: add `const LCD_VISUALIZER_BAR_FALL: f32 = 0.25;`
  next to `LCD_VISUALIZER_PEAK_FALL`, with a doc comment: the most a bar may drop per spectrum
  reply, so a band falls from full to the rail in four polls (about one second at the four-a-second
  poll). Move the body of `next_spectrum_peaks` into a private
  `fn fall_toward(previous: Option<Spectrum>, spectrum: Option<Spectrum>, fall: f32) -> Option<Spectrum>`
  that applies the same rule with `fall` in place of the constant: missing `spectrum` → `None`;
  missing `previous` counts as zeros; each band is clamped `0.0..=1.0` with NaN as zero, then
  `level.max(held - fall).max(0.0)`. `next_spectrum_peaks` becomes `fall_toward(previous,
  spectrum, LCD_VISUALIZER_PEAK_FALL)`. Add `pub fn next_spectrum_bars(previous, spectrum)` =
  `fall_toward(previous, spectrum, LCD_VISUALIZER_BAR_FALL)`, documented like the peaks function.
  Re-export it beside `next_spectrum_peaks` wherever that is re-exported (`views` module, and the
  `use` list in `src/ui/views/tests/mod.rs`).
- `src/ui/handlers/playback/preview.rs` `spectrum`: inside the existing `reply_is_current`
  guard, keep computing the peaks from the raw reply, then set
  `player.spectrum = views::next_spectrum_bars(player.spectrum, spectrum)`. Update the doc
  comment: the reply advances the bars' falloff and the peaks' hold-and-fall. The peaks fall
  0.125 per reply and the bars 0.25, so a peak never ends up below its bar. Nothing else changes:
  Stop and a new selection still clear `spectrum` (`handlers/playback.rs`), Pause still freezes
  the bars because the poll is not subscribed while paused, and `visible_spectrum` still hides
  them.
- Tests:
  - In `src/ui/views/tests/now_playing.rs`, add
    `next_spectrum_bars_rise_at_once_and_fall_a_quarter_per_reply`. A band at 1.0 then a reply
    of 0.0 gives 0.75, then 0.5. A louder reply replaces the falling level immediately. NaN and
    out-of-range levels clamp. A `None` reply gives `None`. The bar falls further per reply than
    `next_spectrum_peaks` does from the same inputs.
  - In `src/ui/tests/readouts_tests.rs`, update `spectrum_reply_stores_the_loaded_previews_spectrum`.
    After the lower reply (band 2 goes 0.5 → 0.0), `player.spectrum.unwrap().bands[2]` is 0.25,
    not `lower`. The peak is still 0.375, and a `None` reply still clears both. Rename it
    `spectrum_reply_stores_the_bars_and_lets_a_quieter_band_fall`.
  - `spectrum_reply_with_a_stale_epoch_or_a_pending_transition_is_dropped` should pass
    unchanged. Its kept `recording_spectrum()` (band 2 = 0.5) falls to 0.25, which equals the
    stale value `[0.25; BAND_COUNT]` it then expects. Confirm this when you run it.
- `docs/usage.md`: in the LCD visualizer paragraph, after "A thin gray peak marker above each bar
  jumps up with the bar and then drops back slowly", say the bars also jump up at once but sink
  back over about a second when a band goes quiet, faster than their markers.
- `docs/invariants.md`, LCD visualizer bullet (the one naming `next_spectrum_peaks`): state that
  `WinampPlayer::spectrum` holds the drawn bars, advanced by `next_spectrum_bars` (the higher of
  the band and the previous bar less 0.25), inside the same reply guard. Pin it with the new test
  and the renamed readouts test. Note that the peaks fall slower (0.125), so a peak is never below
  its bar.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- While playing, a band that goes quiet drops 0.25 of the strip per spectrum reply instead of
  falling to the rail at once. A louder reply raises it immediately. The peak markers still hold
  and fall 0.125 per reply.
- Pause still freezes the bars, while Stop and a new selection still clear them. A stale reply or
  one that arrives during a transition is still dropped, and hiding the visualizer still hides
  the bars.
- The new and updated tests pass, docs/usage.md and docs/invariants.md describe the falloff, and
  `make check` passes.

### Match each typed word separately in Jump to File, like Winamp's Jump to file (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** Winamp's Jump to file matches a title when every space-separated word typed appears
somewhere in it, in any order, so `band two` finds `The Sample Band - Two`. Our Jump to File
panel compares the whole trimmed query as one substring, so the same query matches nothing: the
cached row title is `<artist> - <title>` (`library::display_title_for`), and typing the artist
then the title never matches across the ` - ` join. Make the filter match word by word.

**Approach.** Change only `views::jump_file::jump_file_matches` in `src/ui/views/jump_file.rs`:
lowercase the query, split it with `str::split_whitespace` into words, and keep an index when
its lowercased title `contains` every word (`Iterator::all`). An empty or all-whitespace query
yields no words, and `all` over no words is true, so it still matches every index; the explicit
`query.is_empty()` branch goes away. Lowercase each title once per call, as today. Order stays
list order. The view (`view_jump_file_overlay`) and the handlers in `src/ui/handlers/jump.rs`
(`move_jump_file_selection` and the submit path) already call this one function, so the drawn
rows, highlight, and the row Enter plays change together and need no edits. Update the function's
doc comment to say the query is split on whitespace and each word must appear in the title as a
case-insensitive substring, in any order. No new dependency, state, or message.

**Files touched.**
- `src/ui/views/jump_file.rs`: `jump_file_matches` body and doc comment.
- `src/ui/views/tests/jump_file.rs`: keep `matches_blank_all_case_insensitive_trimmed_in_order`
  as is (every assertion there holds under word matching) and add
  `matches_every_whitespace_separated_word_in_any_order`, over titles such as
  `"The Sample Band - One"`, `"The Sample Band - Two"`, `"Other Act - Two Step"`: `"band two"`
  gives `[1]`; `"two band"` gives `[1]` (any order); `"TWO"` gives `[1, 2]`; `"two  step"`
  (double space, and with a tab) gives `[2]`; `"band zzz"` gives `[]` (every word must match);
  `"- two"` gives `[1, 2]` (a punctuation word is still a plain substring).
- `src/ui/tests/jump_file_tests.rs`: add `submit_matches_the_artist_and_title_words_together`,
  using the existing `player_in_songs` and `submit` helpers over `stepping_songs` (artist
  `The Sample Band`, titles `One`, `Two`, …): open the panel, `submit(&mut player, "band two")`,
  and `assert_track_selected(task, epoch, 1)` with the panel closed, the same shape as
  `submit_plays_the_first_match_and_closes`. Confirm the fixture's titles before choosing the
  query; the query must match exactly one row by two words that do not appear together as one
  substring.
- `docs/usage.md`: in the Jump to File paragraph, change "typing filters its cached row titles
  case-insensitively" to say each typed word must appear in the row's artist-and-title text, in
  any order, case-insensitively.
- `docs/invariants.md` `## Jump to File panel`: rewrite the `jump_file_matches` bullet (splits
  the query on whitespace; an index matches when its title contains every word case-insensitively;
  no words matches every index; list order) and add the two new tests to its Pinned by list.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- In Jump to File over a song list, typing `band two` shows and plays `The Sample Band - Two`;
  word order does not matter; a query with one word that matches nowhere shows no rows.
- A blank or whitespace-only query still shows every row, a single-word query behaves as before,
  and the existing Jump to File tests pass unchanged.
- The new tests pass, docs/usage.md and docs/invariants.md describe word matching, and
  `make check` passes.

### Right-click the player to open the options menu, like Winamp's main-window menu (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** In Winamp 2.x, right-clicking anywhere on the main window (or its rolled-up shade
strip) pops up the main menu, and the playlist editor keeps its own right-click menu. Our closest
analog to that menu is the `OPTIONS` overlay, which today opens only from the LCD's `O`, Alt+O,
or the transport row's lightning button. A right-press on the player panels should toggle it
too. The library section stays out of this area.

**Approach.** The player panels already sit inside one outer `MouseArea` that carries the volume
wheel: `MouseArea::new(player_panels).on_scroll(views::volume_wheel_message)` in
`src/ui/view/normal.rs` `view_normal`, and the title bar plus shade strip
`MouseArea::new(...).on_scroll(views::volume_wheel_message)` in `src/ui/view/shade.rs`
`view_shade`. Add `.on_right_press(Message::ToggleOptions)` to both wrappers. No new message or
handler is needed: `handlers::window::toggle_options` already closes the other transient panels,
resets `options_selected`, and restores a shaded window before the menu draws. A second
right-press does not close the menu: while it is open, `view_options_overlay` maps the base to
`Message::Ignored`, and the backdrop (`modal_overlay`) reacts only to a left press. Close, a
left click on the backdrop, Escape, or Alt+O still close it.
iced 0.14's `MouseArea::update` (iced_widget-0.14.2 `src/mouse_area.rs`) lets the content handle
the event first and then publishes `on_right_press` for `ButtonPressed(Right)`. The nested
widgets (buttons, sliders, the preset pick list, and the inner `MouseArea`s for the LCD title
drag, elapsed readout, visualizer, `O A I D V` letters, title-bar drag region, and shade-strip
double-click) react only to the left button, so a right-press over any of them reaches the outer
wrapper. The library column is pushed outside that wrapper in `view_normal`, so a right-press over
the browse list or library footer publishes nothing new. Update the comment above the wrapper in
`view_normal` so it covers the right-press as well as the wheel.

**Files touched.**
- `src/ui/view/normal.rs`, `src/ui/view/shade.rs`: the two `.on_right_press` calls and comments.
- `src/ui/tests/mod.rs`: add a helper `root_right_press_messages(player, bounds) -> Vec<Message>`
  beside `root_wheel_messages`. It uses `layout_capture::publish_at` on `view(player)` with

### Ctrl+click Previous and Next to jump to the list's first and last song, like Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+B (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** Winamp's Ctrl chords on the Previous and Next keys (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+B) go to the start and
end of the list, and its transport buttons follow the same rule when Ctrl-clicked. Our keys
already do this: `shortcuts::shortcut` maps Ctrl+Z to `Message::FirstTrack` and Ctrl+B to
`Message::LastTrack`, handled by `handlers::playback::stepping::jump_to_edge_track`. The ◀◀ and
▶▶ buttons always step one song, though, because nothing in the UI knows a modifier is held:
`shortcuts::message_for` maps `keyboard::Event::ModifiersChanged` to `None`. Make a Ctrl-held
click on Previous play the first song and a Ctrl-held click on Next play the last song. This
applies in the main transport row, the shade strip, and the library footer.

**Approach.** Decided, so the implementer has no open questions:
- Track Control on the player. Add `pub(in crate::ui) control_held: bool` to `WinampPlayer`
  (src/ui/player.rs), `false` at construction, not saved in settings.
- Add a new always-on listener `modifiers_message(event, _status, _window)` in
  src/ui/subscriptions/listeners.rs, in the same shape as `mixer_key_message`. It maps
  `iced::Event::Keyboard(keyboard::Event::ModifiersChanged(m))` to
  `Message::ControlHeld(m.control())`, and `iced::Event::Window(iced::window::Event::Unfocused)`
  to `Message::ControlHeld(false)`, so a Ctrl released outside the window does not stick. Every
  other event maps to `None`. Re-export it from `subscriptions/mod.rs` next to the other
  listeners, and push it unconditionally in `subscriptions` with `iced::event::listen_with`.
  Leave `message_for` alone: its `ModifiersChanged → None` test stays valid.
- Add three variants to `Message` (src/ui/message.rs), each with a one-line comment like its
  neighbours: `ControlHeld(bool)`, `PreviousButton`, and `NextButton`. The update arms in
  src/ui/mod.rs: `ControlHeld(held)` sets `player.control_held` and returns `Task::none()`.
  `PreviousButton` / `NextButton` call new `stepping::previous_button(player)` /
  `stepping::next_button(player)` in src/ui/handlers/playback/stepping.rs.
  `previous_button` returns `jump_to_edge_track(player, false)` while `control_held`, otherwise
  `step_track(player, false)`. `next_button` does the same with `true`. A Ctrl-click therefore
  keeps every Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+B guarantee (it ignores Shuffle and Repeat, scrolls the landed row
  into view, and does nothing with an empty list).
- In `views::transport::transport_glyphs` (src/ui/views/transport.rs), the Previous and Next
  entries emit `Message::PreviousButton` and `Message::NextButton` in place of
  `PreviousTrack`/`NextTrack`. The shade strip and library footer pick this up through
  `views::mini_transport::mini_transport_controls`. Keys keep their messages: Z, B, keypad 4/6,
  and the media Previous/Next keys still send `PreviousTrack`/`NextTrack`, so a Ctrl-held media
  key does not turn into an edge jump. Update the doc comment on `transport_glyphs`.
- Only Control matters. Shift, Alt, and Logo clicks behave like plain clicks, and no other
  button changes.

**Files touched.** src/ui/player.rs, src/ui/message.rs, src/ui/mod.rs,
src/ui/subscriptions/{mod.rs,listeners.rs}, src/ui/handlers/playback/stepping.rs,
src/ui/views/transport.rs, src/ui/views/tests/transport.rs (the
`transport_glyphs_match_the_mockup_order_and_widths` message asserts), a new
`src/ui/tests/ctrl_click_tests.rs` registered in `src/ui/tests/mod.rs` (stepping_tests.rs is
already over 1000 lines), docs/usage.md, docs/invariants.md.

**Tests** (new file, using `player_stepping_from` and `assert_track_selected` from
`src/ui/tests/mod.rs`):
- `ctrl_click_previous_plays_the_first_song` and `ctrl_click_next_plays_the_last_song`: send
  `ControlHeld(true)` and then the button message, and assert the edge row is selected.
- `plain_button_clicks_step_one_song`: with `control_held` false, `PreviousButton` /
  `NextButton` select the same rows as `PreviousTrack` / `NextTrack`.
- `control_release_restores_plain_steps`: `ControlHeld(true)` then `ControlHeld(false)`, and the
  next `NextButton` steps one song.
- `modifiers_message_tracks_control_and_focus_loss`: `ModifiersChanged(Modifiers::CTRL)` gives
  `ControlHeld(true)`, `ModifiersChanged(Modifiers::SHIFT)` gives `ControlHeld(false)`, window
  `Unfocused` gives `ControlHeld(false)`, and a `KeyPressed` gives `None`.

**Docs.** docs/usage.md: after the sentence "Ctrl+Z plays the first song of the list Z and B step
through and Ctrl+B plays its last song.", add that a Ctrl-held click on the Previous or Next
button, in the transport row, the shade strip, or the library footer, does the same, while a
plain click steps one song. In docs/invariants.md `## List edge jumps`, extend the guarantee to
Ctrl-clicked Previous/Next, name `stepping::previous_button`/`next_button` and
`listeners::modifiers_message` under Enforced by, and add the new tests to Pinned by. In the
shade-mode section that lists the strip's button messages (`Message::PreviousTrack`, …), change
Previous/Next to `Message::PreviousButton`/`Message::NextButton`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With Ctrl held, clicking ◀◀ in any of the three transport rows plays the showing list's first
  song, and clicking ▶▶ plays its last song, whatever Shuffle and Repeat are set to.
- Without Ctrl, both buttons step exactly as today, including Previous's restart after three
  seconds and Shuffle's retrace.
- Losing window focus clears the held state.
- Every keyboard binding maps to the same message as before.
- The new tests pass, the docs describe the Ctrl-click, and `make check` passes.

### Blink the shade strip's and library footer's paused time readout, like Winamp (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** Winamp blinks the paused time in the window-shade bar as well as in the main LCD. Our
LCD's large elapsed readout already blinks while paused: `handlers::playback::preview::position_tick`
flips `WinampPlayer::blink_visible` on each one-second position poll, and
`views::now_playing::elapsed_readout_color` draws the hidden phase transparent. The compact
readout (`00:53/3:30`) is the only time shown in shade mode. It is built once by
`mini_transport_row_with_optional_seek` in `src/ui/views/mini_transport.rs` and shared by the
shade strip and the library footer, and it stays solid green while paused. That makes it
impossible to tell a paused rolled-up window from a playing one at a glance. Make the compact
readout blink in step with the LCD.

**Approach.** Decided, so the implementer has no open questions:
- The whole compact readout text blinks, both elapsed and `/total`. Winamp's shade bar shows only
  the time, so the whole readout is the blinking part. Keeping it one `Text` also leaves the
  layout untouched.
- The hidden phase draws the text fully transparent and does not remove it, so its bounds and
  the seek and volume sliders do not move (the same technique `elapsed_readout_color` uses).
- The playing and stopped colors are unchanged: `theme::LCD_GREEN`, as today. The readout's click
  behavior is also unchanged: `elapsed_readout_clickable` still gates it, so a paused readout in
  its hidden phase still toggles the time display.
- No new timer or subscription. `needs_position_poll` already holds while paused with a known
  position, so the existing poll keeps the phase moving in shade mode.

Changes:
- `src/ui/views/mini_transport.rs`: add a pure
  `pub(super) fn compact_readout_color(mode: TransportMode, visible: bool) -> Color`. It returns
  `Color::from_rgba(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)` for `(TransportMode::Paused, false)` and
  `theme::LCD_GREEN` otherwise. In `mini_transport_row_with_optional_seek`, replace
  `.color(theme::LCD_GREEN)` on the readout with `.color(compact_readout_color(mode, elapsed_visible))`.
  Add an `elapsed_visible: bool` parameter right after `mode` to
  `mini_transport_row_with_optional_seek`, `mini_transport_row`, `mini_transport_row_with_seek`,
  `mini_transport_strip`, `mini_transport_strip_with_seek` and `view_library_strip`, and thread it
  through. `mini_transport_strip_with_seek` grows to 8 arguments, past clippy's
  `too_many_arguments` limit of 7, so give it `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` with a
  one-line comment, as `now_playing_row` in `src/ui/views/now_playing.rs` does. Update the module doc and `view_library_strip`'s doc to say the paused readout blinks.
- `src/ui/views/shade.rs`: add `elapsed_visible: bool` after `mode` to `view_shade_strip`, pass it
  on, and mention the blink in its doc.
- `src/ui/view/shade.rs` (`view_shade`) and `src/ui/view/player_panels.rs` (the
  `views::view_library_strip` call): pass `player.blink_visible`.
- Tests: every existing call of `view_shade_strip` / `view_library_strip` (in
  `src/ui/views/tests/shade.rs` and `src/ui/views/tests/seek_wheel.rs`) passes `true`. Add these
  to `src/ui/views/tests/shade.rs`, importing `compact_readout_color` through
  `src/ui/views/tests/mod.rs` the way it imports `mini_transport_readout`:
  - `compact_readout_color_blinks_only_while_paused`: Paused+false is transparent (alpha 0).
    Paused+true, Playing with either phase, and Stopped with either phase are `theme::LCD_GREEN`.
  - `compact_readout_keeps_its_bounds_when_the_blink_hides_it`: lay out
    `view_shade_strip(TransportMode::Paused, false, …)` and `(Paused, true, …)` with
    `captured_mini_strip`. Both capture the `00:53/3:30` text, and the volume-slider rectangle is
    equal in the two.
- `docs/usage.md`: in the paragraph with "While paused, the large elapsed readout blinks once per
  second", add that the compact readouts in the library footer and the shade strip blink with it.
- `docs/invariants.md`: in the paused-blink guarantee (the bullet naming
  `WinampPlayer::blink_visible` and `elapsed_readout_color`), add that
  `views::mini_transport::compact_readout_color` draws the compact readout transparent in the
  hidden phase without removing it, and name the two new tests.

**Files touched.** `src/ui/views/mini_transport.rs`, `src/ui/views/shade.rs`,
`src/ui/view/shade.rs`, `src/ui/view/player_panels.rs`, `src/ui/views/tests/shade.rs`,
`src/ui/views/tests/seek_wheel.rs`, `src/ui/views/tests/mod.rs`, `docs/usage.md`,
`docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- While paused, the shade strip's and the library footer's `elapsed/total` readout disappears and
  reappears on alternate one-second polls, in phase with the LCD's large readout.
- While playing or stopped, the compact readout looks as it does today.
- The hidden phase keeps the readout's bounds, so no strip control moves. Clicking the paused
  readout in either phase still toggles elapsed/remaining.
- No new subscription or timer is added.
- The two new tests pass, the docs describe the blink, and `make check` passes.

### Show 10 songs back and 10 songs forward in the options menu, like Winamp's Playback menu (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** Winamp's Playback menu lists `10 tracks back` and `10 tracks fwd` (keypad 1 and 3)
right before `Jump to time` and `Jump to file`. Our ten-song jumps (`Message::JumpTracksBack` /
`Message::JumpTracksForward`, handled by `handlers::playback::stepping::jump_ten_tracks`) are
reachable only from the numeric keypad (`numpad_shortcut` in `src/ui/shortcuts.rs`), so on a
keyboard with no keypad, which includes most Mac laptops, there is no way to use them. Add two
options-menu rows that run the same jumps.

**Approach.**
- `src/ui/message.rs`: add `OptionsChoice::JumpTracksBack` and `OptionsChoice::JumpTracksForward`
  (doc comments: "Reuses [`Message::JumpTracksBack`]." / "… [`Message::JumpTracksForward`].") and
  `OptionsRow::JumpTracksBack` / `OptionsRow::JumpTracksForward`. Put the two rows in
  `OptionsRow::ALL` directly **before** `JumpTime`, following Winamp's order (`ALL` grows from 12 to 14:
  …, `Shuffle`, `JumpTracksBack`, `JumpTracksForward`, `JumpTime`, `JumpFile`, `About`, `Close`).
  Map them in `OptionsRow::message` to `Message::OptionsChoice(OptionsChoice::JumpTracksBack)` /
  `(…JumpTracksForward)`, and update `options_rows_map_to_mouse_messages_in_draw_order`.
- `src/ui/views/options.rs`: `options_row_label` returns the fixed labels `10 songs back` and
  `10 songs forward` ("songs" matches the rest of the app's wording). No new state goes into
  `OptionsState`. Update the `view_options_overlay` doc comment, which lists which rows publish
  `OptionsChoice`.
- `src/ui/handlers/window.rs` `options_choice`: dispatch the new choices to
  `super::playback::stepping::jump_ten_tracks(player, false)` / `(player, true)` and return that
  task. The function already clears `options_visible` first, so an empty list or no song list
  only closes the menu, because `jump_ten_tracks` schedules nothing then.
- Tests:
  - `src/ui/tests/jump_tests.rs`: a new test,
    `options_ten_song_rows_jump_like_the_keypad`. Use `player_jumping_from("song-15")` with
    `options_visible = true`. Each row, by mouse (`row.message()`) and by keyboard
    (`options_selected` set to the row's index found in `OptionsRow::ALL`, then
    `Message::OptionsActivate`), closes the menu and yields
    `assert_track_selected(task, 0, 5)` for back and `(task, 0, 24)` for forward (15+10 clamps to 24).
    A second case uses `test_player()` with no songs: the row closes the menu and
    schedules no work (`assert_no_task`). The existing
    `options_jump_rows_open_their_panels_or_just_close` hard-codes positions 8 and 9. Change it to
    look the positions up in `OptionsRow::ALL`, or bump them to 10 and 11.
  - `src/ui/tests/panels_tests.rs`: the exhaustive `match choice` (the arm listing
    `OptionsChoice::JumpTime | OptionsChoice::JumpFile`) gets the two new variants in an
    `unreachable!("covered by options_ten_song_rows_jump_like_the_keypad")` arm.
  - `src/ui/views/tests/chrome.rs`: add `"10 songs back"` and `"10 songs forward"` to the label
    lists in `options_overlay_draws_each_row_with_its_state` and
    `options_overlay_publishes_each_choice_and_closes_from_close_and_backdrop`, with match arms
    asserting each publishes its `OptionsChoice`.
- Docs: in `docs/usage.md`'s options-menu sentence, insert `10 songs back`, `10 songs forward`
  before `Jump to time` in the row list and say they jump ten songs back or forward exactly like
  keypad 1 and 3 (doing nothing beyond closing the menu with no song list showing). In
  `docs/invariants.md` `## Options panel`, add the two rows to the row list and the guarantee's
  summary line, and add `handlers::playback::stepping::jump_ten_tracks` to the `options_choice`
  dispatch bullet. Pin the new test there too.

**Files touched.** `src/ui/message.rs`, `src/ui/views/options.rs`, `src/ui/handlers/window.rs`,
`src/ui/tests/jump_tests.rs`, `src/ui/tests/panels_tests.rs`, `src/ui/views/tests/chrome.rs`,
`docs/usage.md`, `docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- The options menu draws `10 songs back` and `10 songs forward` between `Shuffle: On/Off` and
  `Jump to time`. Up/Down reach them, and Enter or a click activates them.
- Choosing either row closes the menu and plays the song ten places back or forward in the
  showing list, clamped at its ends, ignoring Shuffle and Repeat. This is the same

### Mark a paused or stopped track in the window title, like Winamp's `[Paused]` and `[Stopped]` (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** Winamp's taskbar title names the current song and adds the transport state when it is not
playing: `1. Artist - Title - Winamp [Paused]` while paused and `… - Winamp [Stopped]` while
stopped. Our window title (`WinampPlayer::window_title`) already names the track as
`<number>Artist - Title - nostalgia` but reads the same whether the song plays, pauses, or stops,
so the taskbar cannot tell a paused song from a playing one. Append ` [Paused]` or ` [Stopped]`
after `nostalgia` while a known track is current and the transport is paused or stopped. Leave the
playing title and the plain `nostalgia` fallback (no current track, or an unknown id) unchanged.

**Approach.**
- `src/ui/player/presentation.rs` `window_title`: it already holds the `AppState` lock as
  `state`. After pushing `APP_TITLE`, match `state.transport_mode()` (`crate::state::TransportMode`):
  `Playing` adds nothing, `Paused` pushes `" [Paused]"`, and `Stopped` pushes `" [Stopped]"`. Raise
  the `String::with_capacity` slack to cover the suffix. Leave the early `APP_TITLE` return alone:
  with no known track the title stays plain `nostalgia` whatever the mode, so a fresh launch does
  not read `nostalgia [Stopped]`. Update the doc comment to describe the suffix. Its sentence
  "Stop leaves `current_track` in place, so the interrupted track's name stays in the title" stays
  true; add that the title then ends in ` [Stopped]`.
- `src/ui/mod.rs`: the `init_ui` doc comment says the title follows the current track. Add "and
  its paused/stopped state" so it stays accurate. No code change there; iced already re-reads
  `.title(...)` after every update.
- Tests in `src/ui/tests/window_tests.rs`:
  - `window_title_names_the_current_track` currently asserts titles on a default `test_player()`,
    whose `AppState` is stopped. With the suffix, those known-track asserts would read
    `… - nostalgia [Stopped]`. Set `state.blocking_lock().is_playing = true` right after seeding
    `current_track`, so the existing number/artist assertions keep their playing-title strings.
    Change the final Stop assertion (after `state.blocking_lock().stop()`) to expect
    `"1. The Sample Band - Opening - nostalgia [Stopped]"`. Update its leading comment.
  - New test `window_title_marks_a_paused_or_stopped_track`: seed the same `KnownTrack` and
    `current_track`. Assert the title has no suffix after `AppState::play()`, ends in
    ` [Paused]` after `AppState::pause()`, and ends in
    ` [Stopped]` after `AppState::stop()`. Then set `current_track = None` and assert the title
    reads plain `nostalgia` while stopped and while paused, with no suffix. Reuse the existing
    `KnownTrack` literal, or the `make_current_track_known` helper in the same file (it seeds
    `song-1` as `1. The Sample Band - Opening`).
- `docs/usage.md`: in the window-title sentence (`<number>Artist - Title - nostalgia` …), say that
  the title ends in ` [Paused]` while paused and ` [Stopped]` while stopped, like Winamp's taskbar
  title. It still keeps the interrupted track's name across Stop and still reads just `nostalgia`
  when no known track is current.
- `docs/invariants.md` `## Now Playing label`: extend the "iced application window's title" bullet
  with the suffix rule (nothing while playing, ` [Paused]`, ` [Stopped]`, never on the plain
  `nostalgia` fallback). Add `window_title_marks_a_paused_or_stopped_track` to that section's
  pinned tests next to `window_title_names_the_current_track`.

**Files touched.** `src/ui/player/presentation.rs`, `src/ui/mod.rs` (doc comment only),
`src/ui/tests/window_tests.rs`, `docs/usage.md`, `docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With a known current track, the window title reads `<number>Artist - Title - nostalgia` while
  playing, gains ` [Paused]` while paused, and gains ` [Stopped]` while stopped (including after
  Stop and after a preview ends with nothing to advance to).
- With no current track or an unknown id, the title is plain `nostalgia` in every transport mode.
- The number and artist rules are unchanged: an empty number or artist is still omitted.
- `docs/usage.md` and `docs/invariants.md` describe the suffix, and `make check` passes.

### Show Jump to time and Jump to file in the options menu, like Winamp's Playback menu (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** Winamp's main menu lists "Jump to time  Ctrl+J" and "Jump to file  J" under Playback.
Our options menu already carries Winamp menu items beyond Options proper (Stop after current came
from that same Playback menu), but our two jump panels open only from the keyboard. Add two rows,
`Jump to time` and `Jump to file`, after `Shuffle: On/Off` and before `About Nostalgia`, so a
mouse-only user can reach both panels.

**Approach.**
- `src/ui/message.rs`: add `OptionsChoice::JumpTime` and `OptionsChoice::JumpFile`, and
  `OptionsRow::JumpTime` / `OptionsRow::JumpFile` between `Shuffle` and `About` in the enum and in
  `OptionsRow::ALL` (its length goes from 10 to 12). `OptionsRow::message` maps them to
  `Message::OptionsChoice(OptionsChoice::JumpTime)` / `(OptionsChoice::JumpFile)`. Route them
  through `OptionsChoice`, not straight to `Message::ToggleJumpTime` / `ToggleJumpFile` the way
  About maps to `ToggleAbout`. The reason: `toggle_jump_time` returns early when
  `playback_duration` is `None`, and `toggle_jump_file` returns early when `song_list` is `None`.
  An early return skips `close_transient_panels`, so with a direct mapping an unavailable row would
  leave the menu open. `options_choice` clears `options_visible` first, so the menu always closes.
  Extend `options_rows_map_to_mouse_messages_in_draw_order` with the two new messages.
- `src/ui/handlers/window.rs` `options_choice`: add `OptionsChoice::JumpTime =>
  super::jump::toggle_jump_time(player)` and `OptionsChoice::JumpFile =>
  super::jump::toggle_jump_file(player)`, returning their tasks (the input focus, and the shade
  restore inside them). `options_choice` has already cleared `options_visible`, and opening the
  menu ran `close_transient_panels`, so neither jump flag is set and each toggle takes its opening
  branch. `handlers::jump` is a `pub(super)` sibling of `handlers::playback`, so `super::jump::…`
  resolves from `window.rs` the way `super::playback::…` already does. `options_activate` needs no
  change: it already forwards any `OptionsChoice` to `options_choice`.
- `src/ui/views/options.rs` `options_row_label`: `OptionsRow::JumpTime => "Jump to time"` and
  `OptionsRow::JumpFile => "Jump to file"`. They are fixed labels, like `About Nostalgia`, so no
  `OptionsState` field and no label helper. Update the module and `view_options_overlay` doc
  comments, which describe the menu as on/off choices plus About.
- Tests:
  - `src/ui/views/tests/chrome.rs`: add `Jump to time` and `Jump to file` to the fixed rows that
    `options_overlay_draws_each_row_with_its_state` chains with About and Close. In
    `options_overlay_publishes_each_choice_and_closes_from_close_and_backdrop`, add both labels
    and the arms that assert their `OptionsChoice`.
  - `src/ui/tests/panels_tests.rs`: `options_choice_applies_each_toggle_and_closes_the_panel`'s
    exhaustive `match` needs an `unreachable!` arm naming the new test below.

### Drag the scrolling LCD title to scroll it by hand, like Winamp (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** In Winamp 2.x you can press on the scrolling song title in the main window and drag it
left or right to scroll it by hand. Automatic scrolling pauses during the drag and resumes from
the dragged position on release. Our Now Playing marquee only scrolls on its own. Add the drag.
It applies only while the line is too long for the LCD, which is when `push_title` windows it
through `marquee_text`. A title that fits stays a plain, unclickable label.

**Approach.**

- `src/ui/views/now_playing/text.rs`: add `TITLE_DRAG_PX_PER_CHAR: f32 = 10.0`. The LCD text is
  size 20, so this is roughly one glyph. Add `marquee_cycle_len(label, artist, number) -> usize`,
  which is `display_len(..) + MARQUEE_GAP` (the period `marquee_text` wraps on). Add
  `dragged_marquee_offset(start: usize, dx: f32, cycle: usize) -> usize`. It computes
  `steps = (-dx / TITLE_DRAG_PX_PER_CHAR).trunc()` and returns
  `((start % cycle) as i64 + steps as i64).rem_euclid(cycle as i64) as usize`. Dragging left
  (negative `dx`) reveals later characters, so the text follows the pointer. Re-export both
  through `views` the way `needs_marquee` is re-exported.
- `src/ui/message.rs`: add `TitleDragPressed`, `TitleDragMoved(f32)` (window-space cursor x) and
  `TitleDragReleased`, each with a doc comment.
- `src/ui/views/now_playing.rs`, `push_title`: in the overlong branch, wrap the `marquee_text`
  label in a `MouseArea` with `.on_press(Message::TitleDragPressed)` and
  `.interaction(Interaction::Grab)`. The fitting branch is unchanged.
- `src/ui/player.rs`: add a documented field `title_drag: Option<TitleDrag>`, initialised to
  `None`. `TitleDrag { start_offset: usize, anchor_x: Option<f32> }` is defined in the new
  handler module. `needs_marquee` also returns `false` while `title_drag.is_some()`, alongside
  the `mixer_drag` and `seek_preview` checks.
- New `src/ui/handlers/playback/title_drag.rs` (declared from `playback.rs`), with a module doc:
  - `title_drag_pressed` stores `TitleDrag { start_offset: player.marquee_offset, anchor_x: None }`.
  - `title_drag_moved(x)` does nothing without a drag. On the first move it records `anchor_x`.
    On later moves it sets `marquee_offset` to `dragged_marquee_offset(start_offset, x - anchor,
    cycle)`. `cycle` comes from `views::marquee_cycle_len` over the label, artist and number,
    resolved exactly as `needs_marquee` resolves them. A `cycle` of 0 cannot happen because the
    gap is nonzero.
  - `title_drag_released` clears the drag.
  - Route the three messages in `src/ui/mod.rs`'s `update` dispatch.
- `src/ui/handlers/playback.rs`: where a new selection sets `player.marquee_offset = 0`, also set
  `player.title_drag = None`, so a drag cannot carry an old song's offset into a new one.
- `src/ui/subscriptions/listeners.rs`: add `title_drag_message(event, _status, _window)`.
  - `mouse::Event::CursorMoved { position }` maps to `TitleDragMoved(position.x)`.
  - A left-button `ButtonReleased` and `mouse::Event::CursorLeft` map to `TitleDragReleased`.
  - Every other event maps to nothing. Status is ignored, because the drag must follow the
    pointer off the title.
- `src/ui/subscriptions/mod.rs`, `subscriptions`: add a trailing `title_drag_active: bool`
  parameter. When it is true, push `iced::event::listen_with(title_drag_message)`.
  `src/ui/mod.rs` passes `player.title_drag.is_some()`. Update every `subscriptions(...)` call in
  `src/ui/tests/subscriptions_tests.rs` with a trailing `false`.

**Tests.**

- `text.rs` unit tests:
  - `dragged_marquee_offset_follows_the_pointer_and_wraps`: dragging left 25 px from 0 gives 2.
    Dragging right 10 px from 0 wraps to `cycle - 1`. A 9 px move gives the start unchanged.
  - `marquee_cycle_len_is_the_line_plus_its_gap`.
- `src/ui/views/tests/now_playing.rs`, `the_overlong_title_publishes_a_drag_press_and_a_fitting_one_does_not`:
  a `publish_at` left press on the title text publishes `TitleDragPressed` for a line over
  `MARQUEE_WIDTH`, and publishes nothing for a short line.
- `src/ui/tests/mixer_tests.rs` (beside `the_marquee_pauses_during_a_mixer_drag`), or a new
  `src/ui/tests/title_drag_tests.rs` if that file is crowded. Use `seed_current_title` with an
  overlong title. Add `the_marquee_pauses_while_the_title_is_dragged_and_resumes_from_there`:
  - Pressed: `needs_marquee()` is false.
  - `TitleDragMoved(100.0)` then `TitleDragMoved(70.0)`: the offset advances by 3.
  - `TitleDragReleased`: `needs_marquee()` is true and the offset stays at 3.
  - A `TitleDragMoved` without a press changes nothing.
  - A new selection mid-drag clears `title_drag`.
- `subscriptions_tests.rs`: the listener count grows by one only with `title_drag_active`.
  `title_drag_message` maps a cursor move, a left release and `CursorLeft` as above, and ignores
  a key press and a right-button release.

**Docs.**

- `docs/usage.md`: after "scrolled across the display when the line is longer than it", say that
  pressing on the scrolling title and dragging left or right scrolls it by hand (one character
  per 10 pixels). Automatic scrolling pauses until release and resumes from there, like Winamp.
- `docs/invariants.md`: in `## Now Playing label`, next to the marquee-timer bullets, add that
  `needs_marquee` is false during a title drag, and that `title_drag_message` is subscribed only
  while one is active. Add the new tests to that section's pinned-by list.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- With a title too long for the LCD, pressing on it and dragging moves the shown window one
  character per 10 px, with the text following the pointer and wrapping through the gap. The
  automatic scroll is paused for the whole drag, and on release it resumes from the dragged
  offset. Releasing off the title, or the cursor leaving the window, also ends the drag.
- A title that fits the LCD is not a drag target. The elapsed-readout click, the mixer and seek
  readouts, and marquee behaviour outside a drag are unchanged. `make check` passes.

### Hold and drop peak markers above the LCD spectrum bars, like Winamp's analyzer (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** Winamp's spectrum analyzer draws a thin gray peak marker above each bar. The marker
jumps up with the bar, holds when the bar falls, and then drops back slowly. Nostalgia's LCD
visualizer (`views::now_playing::visualizer::now_playing_visualizer_row`) draws only the bars, so
it jumps straight from one poll's levels to the next. Add the markers. They are presentation state
only, held beside the stored spectrum, and they follow the bars' lifecycle: Pause freezes them,
Stop and a new selection clear them, and hiding the visualizer hides them too. This work does not
depend on the Stop-after-current series and touches none of its files.

**Approach.**

- `src/ui/views/now_playing/visualizer.rs`:
  - Add `const LCD_VISUALIZER_PEAK_FALL: f32 = 0.125;`. This is how far a held peak drops on each
    spectrum reply, as a fraction of full height: 3 px of the 24 px strip, so a peak falls the
    whole strip in about two seconds at the poll's four replies a second.
  - Add `const LCD_VISUALIZER_PEAK_HEIGHT: f32 = 1.0;` (the marker's height in px) and
    `const LCD_VISUALIZER_PEAK_COLOR: Color = Color::from_rgb8(150, 150, 150);` (the base skin's
    `viscolor.txt` peak-dot gray). Every ramp color has blue at or below 41, so this is the only
    visualizer color with strong blue.
  - Add `pub fn next_spectrum_peaks(previous: Option<Spectrum>, spectrum: Option<Spectrum>) ->
    Option<Spectrum>`. A `None` spectrum returns `None`. Otherwise each band becomes
    `max(level, previous_band - LCD_VISUALIZER_PEAK_FALL)` floored at `0.0`. `level` is the
    reported band run through `clamp_with_nan_fallback(band, 0.0, 1.0, 0.0)`, and a missing
    `previous` counts as all zeros. The function is pure so the hold-and-fall rule is testable.
  - Add `pub fn visualizer_peak_marker_bottom(height: f32, peak_height: f32) -> Option<f32>`. It
    returns the marker's bottom edge in px above the rail, which is `max(peak_height, height)`
    clamped to `0.0..=LCD_VISUALIZER_HEIGHT - LCD_VISUALIZER_PEAK_HEIGHT`. It returns `None` when
    `peak_height` is not above `0.0`, NaN included. The marker therefore never sits inside its
    bar, and it always stays inside the strip.
  - `now_playing_visualizer_row` gains a second parameter, `peaks: Option<Spectrum>`. It scales
    the peaks with the existing `visualizer_bar_heights` and zips them with the bar heights.
  - For a band with a marker, the column is built top-down. First a spacer of
    `LCD_VISUALIZER_HEIGHT - bottom - LCD_VISUALIZER_PEAK_HEIGHT`. Then the 1 px marker, a
    `Container` styled with `LCD_VISUALIZER_PEAK_COLOR`. Then a spacer of `bottom - drawn`, then
    the ramp segments of `drawn = height.min(bottom)`.
  - Zero-height spacers are skipped, as the existing spacer already is. The column's fixed
    width and height stay the same.
  - A bar at full height gives its top pixel to the marker. A band without a marker draws
    exactly as today.
  - Update the doc comments of `now_playing_visualizer_row` and the module to describe the
    markers.
- `src/ui/views/now_playing.rs`: re-export `next_spectrum_peaks` beside `visible_spectrum`. Add
  `peaks: Option<Spectrum>` after `spectrum` to both `view_now_playing` and
  `now_playing_content` (both already carry `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]`), and pass it
  to `now_playing_visualizer_row`.
- `src/ui/views/mod.rs`: add `next_spectrum_peaks` to the `pub use now_playing::{…}` list.
- `src/ui/player.rs`: add `pub(in crate::ui) spectrum_peaks: Option<Spectrum>` after
  `spectrum`. Its doc says it holds the peak markers' levels, follows `spectrum`, is not
  persisted, and starts as `None` in `WinampPlayer::new`.
- `src/ui/handlers/playback/preview.rs`, `spectrum`: inside the existing `reply_is_current`
  guard, set `player.spectrum_peaks = views::next_spectrum_peaks(player.spectrum_peaks,
  spectrum)` before storing `player.spectrum`. A dropped reply therefore moves neither of them.
  Update the doc comment.
- `src/ui/handlers/playback.rs`, `reset_position_readout`: set `player.spectrum_peaks = None`
  beside `player.spectrum = None`. Its doc already says Pause does not call it, so frozen
  markers stay on screen through a pause.
- `src/ui/view/player_panels.rs`: pass `views::visible_spectrum(player.spectrum_peaks,
  player.visualizer_visible)` as the new `view_now_playing` argument, after the spectrum one.
- Existing call sites pass `None` for the new parameter and keep their assertions:
  - `view_now_playing` in `src/ui/views/tests/browse.rs`.
  - `now_playing_content` in `captured_content_with_spectrum` (`src/ui/views/tests/lcd_display.rs`)
    and in `src/ui/views/tests/now_playing.rs`.
  - Every `now_playing_visualizer_row(…)` call in those two test files.
- `src/ui/layout_capture.rs`: add `pub(crate) fn max_blue_in(&self, bounds)`, mirroring
  `max_red_in` (channel 2), plus a unit test like
  `max_red_in_reads_only_the_red_of_pixels_inside_the_bounds`.

**Tests.**

- `src/ui/views/tests/now_playing.rs` (beside
  `visible_spectrum_hides_the_stored_bars_while_the_visualizer_is_off`):
  - `next_spectrum_peaks_follows_a_rising_band_and_falls_slowly_after_it`: a missing previous
    gives the clamped bands. A lower reply drops the held band by `0.125`, never below the new
    band and never below `0.0`. A higher reply raises it to the band. An out-of-range or NaN band
    counts as clamped, NaN as `0.0`. A `None` spectrum returns `None`.
  - `visualizer_peak_marker_bottom_sits_on_or_above_its_bar_inside_the_strip`: `None` for a zero
    or NaN peak. The bar's height when the peak is below it. The peak's height otherwise. `23.0`
    for a full-height peak.
- `src/ui/views/tests/lcd_display.rs`:
  - `now_playing_visualizer_row_draws_a_gray_peak_marker_above_a_fallen_bar`: zero bars, with
    peaks band 0 at `1.0`. Through `layout_capture::capture_text_and_pixels`, slot 0's top 1 px
    row has `max_blue_in` above 100, and slot 0 below it has `max_blue_in` below 100.
  - Extend the existing captured-row height check so a row drawn with peaks keeps
    `LCD_VISUALIZER_HEIGHT`.
- `src/ui/tests/readouts_tests.rs`:
  - Extend `spectrum_reply_stores_the_loaded_previews_spectrum`. After a `recording_spectrum()`
    reply, `spectrum_peaks` equals it. A following reply with band 2 at `0.0` leaves band 2's
    peak at `0.375`. A `None` reply clears both.
  - Extend `stop_clears_the_spectrum_while_pause_keeps_it` so Pause keeps `spectrum_peaks` and
    Stop clears it.
  - Add `a_stale_spectrum_reply_leaves_the_peaks_alone`: stored peaks are unchanged after a
    reply whose epoch is out of date.
- `src/ui/tests/panels_tests.rs`: extend
  `toggle_visualizer_hides_and_shows_the_bars_without_clearing_the_spectrum` so the toggle also
  keeps `spectrum_peaks`.

**Docs.**

- `docs/usage.md`: in the visualizer sentence, after "updating about four times a second while
  playback runs", add that a thin gray peak marker above each bar jumps up with the bar and then
  drops back slowly. Change "Pause freezes the bars at their last levels, Stop and a new
  selection clear them" so it covers the markers too. The `V` sentence says hiding hides the
  markers with the bars.
- `docs/invariants.md`:
  - `## UI layout`: the visualizer bullet gets the marker guarantee. The marker draws only for a
    positive peak, never inside its bar, and always inside the strip. Peaks follow the
    hold-and-fall rule and share the spectrum's reply guards, Pause freeze, Stop and selection
    clear, and visibility flag.
  - The section's code paragraph names `next_spectrum_peaks`, `visualizer_peak_marker_bottom`,
    and `WinampPlayer::spectrum_peaks`, and pins the new tests.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- While a preview plays, each bar with a positive peak shows a 1 px gray marker at its highest
  recent level. The marker drops 3 px for each spectrum reply until the bar reaches it again.
- Pause freezes the markers. Stop, a new selection, or a `None` spectrum reply clears them. A
  stale or in-transition reply changes neither the bars nor the markers. Hiding the visualizer
  hides the markers and keeps their stored levels.
- Without peaks, the bars, ramp colors, row height, slot widths, and the
  `Message::ToggleVisualizer` press are unchanged. `make check` passes.
