### Stop after current, part 1/2: Ctrl+V stops after the current song, like Winamp (planned 2026-10-27 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-27 by the feature role

**Goal.** Winamp's Ctrl+V arms "Stop after current": the playing song plays to its end, and then
playback stops instead of advancing; the choice is used up when it fires. Nostalgia binds plain V
to Stop (`shortcut` in `src/ui/shortcuts.rs`) but leaves Ctrl+V unbound, and
`handlers::playback::preview::playback_finished` always advances when a next song exists. Add the
chord and the one-shot stop. Part 2/2 ("Stop after current, part 2/2: show it in the options menu") adds the
visible menu row; this part has no on-screen indicator, like Winamp's main window.

**Approach.**

- `src/ui/player.rs`: add `pub(in crate::ui) stop_after_current: bool` to `WinampPlayer`, doc'd as
  the transient one-shot flag (false at launch, not persisted, cleared when a natural preview end
  consumes it), and initialise it to `false` in `WinampPlayer::new`.
- `src/ui/message.rs`: add `Message::ToggleStopAfterCurrent`, documented beside `Message::Stop`.
- `src/ui/shortcuts.rs`: in `shortcut`'s Control block (the no-Alt, no-Logo match that already holds
  Ctrl+Z/B/R/W/J/A/T), map `v`/`V` with or without Shift to `Message::ToggleStopAfterCurrent`,
  and add `v` to that block's leading comment. Plain V stays `Message::Stop`.
- `src/ui/handlers/playback.rs`: add `pub(in crate::ui) fn toggle_stop_after_current(player)` that
  flips the flag and returns `Task::none()` — no transport, playback, or window change. Dispatch it
  from `update` in `src/ui/mod.rs`.

  (not finished, stale epoch / pending transition, not playing) and before picking the next song,
  when `player.stop_after_current` holds, set it to `false` and return the existing `stop(player)`
  task. Extend the function's doc comment with this rule. A dropped reply leaves the flag armed,
  and manual Play, Pause, Stop, Next, and Previous neither read nor clear it.

  `v`/`V` under `Modifiers::CTRL` and `CTRL | SHIFT`, and `Modifiers::CTRL | ALT` and
  `CTRL | LOGO` mapping to none; `assert_letter_bindings`' plain `v` → `Message::Stop` still holds.
- `src/ui/tests/stepping_tests.rs`, reusing `player_playing_stepping_song` and
  `drive_playback_finished` (which yields `Message::TransportSettled` on the stop path, as
  `preview_end_at_the_last_song_stops_when_repeat_is_off` asserts, and `TrackSelected` on an
  advance):

    list with a next song available, flag armed → after the finished reply, `is_playing` is false,
    `current_track` is still `song-1`, and `stop_after_current` is false.
  - `preview_end_after_stop_after_current_fired_advances_again`: a second song played after the

  - `stop_after_current_survives_a_dropped_finished_reply`: a stale-epoch reply leaves the flag
    armed.
  - `toggle_stop_after_current_flips_only_the_flag`: two `Message::ToggleStopAfterCurrent` updates
    go true then false, and the returned task produces no message; playing state is unchanged.

**Docs.** `docs/usage.md`'s keyboard paragraph (beside "X plays, C pauses, V stops") gains Ctrl+V;
`docs/invariants.md` `## Preview end` records the one-shot rule and pins the new stepping tests.

**Acceptance criteria.**

### Split the root screen assembly into one module per branch (planned 2026-10-26 by the organize role) — done 2026-10-26 by the feature role

**Goal.** `src/ui/view.rs` is the root assembly: a 366-line module with `view()` and `screen()` holding three
unrelated jobs — the shaded tree, the normal-mode panel stack plus browse column, and the transient
overlay selection. A change to the shaded strip has to read past the normal and overlay branches,
and the normal branch resolves one 17-field state snapshot whose fields only some of its panels
use. Split `view` into a `src/ui/view/` directory with one module per assembly, so each module owns
only the state and widgets its branch draws. The public entry point stays `ui::view::view`, and the
assembled tree, overlay precedence, and published messages stay exactly what `view()` builds today.

**Target structure.**

- `src/ui/view/mod.rs`: the module doc and `pub(in crate::ui) fn view(player)`, which builds
  `shade::view_shade(player)` when `player.shaded` holds, otherwise
  `normal::view_normal(player)`, then hands that base to `overlay::apply_overlays`, retaining the outer `OptionsShortcut` wrapper.
- `src/ui/view/shade.rs`: `view_shade`, owning the shade branch's state snapshot
  (`transport_mode`, `volume`, elapsed, total, position, duration), the title-bar and shade-strip
  column, and the `MouseArea::on_scroll(views::volume_wheel_message)` around it.
- `src/ui/view/normal.rs`: `view_normal`, owning the `library_panel_visible` branch, the
  `MouseArea::on_scroll(views::volume_wheel_message)` around the panel stack, and the column that
  appends `library::view_library(player, footer)` while the library panel is visible.
- `src/ui/view/player_panels.rs`: `view_player_panels`, owning the normal branch's current-track,
  playback-format, spectrum, transport, volume, balance, Repeat, Shuffle, and equalizer snapshot
  and the title bar, Now Playing bar, seek bar, transport row, and optional equalizer section it
  feeds. It returns the panels and an optional footer built from the same snapshot; the footer
  is constructed only while the library is visible.
- `src/ui/view/library.rs`: `view_library`, owning the `CurrentView` match and its per-level
  arguments, the current-track lock for the Songs and All Songs playing-row markers, the Back,
  Retry, Open, browse-navigation, and flat-list buttons, the search row, the current list, and the
  library strip.
- `src/ui/view/overlay.rs`: `apply_overlays(base, player)`, owning the about → options → file info →
  jump time → jump file chain and its `!player.shaded` guards.

**Implementation adjustment 2026-10-26 by the feature role:** retain the existing
`options_shortcut.rs` child and its root wrapper. Pass the footer from `player_panels` to
`library` through `normal` to preserve its shared LCD time snapshot rather than taking another
state lock for footer values.

No handler or `views` module changes; every item in the new directory is `pub(super)` except the
`view` entry point.

**Approach.** Move each branch whole, keeping its explanatory comments with the widgets they
describe. Resolve each state lock inside the module that reads it, so `view()` no longer holds the
17-field snapshot and each module locks only for its own fields. Keep the two deliberate second
locks for the Songs and All Songs playing-row markers in `library`. Replace `src/ui/view.rs` with
the directory rather than keeping a compatibility shim. Update `docs/invariants.md`'s current-path
mentions of `src/ui/view.rs` in the Library search clearing, UI layout, Volume wheel, About panel,
and Options panel sections to the owning file; leave historical `PLANS-DONE.md` and `BUGS-FIXED.md`
paths alone. No behavior
test is added: the existing root-view, layout, panel, browse, and shortcut tests already exercise
`ui::view::view`.

**Files touched.** `src/ui/view.rs` (deleted); new
`src/ui/view/{mod,shade,normal,player_panels,library,overlay}.rs`; `docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- `ui::view::view` remains the only root-assembly entry point, and `src/ui/mod.rs`'s re-export and
  `init_ui` wiring are unchanged.
- The widget calls, their arguments, the overlay precedence, and every published message match the
  current `view()`; the existing root-view, layout, panel, browse, and shortcut tests pass without
  changes.
- `src/ui/view.rs` no longer exists, and a grep for `src/ui/view.rs` over `src/`, `docs/`, and the
  open backlog finds no stale path (the historical archives keep theirs).
- `make check` passes.

### Open and navigate the options menu from the keyboard (planned 2026-10-26 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-26 by the feature role

**Goal.** The transient options menu is the only panel with no keyboard route: it opens only from
the LCD's `O` cell or the transport row's lightning button, and its rows only accept mouse clicks.
Give it the treatment the other panels already have: `Alt+O` opens and closes the menu like `Alt+3`
opens File info and `Ctrl+F1` opens About, and while the menu is open Up and Down move a highlighted
row and Enter invokes it, mirroring the Jump to File panel's arrow-and-Enter navigation. Mouse
clicks, labels, widths, and every existing toggle's behavior stay as they are; the menu and its
highlight remain layout-only and unpersisted.

**Approach.**

- `src/ui/message.rs`: add `Message::OptionsSelectionUp`, `Message::OptionsSelectionDown`, and
  `Message::OptionsActivate`, documented beside `ToggleOptions`/`OptionsChoice`. Add
  `pub(in crate::ui) enum OptionsRow { AlwaysOnTop, TimeDisplay, Visualizer, EqualizerPanel,
  LibraryPanel, About, Close }` with `ALL: [Self; 7]` in draw order and `message(self) -> Message`
  returning exactly the message each row's button publishes (`OptionsChoice(..)` for the five
  toggles, `ToggleAbout`, `ToggleOptions`). This keeps the row order in one place shared by the
  view and the keyboard handler. Unit-test that `ALL` maps to those messages in order.
- `src/ui/player.rs`: add `pub(in crate::ui) options_selected: usize` (default `0`), documented as
  an index into `OptionsRow::ALL`, reset whenever the menu opens, layout-only and not persisted.
- `src/ui/handlers/window.rs`: in `toggle_options`, reset `options_selected = 0` on the opening
  branch. Add `options_selection_up`/`options_selection_down`, which are no-ops unless
  `options_visible` holds and otherwise clamp at the first and last rows. Add `options_activate`,
  which is a no-op unless `options_visible` holds, takes `OptionsRow::ALL.get(options_selected)`,
  and dispatches the message from `OptionsRow::message` by calling the existing `options_choice`,
  `toggle_about`, or `toggle_options` for that message, so a keyboard activation follows exactly
  the mouse row's path.
- `src/ui/shortcuts.rs`: add `options_shortcut(physical_key, modifiers)` matching the physical
  `KeyO` with Alt held and Control, Shift, and Logo released to `Message::ToggleOptions`, and wire
  it into `message_for` before the plain-letter bindings. Add `message_for_options`, used while the
  menu is open: it maps Up and Down (Control, Alt, and Logo released; Shift allowed) to the
  selection messages and Enter to `Message::OptionsActivate`, and falls through to `message_for`
  for every other event so `Alt+O` still closes the menu and the rest of the key table keeps its
  existing behavior, exactly like `message_for_jump_file`.
- `src/ui/subscriptions/mod.rs`: add an `options_open: bool` parameter to `subscriptions` and choose
  the keyboard mapper as Jump to File, then Options, then the normal `message_for`. Update the
  function doc and `src/ui/mod.rs`'s subscription call to pass `player.options_visible`.
- `src/ui/mod.rs`: dispatch the three new messages to the new handlers and re-export `OptionsRow`
  beside `Message` and `OptionsChoice`.
- `src/ui/views/options.rs`: change `view_options_overlay` to take a final `selected: usize`, draw
  its rows by iterating `OptionsRow::ALL` through a new `options_row_label(row, always_on_top,
  time_remaining, visualizer_visible, eq_panel_visible, library_panel_visible)` that delegates to
  the existing five label helpers and returns `"About Nostalgia"`/`"Close"`, and build each row
  with `labeled_button` overridden by `options_row_style(index == selected, status)`. That new pure
  helper keeps `style::chrome_button_style(status)` for an unselected row and, for the selected
  row, paints the blue `theme::ROW_HIGHLIGHT` bar with white `theme::PLAYING_ROW_TEXT` in every
  button status; unit-test both branches. `src/ui/view.rs` passes `player.options_selected`.
- Tests: in `src/ui/shortcuts.rs`, add `options_shortcut_maps_alt_o_and_rejects_other_chords` and
  `message_for_options_maps_up_down_enter_and_falls_back`. In `src/ui/tests/panels_tests.rs`, add
  `options_keyboard_selection_clamps_and_activates_each_row`: opening highlights row 0, Up at the
  first row and Down at the last row stay put, Down walks the rows, and `OptionsActivate` on each
  of the seven rows applies exactly that row's effect and closes the menu (About opens About; Close
  only closes; each toggle flips only its flag, reusing the expectations in
  `options_choice_applies_each_toggle_and_closes_the_panel`). Add a no-op case with the menu
  closed. Update every `subscriptions(...)` call in `src/ui/tests/subscriptions_tests.rs` for the
  new parameter, and update `options_overlay_element` and its tests in
  `src/ui/views/tests/chrome.rs` for the new `selected` argument (row 0 selected).
- Docs: in `docs/usage.md`, add `Alt+O` to the keyboard list as the options menu's open/close
  chord and extend the options-menu paragraph with the highlighted row, Up/Down, and Enter (mouse
  behavior unchanged). In `docs/invariants.md` `## Options panel`, record the `Alt+O` chord, the
  highlighted-row state and its reset, the Up/Down/Enter mapper, the new handlers, the
  `OptionsRow` vocabulary, and the `options_open` subscription choice under **Enforced by** and

**Files touched.** `src/ui/message.rs`, `src/ui/player.rs`, `src/ui/handlers/window.rs`,
`src/ui/shortcuts.rs`, `src/ui/subscriptions/mod.rs`, `src/ui/mod.rs`, `src/ui/views/options.rs`,
`src/ui/view.rs`, `src/ui/tests/panels_tests.rs`, `src/ui/tests/subscriptions_tests.rs`,
`src/ui/views/tests/chrome.rs`, `docs/usage.md`, `docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- `Alt+O` toggles the options menu open and closed, opening it with the same unshade-first and
  close-other-panels behavior as the `O` cell and lightning button; it does not fire with Control,
  Shift, or Logo held. Opening highlights the first row, Up and Down move the highlight and clamp at

### Implement Winamp's AUTO equalizer toggle that loads a genre-matched preset (planned 2026-10-26 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-26 by the feature role

**Goal.** The equalizer mockups (`docs/screenshots/equalizer.png` and `player.png`) draw an `AUTO`
button beside the `ON` button, and Winamp's AUTO button auto-loads the preset named after the
playing track's primary genre. Add that toggle: while AUTO is on, selecting a song whose genre
matches a preset name applies that preset's curve; a song whose genre matches no preset leaves the
current curve alone, and AUTO off never changes it. The choice is persisted like the other mixer
settings. This changes only which preset is applied when a track is selected — playback, browse,
search, and the audio backend's existing equalizer path are otherwise untouched.

**Approach.**

- `src/equalizer.rs`: add pure `pub fn preset_for_genre(genre: &str) -> Option<Preset>` that trims
  the genre and matches a `PRESETS` name case-insensitively (`eq_ignore_ascii_case`), returning
  `None` for blank or unmatched text. Add a unit test covering an exact match, surrounding
  whitespace and mixed case, a blank genre, and an unmatched genre such as `Alternative`.
- `src/state.rs`: add `pub eq_auto: bool` beside `eq_enabled`, defaulting false, documented as
  whether a genre-matched preset is applied when a track is selected; add
  `pub fn toggle_eq_auto(&mut self)` that flips it, next to `toggle_equalizer`, and a test that it
  flips only that flag.
- `src/settings.rs`: carry `eq_auto` in `Settings` (field, `Default` false, `from_state`,
  `apply_to`). Write it as `eq_auto={}` in `to_text` after `eq_enabled`, parse it in `from_text`, and
  update the struct/default/`apply_to` docs from "the equalizer's on/off state" to include the auto
  choice. Extend `state_with_every_field_set` so the round-trip test covers it, add
  `eq_auto_round_trips_and_ignores_malformed_values` (missing, `true`, explicit `false`, and an
  unknown word fall back/parse like `shade`), and add `eq_auto=maybe` to
  `from_text_ignores_malformed_and_unknown_lines`.
- `src/ui/message.rs`: add `ToggleEqAuto` beside `ToggleEqualizer`, documented as the equalizer
  panel's AUTO button. `src/ui/mod.rs` dispatches it to `handlers::mixer::toggle_eq_auto`, which uses
  `mutate_state(player, AppState::toggle_eq_auto)` and schedules no work (the toggle alone changes
  no gain, so nothing is forwarded to the backend).
- `src/ui/handlers/mixer.rs`: add `pub(in crate::ui) fn apply_auto_preset(player: &WinampPlayer,
  genre: &str) -> Task<Message>`: return no task unless
  `equalizer::preset_for_genre(genre)` matches and `player.state.blocking_lock().eq_auto` holds,
  then apply the preset through the existing `mutate_equalizer` path so the pick list, stored
  curve, and a running preview's filters all update together.
- `src/ui/handlers/playback.rs`: in `track_selected`, after the selected `Song` is resolved and
  before the play request is issued, call `super::mixer::apply_auto_preset(player, &song.genre)`.
  Every route that plays a song goes through `TrackSelected` — browse rows, Open, Jump to File,
  Next/Previous, the edge and ten-song jumps, and the preview-end advance — so one call site covers
  them all. Update its doc comment.
- `src/ui/views/equalizer.rs`: add pure `auto_label(bool) -> &'static str` (`"AUTO: On"` /
  `"AUTO: Off"`); give `view_equalizer` an `auto: bool` parameter and push a
  `fixed_width_button(auto_label(auto), AUTO_BUTTON_WIDTH, Message::ToggleEqAuto)` after the
  on/off button, before the preset pick list, with the existing spacer between buttons. Pin
  `AUTO_BUTTON_WIDTH` wide enough for `AUTO: Off` so the label swap cannot reflow the pick list.
  Update the module and function docs.
- `src/ui/view.rs`: capture `state.eq_auto` with the other equalizer values and pass it to
  `views::view_equalizer`.
- Tests: update the five `view_equalizer` call sites in `src/ui/views/tests/equalizer.rs` for the
  new argument and add `auto_button_draws_its_state_and_publishes_toggle_eq_auto`, laying out the
  panel with AUTO off and on through `layout_capture`, asserting the exact `AUTO: Off`/`AUTO: On`
  labels, and clicking the on-state button to observe `Message::ToggleEqAuto`. In
  `src/ui/tests/mixer_tests.rs` add `toggle_eq_auto_flips_only_the_auto_flag` (no scheduled work)
  and `auto_on_applies_a_genre_matched_preset_on_track_selection`, plus cases showing AUTO off and
  an unmatched genre leave a previously applied Rock preset and its bands unchanged. In
  `src/ui/tests/settings_tests.rs` add `toggle_eq_auto_reaches_the_saved_snapshot` and a boot
  restore assertion through `Settings::apply_to`.
- Docs: `docs/usage.md`'s equalizer paragraph names the `AUTO` toggle and its genre-matching rule,
  and the persisted-settings list includes the auto choice. `docs/invariants.md` gains a
  `## Auto-load presets` section after `## Equalizer scale shortcuts` (guarantee, **Enforced by**
  naming `equalizer::preset_for_genre`, `AppState::eq_auto`, `handlers::mixer::apply_auto_preset`,
  and the `track_selected` call, **Pinned by** the new test names, and a History line); update
  `## Settings persistence` for the new key and appended values, and add a History sentence there.

**Files touched.** `src/equalizer.rs`, `src/state.rs`, `src/settings.rs`, `src/ui/message.rs`,
`src/ui/mod.rs`, `src/ui/handlers/mixer.rs`, `src/ui/handlers/playback.rs`,
`src/ui/views/equalizer.rs`, `src/ui/view.rs`, `src/ui/views/tests/equalizer.rs`,
`src/ui/tests/mixer_tests.rs`, `src/ui/tests/settings_tests.rs`, `docs/usage.md`,
`docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- The equalizer panel draws an `AUTO: Off` toggle while auto-loading is off and `AUTO: On` while it
  is on, beside the existing on/off button; pressing it toggles only `AppState::eq_auto`, schedules
  no work, and leaves the gains, preset, and equalizer on/off state alone.
- While AUTO is on, selecting a song whose trimmed primary genre matches a preset name
  case-insensitively applies that preset's preamp and all ten bands and names it in the preset pick
  list; selecting a song with a blank or unmatched genre leaves the current curve and preset exactly
  as they were.
- While AUTO is off, selecting any song changes no equalizer value.
- The auto choice is written as `eq_auto=true|false`, restored on the next launch, and a missing or
  malformed value falls back to off.
- The applied preset reaches a running preview through the existing equalizer forwarding path, and
  playback, browse, search, panel visibility, and the other settings keep their current behavior.
- The usage reference and the two invariant sections describe the toggle and the new persisted
  choice, and the project's check passes.

### Name the active library source in the About panel (planned 2026-10-26 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-26 by the feature role

**Goal.** The README's status says Apple Music browse falls back to the built-in sample library until

while `AppleMusicService::session()` reports a stored session, `Library: Sample library` otherwise —

playback, browse, settings, or sign-in behavior changes, and no new `Message`, state field, or
dependency is added.

**Approach.**

  returning `"Library: Apple Music"` for `true` and `"Library: Sample library"` for `false`, and

  beside the version and tagline. Update the module and function docs from the name/version/tagline

  `about_overlay_draws_the_name_version_tagline_and_library_source`) to lay out both states and

### Remember the rolled-up window-shade mode across launches (planned 2026-10-26 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-26 by the feature role

**Goal.** Every other layout toggle — the readout mode, the visualizer, the EQ and library panels,
and always-on-top — is saved and restored, but `WinampPlayer::shaded` starts `false` on every
launch, so a user who closes the window rolled up gets the full window back. Persist the shade
mode in the settings file the same way: a launch whose file says `shade=true` draws the title bar
plus compact strip from the first view and rolls the window down to `SHADED_HEIGHT`, and its first
unshade restores the size the window opened at. This is a UI mode, not window placement: the
window's size and position stay deliberately unpersisted.

**Approach.**

- `src/settings.rs`: add a private `shade: bool` field beside `always_on_top`; `Settings::default`
  and `Settings::from_state` leave it `false`; add `shaded()` / `set_shaded(bool)` accessors in the
  same style as the other player-owned flags; write `shade={}\n` from `to_text`; and parse the
  `"shade"` key through `parse_into`, so a missing or malformed value falls back to unshaded.
  Update the module and struct docs: six UI-owned values now, naming the shade mode and keeping
  the statement that window size and position are not persisted.
- `src/ui/player.rs`: `persist_settings_if_changed` copies `self.shaded` through
  `snapshot.set_shaded`; `adopt_saved_settings` sets `self.shaded = saved.shaded()` before the
  first view. Update both methods' docs and the `WinampPlayer::shaded` field doc from the
  current "resets each launch"/five-value wording to the persisted six.
- `src/ui/handlers/window.rs`: `window_id_resolved` must capture the launch window's size when the
  restored mode is shaded, because `unshaded_size` is `None` at boot. After storing the id, when
  `player.shaded && player.unshaded_size.is_none()`, also schedule
  `iced::window::size(id).map(Message::WindowShadeMeasured)`; batch it with the saved
  always-on-top `set_level` call when both apply, return exactly one task when only one applies,
  and `Task::none()` when neither does. The existing `window_shade_measured` then stores the
  default size and resizes to the strip, so the first unshade restores it; no new message or
  handler.
- Tests: in `src/settings.rs`, extend `to_text_round_trips_every_field` for the shade flag and add
  `shade_round_trips_and_ignores_malformed_values` (default false, explicit true round-trips, an
  unknown word falls back to unshaded). In `src/ui/tests/settings_tests.rs`, add
  `toggle_window_shade_reaches_the_saved_snapshot` (with no window id, toggling flips `shaded`
  and saves once; another toggle saves the cleared value; `Message::Ignored` saves nothing) and
  `saved_shade_is_restored_on_boot` (adopting a shaded snapshot sets `player.shaded`). Align
  `shaded_eq_toggle_saves_nothing` with the new snapshot by setting `player.saved_settings`'s
  shade flag alongside `player.shaded`, so the update sees no shade change. In
  `src/ui/tests/window_tests.rs`, add `window_id_resolved_measures_a_restored_shade`: a shaded
  player with no captured size schedules work, while an unshaded unpinned one still schedules
  none; then `Message::WindowShadeMeasured(iced::Size::new(800.0, 600.0))` stores that size and
  keeps `shaded` true.
- Docs: `docs/usage.md` adds the shade mode to the saved-values sentence and says a saved-shaded
  launch opens rolled up and unrolls with the same controls. `docs/invariants.md`
  `## Settings persistence` adds the shade mode to the persisted list and the six UI-owned values,
  removes shade state from the "not window placement" sentence (size and position stay
  unpersisted), and updates **Enforced by**, **Pinned by**, and **History**.
  `## Window shade` adds the boot restore bullet (restore before the first view, measure the
  launch size through `window_id_resolved`, resize to `SHADED_HEIGHT`, no measurement for an
  unshaded launch) and updates **Enforced by**, **Pinned by**, and **History**.

**Files touched.** `src/settings.rs`, `src/ui/player.rs`, `src/ui/handlers/window.rs`,
`src/ui/tests/settings_tests.rs`, `src/ui/tests/window_tests.rs`, `docs/usage.md`,
`docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- `shade=true` survives `Settings::to_text` / `from_text`; a missing, empty, or malformed line
  falls back to unshaded, and the file's other keys keep parsing as before.
- Toggling shade writes exactly one new snapshot whose `shaded()` matches the new state, a second
  toggle writes the cleared state, and a message that changes no value writes nothing.
- A launch adopting a shaded snapshot has `player.shaded` set before the first view, so the root
  view draws the title bar plus compact strip; once `WindowIdResolved` lands, it schedules the
  size query (batched with a saved always-on-top level when both apply), and the resulting
  `WindowShadeMeasured` stores that size and resizes to `SHADED_HEIGHT`, leaving the following
  unshade able to restore it. A saved-unshaded, unpinned launch schedules no window work.
- No new `Message`, `WinampPlayer` field, dependency, or window-placement persistence is added;
  the settings file only gains one `shade=` line.
- The usage reference and the settings and window-shade invariants describe the restored shade
  mode, and the project's check passes.

### Split the transport's Play/Pause button into separate Play and Pause buttons, like Winamp (planned 2026-10-26 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-26 by the feature role

**Goal.** `docs/screenshots/transport.png` and `hero.png` draw distinct Play (`▶`) and Pause (`II`)
buttons between Previous and Stop, but `transport_glyphs` in `src/ui/views/transport.rs` builds one
combined Play/Pause button whose glyph swaps with `is_playing`. Split it into two fixed buttons that
dispatch the existing explicit `Message::Play` (the X key's play/resume) and `Message::Pause` (the C
key's pause), in the main transport row, the shade strip, and the library footer. This is
presentation and message wiring only: no new `Message`, handler, state field, setting, or audio
behavior, and the LCD's own transport glyph, the X/C keys, and the system media keys stay as they
are. The mockup's sixth glyph (eject) stays out of scope because the app has no open-a-file action.

**Approach.**

  `("■", "Stop", 30.0, Message::Stop)`, Next `("▶▶", "Next", 34.0, Message::NextTrack)`. Delete

  comments in `src/ui/message.rs` and the `play`/`pause` doc comments in
  `src/ui/handlers/playback.rs` to name the new buttons alongside X and C; the handlers themselves

### Interpolate the equalizer's response curve smoothly between bands (planned 2026-10-26 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-26 by the feature role

**Goal.** The mockup's traced response line curves smoothly between the ten bands, while
`response_curve_offsets` in `src/ui/views/equalizer.rs` joins adjacent band gains with straight
line segments. Ease each adjacent-band span so the trace meets every band at a zero slope and
still passes exactly through that band's gain, matching the mockup's rounded curve instead of the
visible corners a piecewise-linear trace leaves at the band positions. The queued guide plan
draws its 0 dB line and band markers behind the trace and leaves the trace's shape alone, so this
change touches only the offsets and leaves `response_curve_row` and the guide layers untouched.

**Approach.**

- `src/ui/views/equalizer.rs`: in `response_curve_offsets`, replace the linear `fraction` in the
  adjacent-band blend with a cubic smoothstep, `fraction * fraction * (3.0 - 2.0 * fraction)`.
  Keep the existing column-to-band mapping, the `clamp_gain` normalization, the `columns == 0`
  and `columns == 1` guards, and the exact endpoint behavior: column 0 and the last column still
  return the first and last bands' normalized gains, and every band position still returns that
  band's own offset. Because smoothstep is monotone over `0.0..=1.0` and the endpoint offsets are
  already clamped, every returned offset stays in `0.0..=1.0` without a second clamp. Update the
  function's doc comment and the module's trace description to say the line is eased between
  bands rather than straight, and note that a flat curve, all-minimum curve, and all-maximum
  curve are unchanged.
- `src/ui/views/tests/equalizer.rs`: extend
  `response_curve_offsets_follow_the_band_gains` with the eased-shape checks and keep its flat,
  all-minimum, all-maximum, endpoint, and zero/one-column assertions. Use a curve with
  `bands[4] = GAIN_MIN_DB`, `bands[5] = GAIN_MAX_DB`, and every other band `0.0`, laid out with
  `(BAND_COUNT - 1) * 4 + 1` columns so each band lands on exactly column `index * 4`. Assert the
  band columns still equal that band's gain (the curve passes through every band), and assert the
  three columns between those two bands have offsets `0.15625`, `0.5`, and `0.84375` (the
  smoothstep values at `0.25`, `0.5`, and `0.75`) rather than the linear `0.25`, `0.5`, `0.75`,
  proving the span is eased. Assert every offset in that curve lies in `0.0..=1.0`. Leave
  `response_curve_row_keeps_its_height_and_draws_one_segment_per_column` as it is: the row's
  geometry, height, and per-column segment count do not change.
- `docs/usage.md`: in the equalizer-panel description, say the response curve is eased smoothly
  between the band gains rather than drawn as straight segments.
- `docs/invariants.md` `## UI layout`: extend the response-curve bullet with the eased
  interpolation, name `views::equalizer::response_curve_offsets` in **Enforced by**, add the
  updated `response_curve_offsets_follow_the_band_gains` to **Pinned by**, and add a one-line
  History note.

**Files touched.** `src/ui/views/equalizer.rs`, `src/ui/views/tests/equalizer.rs`,
`docs/usage.md`, `docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- `response_curve_offsets` still returns exactly the requested column count, `0.0` for an
  all-minimum curve, `0.5` for a flat curve, and `1.0` for an all-maximum curve, with column 0
  and the last column equal to the first and last bands' normalized gains.
- The trace passes through every band's normalized gain at that band's column, and each span
  between adjacent bands is eased with the cubic smoothstep rather than interpolated linearly
  (the quarter-span offsets are `0.15625` and `0.84375` for a full-span rise).
- Every offset stays within `0.0..=1.0`, including a curve whose gains sit at both ends of the
  range, so no eased overshoot can leave the plot.
- `response_curve_row` keeps its fixed height, one segment per column, and the guide layers the
  queued plan adds; no gain, preset, guide, message, or audio behavior changes.
- The project's check passes.

clamped at the ends, and make every highlight move (Up, Down, and the two page keys) scroll the
match list only as far as needed to show the row. The keys keep their browse-scrolling behavior

  button padding inside), `JUMP_FILE_ROW_SPACING` (2.0), `JUMP_FILE_LIST_PADDING` (4.0),
  `JUMP_FILE_LIST_HEIGHT` (180.0), and the page step `JUMP_FILE_PAGE_ROWS` (5, the rows that fit

  and the 8 px padding fill 176 of the 180 px list.

### Point the mouse wheel at the balance and equalizer sliders (planned 2026-10-26 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-26 by the feature role

**Goal.** A wheel roll over the player panels already nudges the volume, and a roll over the
drawn seek slider seeks instead, but a roll over the balance slider still changes the volume,
and a roll over the equalizer's preamp or a band slider also changes the volume. Make a plain
wheel roll over the balance slider nudge the balance, and over the preamp or any band nudge
that gain, by one slider step in the roll's vertical direction, forwarded live to the audio
backend like a drag. Everywhere else the wheel keeps nudging the volume, and the drawn seek
slider keeps its seek exception. The new wheel paths change no drag readout and schedule no
work. This is independent of the waiting Escape plan: both add a `Message` variant and a
dispatch arm, so keep both when they meet in `src/ui/message.rs` and `src/ui/mod.rs`.

**Approach.**

- `src/ui/views/mod.rs`: extract the existing sign mapping in `volume_wheel_message` into a
  private `fn wheel_direction(delta: ScrollDelta) -> f32` returning `1.0`, `-1.0`, or `0.0`
  (zero also covers `NaN` and a horizontal-only roll). Keep `volume_wheel_message`'s output
  unchanged. Add `pub(super) fn balance_wheel_message(delta) -> Message`,
  `pub(super) fn eq_preamp_wheel_message(delta) -> Message`, and
  `pub(super) fn eq_band_wheel_message(index: usize, delta) -> Message`, each wrapping
  `wheel_direction` in `Message::BalanceWheel`, `Message::EqPreampWheel`, and
  `Message::EqBandWheel(index, direction)`. Change `BALANCE_STEP` and `EQ_STEP` from private to
  `pub(super)` so the handlers use the sliders' own granularity, as `VOLUME_STEP` already does.
- `src/ui/message.rs`: add `BalanceWheel(f32)`, `EqPreampWheel(f32)`, and
  `EqBandWheel(usize, f32)` beside `VolumeWheel`, documenting that each carries a signed wheel
  direction and moves only that shared value by one step without setting `mixer_drag`.
- `src/ui/handlers/mixer.rs`: add `balance_wheel`, `eq_preamp_wheel`, and `eq_band_wheel` beside
  `volume_wheel`. Each returns `Task::none()` for a zero or `NaN` direction. The balance
  handler calls `state.set_balance(state.balance() + direction.signum() * views::BALANCE_STEP)`
  through `mutate_balance`; the preamp and band handlers do the same through `mutate_equalizer`
  with `views::EQ_STEP`, `state.eq_preamp()`, and `state.eq_bands()[band]`. An out-of-range
  `band` is a no-op before the lock. Never set `player.mixer_drag`.
- `src/ui/mod.rs`: dispatch the three new variants to those handlers beside `Message::VolumeWheel`.
- `src/ui/views/transport.rs`: wrap only the balance `chrome_slider` in
  `MouseArea::new(..).on_scroll(super::balance_wheel_message)`. iced runs the slider's own update
  first and the wrapper only when the slider did not capture the event, so the slider's existing
  Ctrl+wheel step stays as it is. Add a `#[cfg(test)]` `BALANCE_SLIDER_ID` on a `Container`
  around that wrapper, like `seek_bar`'s ids.

### Close the transient panels with Escape, like a Winamp dialog (planned 2026-10-26 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-26 by the feature role

**Goal.** Each transient panel — About, File info, Jump to time, and Jump to File — closes from its
own `Close` button, a backdrop click, or its toggle key, but not from the keyboard's universal
dismiss key. Add one shared route: a plain or Shift-held Escape press closes whichever of those
panels is showing, including while its filter or time box has focus. Escape with Control, Alt, or
Logo held, and every other key, stay as they are; with no panel open Escape stays unbound as it is
today, so a focused `Search library` box keeps it for clearing its own focus. The new route only
clears panel-visibility flags: no query, selection, playback, transport, mixer, browse, or settings
state changes, no work is scheduled, and nothing is persisted.

**Approach.**

- `src/ui/player.rs`: add `pub(in crate::ui) fn transient_panel_open(&self) -> bool` beside
  `close_transient_panels`, returning `self.about_visible || self.file_info_visible ||
  self.jump_time_visible || self.jump_file_visible`. Document it beside `close_transient_panels`
  as the read side of the same four-flag set, so the subscription gate and the closer cannot
  drift; the set stays named in this one impl rather than in each caller.
- `src/ui/message.rs`: add a payload-free `EscapePressed` after `JumpFileRowSelected`, documented
  as closing the showing transient panel (About, File info, Jump to time, or Jump to File) by
  clearing only those four visibility flags, changing no other state, and scheduling no work.
- `src/ui/handlers/window.rs`: add `pub(in crate::ui) fn escape_pressed(player: &mut WinampPlayer)
  -> Task<Message>` beside `toggle_about`: call `player.close_transient_panels()` and return
  `Task::none()`. Document that the subscription only delivers it while a panel is open, and that
  with none open it is still a no-op. It is not a toggle, so it never opens a panel.
- `src/ui/timers.rs`:
  - Add `pub(super) fn escape_key_message(event: iced::Event, _status: iced::event::Status,
    _window: iced::window::Id) -> Option<Message>` beside `mixer_key_message`. Match
    `iced::Event::Keyboard(keyboard::Event::KeyPressed { key: keyboard::Key::Named(
    keyboard::key::Named::Escape), modifiers, .. })` and return `Some(Message::EscapePressed)`
    unless `modifiers.control() || modifiers.alt() || modifiers.logo()` holds; every other event,
    and every Escape release, returns `None`. Ignore the status argument deliberately: this
    listener exists so the press is seen even when a focused `TextInput` captures Escape and
    clears its own focus, which `keyboard::listen`'s ignored-only feed would drop.
  - Give `subscriptions` a fifth `transient_panel_open: bool` argument after
    `mixer_readout_showing`, and push `iced::event::listen_with(escape_key_message)` only when it
    holds. Document that the Escape listener joins only while a panel is open, so Escape outside
    a panel rebuilds no screen, and that the event-with-status form is required because the panel
    boxes hold focus.
- `src/ui/mod.rs`: pass `player.transient_panel_open()` as the fifth `subscriptions` argument,
  and route `Message::EscapePressed => handlers::window::escape_pressed(player)` beside the
  `ToggleAbout`/`ToggleFileInfo` arms.
- `src/ui/tests/timers_tests.rs`: append `false` to every existing `subscriptions(...)` call. Add
  `the_escape_listener_runs_only_while_a_transient_panel_is_open`, asserting the baseline
  `subscriptions(false, false, false, false, false)` and
  `subscriptions(false, false, false, false, true)` differ by exactly the Escape listener (3 vs
  2). Add `escape_key_message_maps_escape_but_not_its_chords_or_other_keys`, building a
  `KeyPressed` event as `a_key_or_wheel_event_ends_a_mixer_readout` does
  (`src/ui/tests/mixer_tests.rs`), asserting `Some(Message::EscapePressed)` for a plain and a
  Shift-held press with `Status::Captured` (proving the captured-event seam), and `None` for
  Ctrl, Alt, and Logo chords, an Escape release, and another named key.
- `src/ui/tests/panels_tests.rs`: add
  `escape_closes_each_transient_panel_without_touching_anything_else`. From one `test_player()`,
  drive `Message::SongsLoaded(stepping_songs())`, set `current_view = CurrentView::Songs`, call
  `make_current_track_known`, and set `playback_duration = Some(...)` so all four panels can
  open. Assert `Message::EscapePressed` with no panel open schedules no work and leaves
  `transient_panel_open()` false. Then loop over the four toggles
  (`ToggleAbout`, `ToggleFileInfo`, `ToggleJumpTime`, `ToggleJumpFile`): open it, assert
  `transient_panel_open()`, drive `Message::EscapePressed` with
  `assert_message_schedules_no_work`, and assert `!transient_panel_open()`; snapshot transport
  mode, current track, volume, balance, repeat, shuffle, current view, and the songs row
  selection before the loop and assert them unchanged after it.
- `docs/usage.md`: in the transient-panel sentence, say a plain or Shift-held Escape press closes
  whichever panel is open, like its `Close` button or the backdrop, and that with no panel open
  Escape keeps its existing behavior.
- `docs/invariants.md`: add a `## Transient panel dismissal` section after `## Jump to File panel`
  stating the guarantee above, enforced by `WinampPlayer::transient_panel_open`,
  `timers::escape_key_message`, `Message::EscapePressed`,
  `handlers::window::escape_pressed`, and `WinampPlayer::close_transient_panels`, pinned by the
  three new tests; name `handlers::window::escape_pressed` and `ui::timers` in that section. Add
  one line to each of `## About panel`, `## File info panel`, `## Jump to time panel`, and
  `## Jump to File panel` saying a plain or Shift-held Escape also closes it, cross-referencing
  `## Transient panel dismissal`, and add the new tests to those sections' **Pinned by** lists.

**Files touched.** `src/ui/player.rs`, `src/ui/message.rs`, `src/ui/handlers/window.rs`,
`src/ui/timers.rs`, `src/ui/mod.rs`, `src/ui/tests/timers_tests.rs`,
`src/ui/tests/panels_tests.rs`, `docs/usage.md`, `docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- With any one of About, File info, Jump to time, or Jump to File open, a plain or Shift-held
  Escape press closes exactly that panel: all four `*_visible` flags are false afterwards, no
  task is scheduled, and no other state changes.
- The Escape press is delivered even while the panel's own text box has focus, because the
  listener uses `iced::event::listen_with` and ignores the event status; it is subscribed only
  while `WinampPlayer::transient_panel_open()` holds, so Escape outside a panel sends nothing.
- Escape with Control, Alt, or Logo held and Escape key releases map to nothing, and
  `shortcuts::message_for` still returns `None` for a plain Escape press, so every existing
  keyboard and media-key binding is unchanged.
- With no panel open, `Message::EscapePressed` is a no-op, and Escape keeps its current behavior
  (including a focused `Search library` box clearing its own focus).
- Queries, browse selection, playback, transport, mixer, settings, and persisted state are
  untouched; nothing new is saved.
- `docs/usage.md` and `docs/invariants.md` describe the dismissal route, and `make check` passes.

### Choose the Jump to File match with Up and Down, like Winamp (planned 2026-10-26 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-26 by the feature role

**Goal.** The Jump to File panel's selection bar still marks only the first filtered match, and
Enter or `Jump` always plays that first match. Let plain Up and Down move the highlighted row
through the filtered matches and make Enter, `Jump`, and the selection bar all name that
highlighted row: the first match is highlighted until the user moves, Down from it selects the
second match, Up from it stays on the first, and repeated presses stop at the first or last match
without wrapping. Typing a new filter or reopening the panel puts the highlight back on the first
match. This is the interaction the numbered rows and selection bar already set up; it changes no
playback, browse, filter, settings, or persistence behavior outside the panel.

**Approach.**

- `src/ui/message.rs`: add payload-free `JumpFileSelectionUp` and `JumpFileSelectionDown` beside
  `JumpFileChanged`/`JumpFileSubmitted`, both documented as acting only while the panel is open
  and changing no playback state.
- `src/ui/player.rs`: add `pub(in crate::ui) jump_file_selected: Option<usize>` after
  `jump_file_query`, documented as the highlighted match's source index (`None` means the first
  match, as on opening or after typing), initialize it to `None` in `WinampPlayer::new`, and reset
  it in `handlers::jump::toggle_jump_file` and `jump_file_changed`. It is layout-only and not
  persisted.
- `src/ui/views/jump_file.rs`:
  - Add `pub(crate) fn jump_file_highlighted(matches: &[usize], selected: Option<usize>) ->
    Option<usize>` returning `selected` when it appears in `matches`, otherwise the first match,
    and `None` for an empty list. The view and the submit handler both call it, so the row drawn
    with the selection bar and the row Enter plays cannot drift.
  - Change `view_jump_file_overlay` to take `selected: Option<usize>` after `epoch`, compute
    `let highlighted = jump_file_highlighted(&matches, selected);` before consuming `matches`, and
    style each row `jump_file_row_style(highlighted == Some(index), status)`. Update its doc from
    the first match being the Enter target to the highlighted match, defaulting to the first.
  - Rename `jump_file_row_style`'s `is_default` parameter to `highlighted` (same signature and
    colors) and update its doc and test name; the blue bar and white text stay the browse
    selection style, and every other row keeps the flat green playlist colors.
- `src/ui/views/mod.rs`: re-export `jump_file_highlighted` beside the existing
  `jump_file_matches` `pub(crate) use`.
- `src/ui/view.rs`: pass `player.jump_file_selected` to both `view_jump_file_overlay` calls (the
  Songs and All Songs branches).
- `src/ui/handlers/jump.rs`:
  - Add `jump_file_selection_up` and `jump_file_selection_down`, or one private
    `move_jump_file_selection(player, up: bool)` with both thin public handlers. Each no-ops unless
    `jump_file_visible`; computes `jump_file_matches` from the current query; leaves an empty match
    list with `jump_file_selected = None`; otherwise takes the highlighted match's position in
    `matches` (a stale or `None` selection counts as position 0) and moves it to
    `saturating_sub(1)` for Up or `(position + 1).min(matches.len() - 1)` for Down, storing
    `Some(matches[position])`. Both return `Task::none()` and touch nothing else.
  - Change `jump_file_submitted` to dispatch `views::jump_file_highlighted(&matches,
    player.jump_file_selected)` through `TrackSelected`; no match still leaves the panel, query,
    and selection alone, and a successful submit still closes the panel.
  - `jump_file_changed` resets `jump_file_selected` to `None` after storing the text, so a new
    filter always starts at its first match.
- `src/ui/shortcuts.rs`: add `pub(super) fn message_for_jump_file(event: Event) -> Option<Message>`
  beside `message_for`. For a key press with Control, Alt, and Logo released, `Key::Named(ArrowUp)`
  maps to `JumpFileSelectionUp` and `ArrowDown` to `JumpFileSelectionDown` (Shift allowed, like
  the other letter bindings); every other event falls through to `message_for`, so J, Ctrl+J, and
  the rest keep their existing mappings. iced's `TextInput` does not consume Up/Down (it handles
  Enter, Backspace/Delete, Home/End, Left/Right, and Escape), so the filter box keeps focus while
  these keys reach the listener.
- `src/ui/timers.rs`: give `subscriptions` a `jump_file_open: bool` argument and install
  `keyboard::listen().filter_map(if jump_file_open { message_for_jump_file } else {
  message_for })`, documenting that Up/Down choose a Jump to File match only while that panel is
  open and otherwise stay volume. `src/ui/mod.rs` passes `player.jump_file_visible` and routes the
  two new messages to the handlers. Update every `subscriptions(...)` call in
  `src/ui/tests/timers_tests.rs` with the new argument.
- `src/ui/views/tests/jump_file.rs`: give the `overlay` helper `selected: Option<usize>` (existing
  calls pass `None`); add `jump_file_highlighted_prefers_a_selected_match_and_falls_back_to_first`
  (selected match, stale selection, `None`, empty matches) and
  `overlay_highlights_the_selected_row`, which lays out three unfiltered rows with `Some(2)` and
  uses `layout_capture::capture_text_and_pixels` with `max_red_in` on the selected and a plain row's
  text bounds to prove the selected row draws the white selection text rather than plain green.
- `src/ui/tests/jump_file_tests.rs`: add `down_and_up_move_the_selection_through_the_matches`
  (open, Down selects the second match then the last and stops, Up walks back and stops at the
  first, each step scheduling no task), `typing_a_filter_resets_the_selection_to_the_first_match`,
  and `submit_plays_the_selected_match`. Keep the existing first-match submit test as the default
  behavior.
- `docs/usage.md`: in the Jump to File sentence, say Up and Down move the selection bar through the
  matches and Enter or `Jump` plays the highlighted row, the first match until you move it.
- `docs/invariants.md` `## Jump to File panel`: replace the first-match guarantee with the
  highlighted-match guarantee — `jump_file_highlighted` resolves a still-valid
  `jump_file_selected` or the first match, Up/Down clamp within the filtered matches without
  wrapping, a new query or opening resets the selection, and Enter/`Jump` plays the highlighted
  row — and add `shortcuts::message_for_jump_file`, `handlers::jump`, and `ui::timers` to the
  enforcers plus the new tests to `Pinned by`.

**Files touched.** `src/ui/message.rs`, `src/ui/player.rs`, `src/ui/views/jump_file.rs`,
`src/ui/views/mod.rs`, `src/ui/view.rs`, `src/ui/handlers/jump.rs`, `src/ui/shortcuts.rs`,
`src/ui/timers.rs`, `src/ui/mod.rs`, `src/ui/views/tests/jump_file.rs`,
`src/ui/tests/jump_file_tests.rs`, `src/ui/tests/timers_tests.rs`, `docs/usage.md`,
`docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- With the panel open on an unfiltered three-song list, Down selects the second match and then the
  third and stays there; Up walks back to the second and the first and stays there. The selection
  is the source index, so a filtered row keeps the number its source list gave it.
- Typing a new filter and reopening the panel both put the highlight back on the first match, and
  Enter or `Jump` plays that row.
- Enter or `Jump` plays the highlighted match rather than always the first; with no highlight it
  still plays the first match and closes the panel exactly as before, and a no-match submit still
  leaves the panel and query alone.
- The overlay draws the highlighted row with `theme::ROW_HIGHLIGHT` behind
  `theme::PLAYING_ROW_TEXT` and every other row in the flat green row style; the default selection
  is the first match.
- Up/Down move the Jump to File selection only while the panel is open; with the panel closed they
  still nudge the volume, and every other keyboard shortcut and media key keeps its mapping.
- No playback, audio, browse, filter, settings, or persistence behavior changes; `jump_file_selected`
  is not saved, and closing the panel through `Close`, the backdrop, a row press, or a successful
  submit behaves as today.
- `make check` passes.

  avoids copying `PRESETS` on every rebuild.

  and clipping. The equalizer test uses it to compare two captures when a widget paints outside

  `equalizer_pick_list_shows_custom_for_a_hand_tuned_curve`, which pins

  name `view_equalizer`/`CUSTOM_PRESET_LABEL` and `chrome_pick_list_style` in `Enforced by`, and

### Show the current track's track number in the File info panel, like Winamp's ID3 panel (planned 2026-10-26 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-26 by the feature role

**Goal.** Winamp's File info (ID3) dialog lists a track's number within its album beside its
year and genre. Nostalgia's File info panel names the title, artist, album, year, genre, length,
and loaded preview format, but `Song` carries no track number even though Apple Music reports
one. Carry the source's `attributes.trackNumber` through `Song` and the `KnownTrack` cache and
draw a `Track #: <n>` line between `Genre:` and `Length:` while the source supplies one. No new
state, handlers, settings, or playback behavior.

**Approach.**

- `src/library.rs`: add `#[serde(default)] pub track_number: Option<u32>` to `Song`,
  documented as the track's 1-based position on its album (`None` when the source supplied none
  or reported a non-positive number). Add the `"track_number": null` key to the test
  `song_payload`, and add `song_round_trips_its_track_number` (a `Some(3)` number serializes under
  the `track_number` key and survives the round trip) and
  `song_track_number_defaults_to_none_when_the_payload_omits_it` (a payload from
  `song_required_fields_payload` parses with `None`), beside the existing year and genre tests.
  Add `track_number` to every test-built `Song` literal the compiler reports, as the year and
  genre plans did.
- `src/apple_music/rest/wire.rs`: add `#[serde(rename = "trackNumber")] track_number:
  Option<u32>` to the private `Attributes`, documented as the track's 1-based position on its
  album with absence meaning the API omitted it. Carry it through `Resource::into_song`'s
  destructure and set `Song::track_number` to `track_number.filter(|number| *number > 0)`, so an
  absent number or an API-reported `0` (which no album can use) maps to the `None`
  "source supplied none" sentinel. Update `into_song`'s doc comment to name the track number
  among the fields it moves into the model.
- `src/sample_library.rs`: give the five sample songs their album positions — `1`, `2`, and `3`

### Shade the LCD spectrum bars green through orange by height, like the mockup's analyzer (planned 2026-10-26 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-26 by the feature role

**Goal.** The mockup's LCD analyzer paints each bar with a vertical color ramp — dark green at
the rail, then green, yellow-green, yellow, and orange at the tallest peaks
(`docs/screenshots/hero.png`) — while the app paints every bar flat `theme::LCD_GREEN`. Repaint
the existing ten-bar visualizer from that ramp, keeping the bar widths, gaps, fixed row height,
hidden/visible behavior, and the spectrum data untouched. No state, settings, audio, handler, or
playback change.

**Approach.**

- `src/ui/views/now_playing/visualizer.rs`: add a private ramp for the strip,
  `const LCD_VISUALIZER_RAMP_STEP: f32 = 2.0` and `const LCD_VISUALIZER_RAMP: [Color; 12]`, bottom
  to top, using the 8-bit colors sampled from the mockup's 24 px analyzer:
  `(24, 132, 8)`, `(41, 148, 0)`, `(49, 156, 8)`, `(57, 181, 16)`, `(50, 190, 16)`,
  `(41, 206, 16)`, `(148, 222, 33)`, `(189, 222, 41)`, `(214, 181, 33)`, `(222, 165, 24)`,
  `(198, 123, 8)`, `(214, 115, 0)`. Document that the steps are absolute rows above the rail, so a
  bar's color follows its height rather than being stretched over the bar.
- Add `pub fn visualizer_bar_segments(height: f32) -> Vec<(f32, Color)>`: clamp `height` into
  `0.0..=LCD_VISUALIZER_HEIGHT` (NaN → 0), then, for each ramp step bottom first, push
  `(shown, color)` where `shown = (height - index as f32 * LCD_VISUALIZER_RAMP_STEP)
  .clamp(0.0, LCD_VISUALIZER_RAMP_STEP)` and skip zeros. The returned heights sum to the clamped
  height, so every bar keeps its measured height.
- In `now_playing_visualizer_row`, replace each band's single plain-green `Container` with a
  `Column` of fixed width `LCD_VISUALIZER_BAR_WIDTH` and height `LCD_VISUALIZER_HEIGHT`: a top
  `Space` of `LCD_VISUALIZER_HEIGHT - bar_height` (skipped at zero) followed by one full-width
  segment `Container` per slice, iterated from the top slice down (the reverse of
  `visualizer_bar_segments`' bottom-to-top order) and painted that slice's color. A silent band
  draws only its top spacer, so it keeps its fixed-width slot. Keep the row's height, spacing,
  `MouseArea`/`ToggleVisualizer` press, and empty-spectrum behavior exactly as they are, and do not
  change `visualizer_bar_heights`, `Spectrum`, `WinampPlayer`, or any handler.
- `src/ui/views/tests/lcd_display.rs` (and the import list in `src/ui/views/tests/mod.rs`):
  - Add `visualizer_bar_segments_ramp_from_dark_green_to_orange`: `24.0` yields twelve 2 px
    segments in ramp order summing to 24; `3.0` yields a 2 px step plus a 1 px step in the next
    color; `0.0`, a negative, and NaN yield none; and a fractional height such as `12.5` sums to
    12.5 with no segment over 2 px and its partial top in the correct step's color.
  - Update `now_playing_visualizer_row_draws_one_fixed_width_bar_per_band` to use all ten non-zero
    bands and group the width-8 containers by x: expect ten x positions, each group's segment
    heights summing to `band * 24.0` (within 0.01), every segment at most 2 px tall, and every
    color one of the ramp's. Assert the laid-out row width is
    `BAND_COUNT * 8.0 + (BAND_COUNT - 1) * 3.0` for a spectrum with silent bands, so a silent band
    still reserves its slot.
  - Update `now_playing_content_keeps_the_visualizer_height_with_and_without_a_spectrum` to group
    its width-8 containers by x instead of expecting exactly `BAND_COUNT`; keep its "bars sit
    between the title and status row" and equal-height assertions.
  - Add `now_playing_visualizer_row_paints_its_ramp_from_green_to_orange`: lay the row out with
    one band at `1.0` and the rest `0.0`, draw it with `layout_capture::headless_renderer`, and
    assert the full band's top 2 px strip has a much higher maximum red channel than its bottom
    2 px strip. Add `max_red_in` beside `max_green_in` in `src/ui/layout_capture.rs` (same bounds
    walk over the red byte) so the test can read it; the pure test pins the exact ramp colors, so
    the pixel test only proves the drawing uses them.
  - Update the `CapturedContainers` doc comment in `src/ui/views/tests/mod.rs`, which currently
    says counting containers pins the bar count, to say the bar segments are the containers and
    tests group them by their x position.
- `docs/usage.md`: in the visualizer sentence, replace "small green ten-bar spectrum visualizer"
  with the ten bars shaded from dark green at the rail through yellow to orange at their peaks.
- `docs/invariants.md`: in `## Now Playing label`, change the "exactly `BAND_COUNT` green bars"
  bullet to describe up to twelve 2 px ramp steps per bar, bottom to top, from
  `visualizer_bar_segments`; in `## Preview spectrum`, add
  `views::now_playing::visualizer::visualizer_bar_segments` to the enforcer list and the new tests
  to `Pinned by`, and state that the color follows the bar's height above the rail while the bar
  heights, widths, gaps, row height, and visible/hidden behavior stay unchanged.

**Files touched.** `src/ui/views/now_playing/visualizer.rs`, `src/ui/views/tests/lcd_display.rs`,
`src/ui/views/tests/mod.rs`, `src/ui/layout_capture.rs` (the `max_red_in` test helper),
`docs/usage.md`, `docs/invariants.md`.

**Acceptance criteria.**

- Each non-empty bar is built from consecutive 2 px steps of the ramp starting at dark green at
  the rail; a 24 px bar shows all twelve steps through orange at its top, and a shorter bar shows
  only the steps its height reaches.
- Segment heights for a bar sum to its `visualizer_bar_heights` height (within 0.01), no segment
  exceeds 2 px, zero and NaN heights draw no segments, and every segment uses a ramp color.
- The visualizer row keeps its 24 px height and one fixed-width 8 px slot per band (ten slots,
  3 px gaps), with silent bands still reserving their slots; a press still publishes
  `Message::ToggleVisualizer`, and hiding, Pause, Stop, and a new selection behave exactly as
  before.
- A rendered full-height bar is orange at its top and dark green at its bottom.
- `make check` passes.

### Jump to File from a showing song list with `J`, like Winamp (planned 2026-10-26 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-26 by the feature role

**Goal.** Winamp's `J` opens a Jump to File dialog that filters the playlist and jumps to a match;
Nostalgia has Ctrl+J's Jump to time panel but no Jump to File. Add a transient Jump to File panel
over the showing song list (the browsed Songs list, including album/playlist songs and search
results, or the flat All Songs list): typing filters its cached row titles, Enter or `Jump` plays
the first match, and clicking a row plays it. It reuses the existing `TrackSelected` playback path,
so no library, REST, audio, browse-state, or persistence behavior changes.

**Approach.**

- `src/ui/views/jump_file.rs` (new):
  - `pub const JUMP_FILE_INPUT_ID: &str = "nostalgia-jump-file";` beside the Jump to time box's id.
  - `pub(crate) fn jump_file_matches(titles: &[String], query: &str) -> Vec<usize>`: trim the query;
    an empty query matches every index in order, otherwise keep the index of every title whose
    lowercased text contains the lowercased query, preserving list order. The view and the submit
    handler both call this one function, so the rows shown and the row Enter plays cannot drift.
  - `pub fn view_jump_file_overlay<'a>(base: Element<'a, Message>, query: &'a str, titles: &'a [String], epoch: u64) -> Element<'a, Message>`:
    build a `JUMP TO FILE` heading, a `TextInput` with `JUMP_FILE_INPUT_ID`, placeholder
    `"Filter songs"`, `Message::JumpFileChanged` on input and `Message::JumpFileSubmitted` on
    submit (styled with `style::chrome_text_input_style`), then a fixed-height `Scrollable` of one
    `Button` per match showing `titles[index]` and publishing
    `Message::JumpFileRowSelected { epoch, index }` (styled with `style::playlist_row_style`). When
    there are no matches, draw `No songs` for an empty list and `No matching songs` otherwise, then
    `Jump` (`Message::JumpFileSubmitted`) and `Close` (`Message::ToggleJumpFile`) buttons. Stack it
    with `modal::modal_overlay(..., Message::ToggleJumpFile)`. No state or playback is touched here.
- `src/ui/views/mod.rs`: declare `mod jump_file;` and re-export `JUMP_FILE_INPUT_ID`,
  `jump_file_matches`, and `view_jump_file_overlay`; extend the module doc's panel list.
- `src/ui/message.rs`: add `ToggleJumpFile`, `JumpFileChanged(String)`, `JumpFileSubmitted`, and
  `JumpFileRowSelected { epoch: u64, index: usize }`, with comments naming the panel and the
  `TrackSelected` dispatch.
- `src/ui/player.rs`: add `jump_file_visible: bool` and `jump_file_query: String` after the Jump to
  time fields, documented as transient, not persisted, and mutually exclusive with the other
  transient panels; initialize them in `WinampPlayer::new`.
- `src/ui/handlers/jump.rs`: add a private `song_list(player) -> Option<(&[String], u64)>` that
  returns `songs.titles`/`songs.epoch` for `CurrentView::Songs` and
  `all_songs.titles`/`all_songs.epoch` for `CurrentView::AllSongs`, and `None` otherwise (the same
  view-to-buffer rule `track_selected` and `showing_songs` use). Then:
  - `toggle_jump_file`: if visible, clear the flag and return no task; otherwise return no task
    unless `song_list` is `Some`. Opening sets the flag, clears the query, closes About, File info,
    and Jump to time, focuses `JUMP_FILE_INPUT_ID`, and while shaded calls `toggle_window_shade`
    first (exactly `toggle_jump_time`'s shape).
  - `jump_file_changed`: store the typed text; the view re-filters live.
  - `jump_file_submitted`: when the panel is open, call `jump_file_matches` on the current list; a
    missing first match leaves the panel and query alone, otherwise clear the flag and return
    `Task::done(Message::TrackSelected { epoch, index })` for the first match's source index.
  - `jump_file_row_selected`: when the panel is open, clear the flag and return
    `Task::done(Message::TrackSelected { epoch, index })`; the existing epoch/index guards in
    `TrackSelected` reject a stale press.
  - In `toggle_jump_time`'s opening branch, also clear `jump_file_visible`.
- `src/ui/handlers/window.rs`: in the opening branches of `toggle_about` and `toggle_file_info`,
  also clear `jump_file_visible`; leave their other behavior alone.
- `src/ui/mod.rs`: route the new variants in `update` to the handlers above.
- `src/ui/view.rs`: after the Jump to time branch, add a `jump_file_visible && !shaded` branch that

  `JumpFileRowSelected { epoch, index }`, `JumpFileSubmitted`, and `ToggleJumpFile` respectively;
  assert the empty-list and no-match wordings.

  alone; a row press dispatches the clicked index; Jump to File and About/File info/Jump to time
  close each other; opening while shaded restores the window; and a root-view capture over a
  `Songs` fixture with the flag set draws `JUMP TO FILE`, the filtered row, and not the filtered-out
  row.
- `src/ui/shortcuts.rs` tests: add `message_for_maps_j_to_jump_file`, and update
  `message_for_maps_ctrl_j_to_jump_time` so plain `j` now expects `ToggleJumpFile` while the

- `docs/invariants.md`: add a `## Jump to File panel` section after `## Jump to time panel` with the

`src/ui/player.rs`, `src/ui/handlers/jump.rs`, `src/ui/handlers/window.rs`,

- The panel lists exactly the showing list's cached titles that contain the trimmed query
  case-insensitively, in list order; a blank query lists every title. An empty list reads
  `No songs` and a non-empty list with no match reads `No matching songs`.

### Show the loaded preview's format in the File info panel, like Winamp (planned 2026-10-26 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-26 by the feature role

**Goal.** Winamp's File info completes the current file's details with its format. Nostalgia's
panel names the title, artist, album, and length, and its LCD status row already shows the loaded
preview's average bitrate, sample rate, and channel mode. Add the same values to the File info
panel as one `Format: …` line when `WinampPlayer::playback_format` is `Some`, reusing
`views::now_playing::format_playback_prefix` and `views::now_playing::channel_mode_label`. No new
message, state, handler, or persistence behavior.

    `const FORMAT_LABEL: &str = "Format: ";` beside the existing labels.

    the length line and before the `Close` button, push
    `Text::new(format!("{FORMAT_LABEL}{} {}", format_playback_prefix(format),
    channel_mode_label(format.channels)))` only when `format` is `Some`. With `None` the panel
    draws no format line. The title line, the empty-artist and empty-album omissions, the length,

  argument. This is the same value the LCD status row draws; it stays through Pause and is cleared

title, artist, and length. The REST resource already parses `attributes.albumName` for

`album_id`, so the title is gone by the time a track plays. Carry the album title onto `Song`,
cache it on `KnownTrack` when a track plays, and draw an `Album: …` line in

**Approach.**

    `song_required_fields_payload` (it is optional) and add

### Next, Previous, and track jumps scroll only as far as needed to show the landed row, like Winamp (planned 2026-10-25 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-26 by the feature role

**Goal.** In Winamp's playlist editor, stepping tracks leaves the list alone while the new row is
visible, and otherwise scrolls only far enough to bring it into view. Nostalgia does something
different. While a song list shows, Next, Previous, a shuffled retrace, the preview-end advance,
Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+B, and keypad 1/3 all call `scroll_browse_to_playing_row`, and that function snaps the
landed row to the viewport's top through `scroll_browse_to_row`. So each step down a visible list
jerks it upward. Route those steps through the existing minimal-scroll `reveal_browse_row`, which
Alt+Up/Alt+Down already uses, and leave the view gating as it is.

**Approach.**

- `src/ui/handlers/browse/scroll.rs`:
  - `scroll_browse_to_playing_row` should call `reveal_browse_row(index)` in place of
    `scroll_browse_to_row(index)` for `CurrentView::Songs | CurrentView::AllSongs`. Every other
    view still returns `Task::none()`. Update its doc comment to say the scroll goes only as far
    as needed, and not at all when the row is already fully visible.
  - Delete `scroll_browse_to_row`. After this change nothing calls it (grep `src` to confirm),
    and clippy `-D warnings` would reject it as dead code.
  - Retarget the intra-doc links that name it, because `make docs` fails on a broken link. In
    the `scroll_browse_by` doc, contrast with `reveal_browse_row`. In the `reveal_row_offset`
    doc, state the geometry directly: row `index` spans from `BROWSE_LIST_PADDING + index *
    BROWSE_ROW_HEIGHT` for one `BROWSE_ROW_HEIGHT`.
  - Grep `src` and `docs` for any other `scroll_browse_to_row` mention and fix it too.
- `src/ui/tests/stepping_tests.rs`: the current assertions use `assert_task_scrolls_browse_list_to`.
  Its `browse_scroll_effects` reports a zero-height viewport at offset 0, so under reveal the
  expected offsets change. Rewrite these tests to use `browse_scroll_effects_at` from
  `src/ui/tests/mod.rs` with an explicit viewport, in the style of `move_row_tests.rs`:
  - `next_and_previous_scroll_the_showing_song_list_to_the_landed_row` becomes
    `next_and_previous_reveal_the_landed_row_only_when_it_leaves_the_viewport`. From song-2,
    with a one-row viewport (`views::BROWSE_ROW_HEIGHT`) scrolled to song-2's top
    (`PAD + 1*ROW`):

    - Previous (re-run from a fresh song-2 fixture) scrolls up to `PAD`.

    at offset 0. The advance to index 1 then scrolls to `PAD + 2*ROW - ROW`. Add a sibling,

  - `edge_jumps_scroll_the_showing_song_list`: Ctrl+B (LastTrack) with a one-row viewport at 0
    scrolls to `PAD + (last+1)*ROW - ROW`. Ctrl+Z (FirstTrack) with a one-row viewport
    scrolled to the last row scrolls to `PAD`.
  - `stepping_while_another_browse_level_shows_does_not_scroll` stays unchanged.
- `src/ui/tests/mod.rs`: if `assert_task_scrolls_browse_list_to` has no callers left, delete it

### Alt+E and Alt+G toggle the library and equalizer panels, like Winamp (planned 2026-10-25 by the plan role) — done 2026-10-25 by the feature role

**Goal.** In Winamp 2.x, Alt+E shows or hides the playlist editor and Alt+G shows or hides the
graphical equalizer. Nostalgia's playlist-editor analogue is the library section behind the `PL`
button, and no key reaches it. Its equalizer panel answers only to plain `E` and the `EQ` button.
Bind Alt+E to `Message::ToggleLibraryPanel` and Alt+G to `Message::ToggleEqualizerPanel`, so
both windows toggle from the keyboard the Winamp way. Both remain layout-only toggles. In shade
mode both keys do nothing, as plain `E` does today.

**Approach.**

- `src/ui/shortcuts.rs`: add `fn panel_shortcut(physical_key: &key::Physical, modifiers:
  Modifiers) -> Option<Message>`, written like `file_info_shortcut`. It requires Alt held with
  Control, Shift, and Logo released. It maps `key::Physical::Code(key::Code::KeyE)` to
  `Message::ToggleLibraryPanel` and `key::Code::KeyG` to `Message::ToggleEqualizerPanel`. Match
  by physical key, not logical character, because on macOS Alt+E and Alt+G produce other
  logical characters (a dead key, `©`). The doc comment should say so. Chain it in
  `message_for` right after `file_info_shortcut`. Add Alt+E and Alt+G to `message_for`'s doc
  comment list. `shortcut` still returns `None` for every Alt chord, so
  `shortcut_ignores_chord_modifiers` stays true unchanged.

  flipping the flag while `player.shaded`, the same guard `toggle_equalizer_panel` has. Shade
  mode draws no `PL` button (only the main transport row in `views/transport.rs` pushes
  `library_panel_toggle()`), so the guard changes only the new key path. Update the doc comment.
- `docs/invariants.md`: in the EQ toggle bullet, add that Alt+G dispatches the same
  `Message::ToggleEqualizerPanel`. In the `PL` toggle bullet, add that Alt+E dispatches
  `Message::ToggleLibraryPanel`, that its other modifier chords stay unbound, and that shade mode
  changes nothing because the toggle leaves `library_panel_visible` alone while
  `WinampPlayer::shaded` holds. Add the new tests to that section's test list.
- `README.md` (Usage keys paragraph, outside the brief markers): after the sentence on E and
  the `EQ` button, add "Alt+E shows or hides the library section exactly like the `PL` button,
  and Alt+G the equalizer panel like `EQ`, as Winamp's Alt+E and Alt+G toggle its playlist
  editor and equalizer."
